790: Introduction
791: Welcome to DataForSEO API!
792: This is the starting point on your journey towards building powerful SEO software, data analysis pipelines, and robust no-code automations. With DataForSEO you can get all the data you need while saving your time and budget.
793: Getting started
794: Follow our recommended learning path to master DataForSEO APIs.
795: 1. Kickstart Guide to our APIs
796: 2. Dashboard Guide
797: 3. Test with API Playground
798: 4. Free Unlimited Trial Info
799: 5. Sandbox Best Practices
800: REST technology
801: DataForSEO API is using the REST technology for interchanging data between your application and our service. The data exchange is made through the widely used HTTP protocol, which allows applying our API to almost all programming languages.
802: Client libraries
803: You can create your REST class or use the following ready-made classes:
804: PHP DataForSEO Client
805: Recommended: officially supported PHP Client. Author – Vitaliy Lyabakh – jovixv
806: C# DataForSEO Client
807: Recommended: officially supported C# Client. Author – DataForSEO team
808: Java DataForSEO Client
809: Recommended: officially supported Java Client. Author – DataForSEO team
810: Python DataForSEO Client
811: Recommended: officially supported Python Client. Author – DataForSEO team
812: TypeScript DataForSEO Client
813: Recommended: officially supported TypeScript Client. Author – DataForSEO team
814: PHP Simple Rest Client
815: PHP REST Client build with cURL. Author – Fabio Agostinho Boris.
816: Python Simple Rest Client
817: Python REST Client. Author – DataForSEO.
818: PHP, Python, C# and Postman examples
819: Choose your preferred programming language or API testing tool.
820: PHP Examples
821: PHP code examples
822: Python Examples
823: Python code examples
824: C# Examples
825: C# code examples
826: POSTMAN Examples
827: POSTMAN examples
828: POSTMAN Documenter
829: Online POSTMAN Documenter
830: Data encoding
831: All data you send to DataForSEO API should be UTF-8 encoded.
832: If you use one of the Clients listed in the first table, gzip will be the default format of data exchange. You will see Content-Encoding: gzip in the header.
833: All the responses are returned in the JSON format by default, but we also support responses in the XML format – just append .xml to the end of your request. In addition to that, you can request HTML results from endpoints that return HTML-encoded results by appending .html to the end of the request’s URL path.
834: For example, the following requests will return response encoded in XML or HTML accordingly:
835: https://api.dataforseo.com/v3/appendix/user_data.xml
836: https://api.dataforseo.com/v3/serp/google/organic/task_get/html/09061543-1535-0066-0000-6240830f56ba.html
837: Rate limits
838: Each of DataForSEO APIs has a certain rate limit, which you can find in the HTTP header of every endpoint.
839: Rate limit HTTP headers we use:
840: X-RateLimit-Limit – the rate limit ceiling per minute for the given endpoint;
841: X-RateLimit-Remaining – the number of requests remaining in the current rate limit window.
842: If your system requires rate limits to be increased, please contact our support team.
843: Results storage
844: The term for storing API results in our system depends on the API and method of data retrieval.
845: Standard method: results are stored for 30 days*
846: Live method: results are not stored*
847: HTML results: results are stored for 7 days
848: *for SERP API in both Standard and Live methods, the results in JSON format are stored for 30 days.
849: To learn more about the terms of results storage, check this Help Center article.

818: Create a free account with DataForSEO, then go to the API Access tab in the account dashboard to find your API login and password, which you’ll need to authenticate and use the DataForSEO APIs. Note that the API password is generated automatically by DataForSEO and is different from your account password.
819: DataForSEO is using the Basic Authentication, which makes it possible to call our APIs with almost any programming language, Postman app, REST API platforms, and all major frameworks.

821: Authorization: Basic login:password

790: Sandbox
791: Sandbox is a technical environment for developers where DataForSEO API can be used without unnecessary expenses.
792: You can learn more about DataForSEO Sandbox in our Help Center.
793: Pricing
794: Your account will not be charged for using Sandbox endpoints
795: POST
796: https://sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/$path
797: Description of the dynamic field:
798: path
799: API path
800: specify the path to the endpoint you’d like to test
801: example:
802: serp/google/maps/task_post
803: Sandbox cost and use case
804: Sandbox is completely free for any registered user at DataForSEO. The main use case for Sandbox is configuring your software to work with our data.
805: It is not necessary to spend money on actual API calls while integrating DataForSEO API. The sandbox allows sending requests to any DataForSEO API and getting the results for free. Sandbox environment also works with pingback_url and postback_url functions.
806: Note that these will be only generic responses. All the results you receive within Sandbox contain dummy data. However, the structure and fields of the sandbox response are identical to that of the actual API response.
807: Sandbox has the same rate limits as the production environment and allows sending 10000 API calls per minute with each POST call containing no more than 100 tasks. The live method allows sending 10000 API calls per minute as well, but each POST call can contain only 1 task.
808: How to use Sandbox for SERP API?
809: In order to use sandbox endpoints, you need to change the hostname in the URL when sending an API call from api.dataforseo.com/v3/ to sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/
810: There is no need to adjust the code or make any other changes to POST data.
811: If you want to set a SERP API task through the sandbox, you should use the following URL structure:
812: https://sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/serp/google/organic/task_post
813: To collect the results of the task through the sandbox, it’s necessary to make a GET request with the URL structure as in the example:
814: https://sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/serp/google/organic/task_get/advanced/$id
815: If you want to use the sandbox to see the structure of all available SERP features and extra elements on the search engine results page, you can request the following URL:
816: https://sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/serp/google/organic/task_get/advanced/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
817: The response will include all available items in the Google Organic SERP Advanced endpoint with the fields containing dummy data.
818: How to use Sandbox for Keywords Data API?
819: To send a request to any Keywords Data API endpoint, you should follow the same principle.
820: Just change the hostname in the URL of your request according to the example:
821: https://sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/keywords_data/google/search_volume/task_post
822: After that, make a GET request to the API server to retrieve sample results with the same change in the URL structure:
823: https://sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/keywords_data/google/search_volume/task_get/$id
824: How to use Sandbox for Domain Analytics API?
825: To send a request to any Domain Analytics API endpoint, you should follow the same principle.
826: Just change the hostname in the URL of your request according to the example:
827: https://sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/domain_analytics/technologies/aggregation_technologies/live
828: Since all Domain Analytics API endpoints have the live method of delivering data, you won’t have to make a separate GET request to retrieve results.
829: How to use Sandbox for DataForSEO Labs API?
830: To send a request to any DataForSEO Labs API endpoint, you should follow the same principle.
831: Just change the hostname in the URL of your request according to the example:
832: https://sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/dataforseo_labs/google/related_keywords/live
833: Since all DataForSEO Labs API endpoints have the live method of delivering data, you won’t have to make a separate GET request to retrieve results.
834: How to use Sandbox for Backlinks API?
835: To send a request to any Backlinks API endpoint, you should follow the same principle.
836: Just change the hostname in the URL of your request according to the example:
837: https://sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/backlinks/referring_domains/live
838: Since all Backlinks API endpoints have the live method of delivering data, you won’t have to make a separate GET request to retrieve results.
839: How to use Sandbox for OnPage API?
840: To send a request to any OnPage API endpoint, you should follow the same principle.
841: Just change the hostname in the URL of your request according to the example:
842: https://sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/on_page/task_post
843: After that, make another POST request to the API server to retrieve sample results with the same change in the URL structure:
844: https://sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/on_page/pages
845: https://sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/on_page/links
846: How to use Sandbox for Content Analysis API?
847: To send a request to any Content Analysis API endpoint, change the hostname in the URL of your request according to the example:
848: https://sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/content_analysis/search/live
849: The API server will provide you with sample results in response.

790: SERP API: Overview
791: This API is designed to provide you with SERP results
792: SERP API encompasses a broad range of endpoints. You can get the full list here.
793: All major search engines are supported: Google, Bing, YouTube, Yahoo, Baidu, Naver, and Seznam.
794: The returned results are specific to the indicated keyword, search engine, language and location parameters. We emulate set location and search engine with the highest accuracy so that the results you receive will match the actual search results for the specified parameters at the time of task setting. You can always check the returned results accessing the check_url in the Incognito mode to make sure the received data is entirely relevant. Note that user preferences, search history, and other personalized search factors are ignored by our system and thus would not be reflected in the returned SERP results.
795: You can indicate the following device types and OS you would like to receive SERP results for when setting a task:
796: • Mobile. Available OS types: iOS, Android
797: • Desktop. Available OS types: Windows, macOS.
798: ‌
799: Note: Google News/Images/Search By Image/Jobs are currently available for desktop only.
800: Additional SERP API functionality includes a SERP Screenshot endpoint and an AI Summary endpoint that work with compatible search engines.
801: To find answers on common questions about SERP API and find guidance on efficient use of its features, visit our Help Center.
802: SERP functions
803: SERP API provides search engine results with three standard functions: Regular, Advanced and HTML.
804: The Regular function is supported in Organic search engine types and provides organic and paid search results for the specified keyword, search engine, and location.
805: The Advanced function is supported across all SERP API search engines. This function provides a complete overview of search results.
806: The HTML function is supported across SERP API and provides a raw SERP HTML page for the specified keyword, search engine, and location.
807: ‌
808: Methods
809: The cost of using SERP endpoints depends on the selected method and priority of task execution. Available methods and priorities are described below.
810: DataForSEO has two main methods to deliver SERP results: Standard and Live.
811: If your system requires delivering instant results, the Live method is the best solution for you. Unlike the Standard method, it doesn’t require making separate POST and GET requests to the corresponding endpoints.
812: If you don’t need to receive data in real-time, you can use the Standard method of data retrieval. This method requires making separate POST and GET requests, but it’s more affordable. Using this method, you can retrieve the results after our system collects them.
813: ‌Alternatively, you can specify pingback_url or postback_url when setting a task, and we will notify you on completion of tasks or send the results to you respectively. Note that if you use the postback_url field, you should also indicate the function that will be applied for data retrieval: regular, advanced or html. Learn more on our Help Center.
814: If you use the Standard method without specifying pingback_url or postback_url, you can receive the list of id for all completed tasks using the ‘Tasks Ready’ endpoint. It is designed to provide you with the list of completed tasks, which haven’t been collected yet. Then, you can retrieve the results using the ‘Task GET’ endpoint.
815: Learn more about task completion and obtaining a list of completed tasks in this help center article.
816: You can send up to 10000 POST and GET API calls per minute in total, with each POST call containing no more than 100 tasks. Contact us if you would like to raise the limit.
817: Visit DataForSEO Help Center to get practical tips for request handling depending on your SERP API payload volume.
818: ‌
819: Priorities and cost
820: The Live method delivers results in real-time, and accordingly, the cost of requests made using this method will be the highest.
821: The Standard method has two different priorities that stand for the relative speed of task execution and have different prices:
822: 1. Normal priority;
823: 2. High priority.
824: Note: setting depth above the default value will increase the cost of the task. For example, if the default value is 10, you will be billed for every 10 results. Learn more about the default depth values and base price in this Help Center article.
825: The cost can be calculated on the Pricing page. To learn more about the cost of all SERP API methods, priorities, and additional parameters, please refer to this help article. You can check your spending in your account dashboard or by making a separate call to the User Data endpoint.
826: You can test SERP API for free using DataForSEO Sandbox.
827: Instead of ‘login’ and ‘password’ use your credentials from https://app.dataforseo.com/api-access

790: Keywords Data API: Overview
791: This API is the ultimate source of data for keyword analysis
792: Keywords Data API encompasses two datasources (Google and Bing) working with a broad range of endpoints:
793: Google
794: Search Volume
795: Keywords For Site
796: Keywords For Keywords
797: Ad Traffic By Keywords
798: Google Trends Explore
799: Bing
800: Search Volume
801: Keywords For Site
802: Keywords For Keywords
803: Keyword Performance
804: Note that Google Ads Keywords Data API is based on the latest version of the Google Ads API that has replaced legacy Google AdWords API. If you’re using DataForSEO Google AdWords API, you need to upgrade to DataForSEO Google Ads API.
805: You can get the full list of available endpoints here. The returned results are specific to the indicated language, location, and other endpoint-specific parameters.
806: The restrictions of Google and Bing endpoints of Keywords Data API are related to Google Advertising Policy and Microsoft Advertising Ad Policies and Guidelines accordingly. Consequently, we are not able to return data for keywords that fall into such categories as weapons, tobacco, drugs, violence, terrorism, etc. If you want to learn more about Google restrictions and prohibited categories, check the article on our blog.
807: Please note that if you post, for instance, 100 keywords in a batch and at least one of them falls into one of the categories listed above, no data will be retrieved for the whole batch of keywords.
808: To find answers on common questions about Keywords Data API and find guidance on efficient use of its features, visit our Help Center.
809: Methods
810: The cost of using Keywords Data endpoints depends on the selected method and priority of task execution. Available methods and priorities are described below.
811: DataForSEO has two main methods to deliver the results: Standard and Live.
812: If your system requires delivering instant results, the Live method is the best solution for you. Unlike the Standard method, this method doesn’t require making separate POST and GET requests to the corresponding endpoints.
813: If you don’t need to receive data in real-time, you can use the Standard method of data retrieval. This method requires making separate POST and GET requests, but it’s more affordable. Using this method, you can retrieve the results after our system collects them.
814: ‌Alternatively, you can specify pingback_url or postback_url when setting a task, and we will notify you on completion of tasks or send them to you respectively.
815: If you need to set several tasks, you can receive the list of id for all completed tasks using ‘Tasks Ready’ endpoint, and then collect the results of each separate task using ‘Task GET’ endpoint.
816: ‌
817: You can send up to 10000 API calls per minute. Contact us if you would like to raise the limit.
818: Visit DataForSEO Help Center to get practical tips for request handling depending on your Keyword Data API payload volume.
819: Cost
820: The price depends on the method of data retrieval. The cost can be calculated on the Pricing page. You can check your spending in your account dashboard or by making a separate call to the User Data endpoint
821: You can test Keywords Data API for free using DataForSEO Sandbox.

790: Backlinks API: Overview
791: Backlinks API is the power source of robust backlink data for domains, subdomains and webpages
792: Backlinks API is designed to be your flexible, fast, and reliable solution for getting quality data on inbound links, referring domains and referring pages for any domain, subdomain, or webpage. This API supplies data based on the live index. We crawl the web each second nonstop, so the stats you get are always up to the moment.
793: We’re continuously evolving our crawling infrastructure, enlarging our index, and enriching the datasets with new stats. You can always check up-to-the-moment volume of our backlink database by calling the Index endpoint.
794: Backlinks API currently has the following set of mission-tailored endpoints that will supply you with a wealth of backlink data:
795: Summary will give you a complete backlink profile of the target.
796: History will reveal the target’s past link-building performance.
797: Backlinks will return a detailed list of the target’s backlinks.
798: Anchors will furnish you with the target’s anchor texts and stats.
799: Domain Pages will uncover pages with the highest and lowest amount of backlinks.
800: Domain Pages Summary provides a summary of all backlinks and related metrics for each page of the target domain or subdomain.
801: Referring Domains will provide backlink data broken down by domains pointing to the target.
802: Referring Networks will uncover IP addresses and subnets that are sending backlinks to the target.
803: Competitors will list competitors sharing a part of the backlink profile with the target.
804: Domain Intersection will list domains pointing to the specified targets.
805: Page Intersection will list referring pages pointing to the specified targets.
806: Timeseries Summary will provide backlink data for the target domain available during a period between the two indicated dates.
807: New & Lost Timeseries will provide the number of new and lost backlinks and referring domains for the specified target.
808: Using any endpoint, you can specify the number of results you want to retrieve, filter, and sort them. We do not charge any fees for using data filtering or sorting rules.
809: DataForSEO Backlinks API allows applying custom filtration to the dataset that will be retrieved. By using filters, you can effortlessly get exactly the data you need. For more information, please refer to the Filters in the Backlinks API.
810: In addition to the endpoints listed above, Backlinks API also allows retrieving backlink stats for up to 1000 domains, subdomains, or pages. Using bulk endpoints, you can get:
811: Bulk Ranks
812: Bulk Backlinks
813: Bulk Spam Score
814: Bulk Referring Domains
815: Bulk New & Lost Backlinks
816: Bulk New & Lost Referring Domains
817: To find answers on common questions about DataForSEO Backlinks API and find guidance on efficient use of its features, visit our Help Center.
818: Methods
819: DataForSEO Backlinks API supports only the Live method of data retrieval. It doesn’t require making separate POST and GET requests to the corresponding endpoints and delivers instant results. You can send up to 10000 API calls per minute. Contact us if you want to raise the limit.
820: Note that the maximum number of requests that can be sent simultaneously is limited to 30.
821: Cost
822: The cost can be calculated on the Pricing page. You can check your spending in your account dashboard or by making a separate call to the User Data endpoint.
823: You can test Backlinks API for free using DataForSEO Sandbox.
824: Instead of ‘login’ and ‘password’ use your credentials from https://app.dataforseo.com/api-access

790: OnPage API: Overview
791: OnPage API is the customizable crawling engine for extracting website performance data
792: Endpoints and Parameters
793: OnPage API encompasses multiple endpoints, which allow you to crawl any website or webpage according to customizable parameters and evaluate its on-page optimization performance against a multitude of SEO and website health benchmarks.
794: Sending a website for crawling is done through a POST request to the OnPage Task Post endpoint. Alongside the required input fields (domain name or URL and maximum number of pages to crawl), you can also use additional customizable parameters, such as:
795: ● Custom thresholds are applied through the checks_threshold field in the Task Post request and can be used to customize default threshold values for parameters in the checks array of OnPage API responses.
796: ● Custom JavaScript rules are applied through the custom_js field in the Task Post request and can be used to execute a custom JavaScript code when crawling pages. You can also use the enable_javascript parameter to execute built-in JavaScript rules set on a crawled site.
797: ● Store raw HTML is applied through the store_raw_html field in the Task Post request and can be used to obtain the HTML of the crawled page by making a request to the Raw HTML endpoint.
798: Besides these parameters, you can also instruct our crawler to:
799: ● load_resources such as images, stylesheets, scripts, and broken resources;
800: ● enable_javascript – that is execute Javascript on the crawled pages;
801: ● enable_browser_rendering to measure Core Web Vitals;
802: ● calculate_keyword_density to obtain keyword density values for target site.
803: Note: additional charges may apply. To learn more about the cost of all OnPage API parameters, please refer to this help article. Check our Pricing to calculate the costs.
804: After the website is fetched for crawling, you can start retrieving results using the following endpoints:
805: Summary – provides a summary of on-page issues found on a website;
806: Pages – returns a list of crawled pages with check-ups and other page performance metrics;
807: Pages by Resource – provides a list of pages and related data that contain a specific resource;
808: Resources – offers a list of resources on a website, including images, scripts, stylesheets, etc.;
809: Duplicate Tags – returns a list of pages that contain duplicate title or description tags;
810: Duplicate Content – returns a list of pages that have content similar to the page specified in the request;
811: Links – provides a list of internal and external links detected on a target website;
812: Redirect Chains – helps to quickly identify and trace down multiple redirects issues;
813: Non-indexable – returns a list of pages that are blocked from being indexed by search engines;
814: Waterfall– provides page speed insights data;
815: Keyword Density – provides keyword density and keyword frequency data for terms appearing on the specified website or web page;
816: Raw HTML – returns the HTML of a page you indicate in the request.
817: You can fetch data on pages gradually as our crawler processes the pages; this way you don’t have to wait until all the submitted pages are crawled. Alternatively, you can request complete results when the crawling is finished. The crawling process indicator is the crawl_progress field in the results of the Summary endpoint. ‌
818: OnPage API allows you to use pingbacks by specifying the pingback_url when setting a task, and we will notify you upon the completion of tasks. Learn more on our Help Center. If you use the Standard method without specifying the pingback_url, you can receive the list of id for all completed tasks using the ‘Tasks Ready’ endpoint. It is designed to provide you with a list of completed tasks, which haven’t been collected yet.
819: Besides auditing sites with the endpoints listed above, you can also perform quick scans of individual pages with the Instant Pages endpoint and capture screenshots of individual pages using the Page Screenshot endpoint. Both of these endpoint work in the Live mode, meaning that you’ll get the results right away in the API response without making a separate request.
820: To find answers on common questions about OnPage API and find guidance on efficient use of its features, visit our Help Center.
821: Limits and Force Stop
822: Using the Task POST function, you can send up to 10000 API calls per minute, with each POST call containing no more than 100 tasks. Contact us if you’d like to raise the limit.
823: Note 1: For all other endpoints of OnPage API (except Instant Pages and Page Screenshot), we do not recommend sending several tasks in one POST call as it may result in system overload and undesirable 4xx or 5xx errors.
824: Note 2: Unlike other OnPage API endpoints, Instant Pages and Page Screenshot work based on a Live method of data processing, meaning you don’t have to make a separate GET request to obtain the results. Using this endpoint, you can send up to 10000 API requests per minute, with each request containing no more than 20 tasks.
825: Note 3: The maximum number of simultaneous requests you can send is limited to 30.
826: In case you need to force stop the crawl process of websites you specified in a task, use the Force Stop endpoint.
827: Visit DataForSEO Help Center to get practical tips for request handling depending on your OnPage API payload volume.

848: The cost of using OnPage API endpoints depends on the parameters set in the OnPage Task Post request. In particular, using load_resources, enable_javascript, enable_browser_rendering, and calculate_keyword_density parameters will result in additional charges. To learn more about the cost of all OnPage API parameters, please refer to this help article.
849: Your account is charged for the actual number of crawled pages. If you specified more pages than a website contains, the difference will be refunded to your account after a task is completed.

790: DataForSEO Labs API: Overview
791: This API is the ultimate source of data for keyword research and search analytics
792: DataForSEO Labs API provides data on keywords, SERPs, and domains based on our in-house databases.
793: The endpoints of this API are grouped by the relevant search engine. In particular, you can get information on keywords, competitors, and rankings from:
794: • Google
795: • Amazon
796: • Google Play
797: • App Store
798: To find answers on common questions about DataForSEO Labs API and find guidance on efficient use of its features, visit our Help Center.
799: Methods
800: DataForSEO Labs API supports only the Live method of data retrieval. It doesn’t require making separate POST and GET requests to the corresponding endpoints and delivers instant results.
801: You can send up to 10000 API calls per minute. Contact us if you would like to raise the limit.

790: Business Data API: Overview
791: This API is designed to provide you with publicly available data on any business entity
792: This API is currently based on business reviews and business information publicly shared on the following platforms:
793: Google
794: Trustpilot
795: Tripadvisor
796: In addition to that, Business Data API encompasses Business Listings endpoints from the DataForSEO Business Listings Database.
797: We’re constantly working on increasing the number of datasources available in Business Data API.
798: To find answers on common questions about Business Data API and find guidance on efficient use of its features, visit our Help Center.
799: Methods
800: Business Data API supports Live and Standard methods of data retrieval.
801: The Live method doesn’t require making separate POST and GET requests to the corresponding endpoints and is suitable for systems that require delivering instant results.
802: The Standard method of data retrieval requires making separate POST and GET requests. Using this method, you can retrieve the results after our system collects them.
803: Alternatively, you can specify pingback_url or postback_url when setting a task, and we will notify you on completion of tasks or send them to you respectively.
804: If you do not specify pingback_url or postback_url, you can receive the list of id for all completed tasks using the ‘Tasks Ready’ endpoint. It is designed to provide you with the list of completed tasks, which haven’t been collected yet. Then, you can retrieve the results using the ‘Task GET’ endpoint.
805: Learn more about task completion and obtaining a list of completed tasks in this help center article.
806: You can send up to 10000 API calls per minute. Contact us if you would like to raise the limit.
807: Priorities and cost
808: The cost can be calculated on the Pricing page. You can check your spending in your account dashboard or by making a separate call to the User Data endpoint
809: Instead of ‘login’ and ‘password’ use your credentials from https://app.dataforseo.com/api-access

790: App Data API: Overview
791: This API is designed to provide accurate data on mobile applications
792: App Data API will help you to obtain data on app rankings, ratings, reviews, app collections featuring the product, and more. This data is especially useful for informing your product development roadmap, automating review management, and understanding the market.
793: We have selected the top two mobile application search platforms:
794: • Using Google App Data API, you can get data for any app published on Google Play.
795: • With Apple App Data API, you can collect data on apps from the App Store.
796: We plan to add more data sources in the future.
797: The returned results are specific to the indicated search engine (Google or Apple), language, and location parameters. We emulate the set location and search engine with the highest accuracy so that the results you receive will match the actual search results for the specified parameters at the time of task setting.
798: To find answers to common questions about App Data API and find guidance on efficient use of its features, visit our Help Center.
799: App Data API functions
800: App Data API provides search engine results with two standard functions: Advanced and HTML.
801: The Advanced function provides a full overview of data based on the specified keyword, app ID, or app collection category, as well as the language and location.
802: The HTML function provides a raw HTML page for the specified app name or identifier, language and location.
803: Note: HTML endpoints are supported in Google App Data API only.
804: ‌
805: Methods
806: App Data API supports only the Standard method of data retrieval. It requires making separate POST and GET requests. Using this method, you can retrieve the results after our system collects them.
807: ‌Alternatively, you can specify pingback_url or postback_url when setting a task, and we will notify you on completion of tasks or send the results to you respectively. Note that if you use the postback_url field, you should also indicate the function that will be applied for data retrieval: advanced or html.
808: If you do not specify pingback_url or postback_url, you can receive the list of id for all completed tasks using the ‘Tasks Ready’ endpoint. It is designed to provide you with the list of completed tasks, which haven’t been collected yet. Then, you can retrieve the results using the ‘Task GET’ endpoint.
809: Learn more about task completion and obtaining a list of completed tasks in this help center article.
810: You can send up to 10000 POST and GET API calls per minute in total, with each POST call containing no more than 100 tasks. Contact us if you would like to raise the limit.
811: ‌
812: Priorities and cost
813: The cost of using App Data API endpoints depends on the selected priority of task execution.
814: The Standard method has two different priorities that stand for the relative speed of task execution and have different prices:
815: 1. Normal priority;
816: 2. High priority.
817: The cost can be calculated on the Pricing page. You can check your spending in your account dashboard or by making a separate call to the User Data endpoint.
818: You can test App Data API for free using DataForSEO Sandbox.

790: Merchant API: Overview
791: Merchant API provides reliable e-commerce data about prices, products, and retailers
792: This API is the updated version of Merchant API v2.
793: Merchant API will provide you with all essential data and metrics for conducting comprehensive competitor analysis, price monitoring, and market niche research. It will help you to adjust and optimize the assortment and pricing according to different locations as well as open up new business opportunities based on quality data.
794: We have selected the top two e-commerce search engines: Google Shopping and Amazon, and we plan to add more in the future.
795: Google Shopping API will provide you with Google Shopping product listing data, product details from the product specification page, prices and sellers data as well as a full URL of the advertised product with all additional parameters.
796: Amazon API is designed to provide data on both organic and paid results from Amazon product listings as well as information about the product and ASINs of all its modifications listed on Amazon.
797: The returned results are specific to the indicated search engine, language and location parameters. We emulate set location and search engine with the highest accuracy so that the results you receive will match the actual search results for the specified parameters at the time of task setting. You can always check the returned results accessing the check_url in the Incognito mode to make sure the received data is entirely relevant. Note that user preferences, search history, and other personalized search factors are ignored by our system and thus would not be reflected in the returned results.
798: To find answers on common questions about Merchant API and find guidance on efficient use of its features, visit our Help Center.
799: Merchant API functions
800: Merchant API provides search engine results with two standard functions: Advanced and HTML.
801: The Advanced function provides a full overview of data based on the specified product name or identifier, language and location.
802: The HTML function provides a raw HTML page for the specified product name or identifier, language and location.
803: ‌
804: Methods
805: Merchant API supports only the Standard method of data retrieval. It requires making separate POST and GET requests. Using this method, you can retrieve the results after our system collects them.
806: ‌Alternatively, you can specify pingback_url or postback_url when setting a task, and we will notify you on completion of tasks or send the results to you respectively. Note that if you use the postback_url field, you should also indicate the function that will be applied for data retrieval: advanced or html.
807: If you do not specify pingback_url or postback_url, you can receive the list of id for all completed tasks using the ‘Tasks Ready’ endpoint. It is designed to provide you with the list of completed tasks, which haven’t been collected yet. Then, you can retrieve the results using the ‘Task GET’ endpoint.
808: Learn more about task completion and obtaining a list of completed tasks in this help center article.
809: You can send up to 10000 POST and GET API calls per minute in total, with each POST call containing no more than 100 tasks. Contact us if you would like to raise the limit.
810: Note: Google Shopping Sellers Ad URL endpoint doesn’t require making a separate POST request and provides results based on the $shop_ad_aclk parameter you specify in the GET URL.
811: ‌
812: Priorities and cost
813: The cost of using Merchant API endpoints depends on the selected priority of task execution.
814: The Standard method has two different priorities that stand for the relative speed of task execution and have different prices:
815: 1. Normal priority;
816: 2. High priority.
817: The cost can be calculated on the Pricing page.

790: Content Analysis API: Overview
791: Content Analysis API is a robust source of data for brand monitoring, sentiment analysis, and citation management
792: Content Analysis API is designed to help you discover citations of the target keyword or brand and analyze the sentiments around it.
793: This API identifies the positive, negative, and neutral polarity in any text, and detects the following sentiment connotations: anger, happiness, love, sadness, share (desire to share content), and fun.
794: Content Analysis API currently has the following set of endpoints:
795: Search will find all citations for the target keyword and provide detailed information about each citation.
796: Summary will give you a complete overview of citation data available for the target keyword.
797: Sentiment Analysis will reveal granular citation stats by positive, negative, and neutral sentiment polarity and by sentiment connotations.
798: Rating Distribution will return citation stats distribution by content rating.
799: Phrase Trends will furnish you with detailed citation stats by date for a target keyword.
800: Category Trends will supply you with citation trends by date in a target category.
801: Using the Search endpoint, you can specify the number of results you want to retrieve, filter, and sort them. We do not charge any fees for using data filtering or sorting rules.
802: The Search endpoint of Content Analysis API allows applying custom filtration to the dataset that will be retrieved. By using filters, you can effortlessly get exactly the data you need. For more information, please refer to Filters in Content Analysis API.
803: To find answers on common questions about DataForSEO Content Analysis API and find guidance on efficient use of its features, visit our Help Center.
804: Methods
805: DataForSEO Content Analysis API supports only the Live method of data retrieval. It doesn’t require making separate POST and GET requests to the corresponding endpoints and delivers instant results. You can send up to 10000 API calls per minute. Contact us if you want to raise the limit.
806: Cost
807: The cost can be calculated on the Pricing page. You can check your spending in your account dashboard or by making a separate call to the User Data endpoint.
808: You can test Content Analysis API for free using DataForSEO Sandbox.

790: AI Optimization API: Overview
791: This API is the ultimate source of data for AI search optimization
792: DataForSEO AI Optimization API provides data for keyword discovery, conversational optimization, and real-time LLM benchmarking.
793: It encompasses the following purpose-driven APIs:
794: • LLM Responses API enables real-time generation of structured responses from leading LLMs, including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity, based on your specified input parameters.
795: • LLM Scraper API provides scraped results from popular LLM platforms, based on the keyword and other input parameters.
796: • AI Keyword Data API delivers search volume estimates and user intent insights based on keyword usage in AI tools like ChatGPT and other large language models.
797: • LLM Mentions API provides data on keyword, brand and website mentions in LLMs, including metrics like AI search volume, impressions and mentions count.
798: To find answers on common questions about AI Optimization API and find guidance on most efficient use, visit our Help Center.
799: Methods
800: The cost of using AI Optimization API depends on the selected method and priority of task execution. Available methods and priorities are described below.
801: DataForSEO has two main methods to deliver the results: Standard and Live.
802: If your system requires delivering instant results, the Live method is the best solution for you. Unlike the Standard method, this method doesn’t require making separate POST and GET requests to the corresponding endpoints.
803: If you don’t need to receive data in real-time, you can use the Standard method of data retrieval. This method requires making separate POST and GET requests, but it’s more affordable. Using this method, you can retrieve the results after our system collects them.
804: ‌Alternatively, you can specify pingback_url or postback_url when setting a task, and we will notify you on completion of tasks or send them to you respectively.
805: If you need to set several tasks, you can receive the list of id for all completed tasks using ‘Tasks Ready’ endpoint, and then collect the results of each separate task using ‘Task GET’ endpoint.
806: AI Keyword Data API and LLM Mentions API support only the Live method of data retrieval. LLM Responses and LLM Scraper APIs support both Standard and Live methods, depending on the selected AI platform.
807: Cost
808: The cost can be calculated on the Pricing page. You can check your spending in your account dashboard or by making a separate call to the User Data endpoint
809: You can test AI Optimization API for free using DataForSEO Sandbox.
810: Instead of ‘login’ and ‘password’ use your credentials from https://app.dataforseo.com/api-access

295: Questions about pricing
296: How does DataForSEO pay-as-you-go pricing work?
297: DataForSEO uses a pay-as-you-go pricing model with no subscriptions or recurring fees. Add funds to your account and pay for API services as you use them. Each API has its own rates and billing units, which you can review on the corresponding API pricing pages.
298: Is there a minimum payment to use DataForSEO APIs?
299: Yes. The minimum account top-up is $50. This amount is added to your account balance and used to pay for API requests you make. It is not a subscription fee or a monthly payment, and you can use the balance at your own pace since it has no expiration date.
300: Does my DataForSEO account balance expire at the end of the month?
301: No. Funds added to your DataForSEO account do not expire. Any unused balance remains available for future API requests.
302: Can I try DataForSEO APIs for free?
303: Yes. You can sign up for free and use your $1 trial credit available to new accounts for trying our APIs in the Playground section of your DataForSEO Dashboard, via MCP in your preferred AI tool, or through our ready-made templates and integrations with platforms like n8n, Postman, Google Sheets. You can also test API integration for free using the DataForSEO Sandbox. The Sandbox provides sample responses for testing, while trial credit lets you test paid API functionality.
304: How can I monitor and limit my API spending?
305: You can track your API usage and costs in the DataForSEO Account Dashboard. Set daily spending limits for your entire account or individual APIs and endpoints to help manage your budget. You can also configure automatic balance top-ups.
306: Can I get a custom pricing quote for high-volume API usage?
307: Yes. If your project involves high request volumes, multiple APIs, or a custom data workflow, contact our support team for help estimating your expected costs and discussing your requirements.
308: How is the cost of an API request calculated?
309: The cost depends on the API, endpoint, mode (Standard and Live) and request parameters. Depending on the endpoint, pricing may be based on tasks, returned results, rows, pages, or other usage units. Check the dedicated pricing page of the API you're interested in for exact rates.
310: What is the difference between Standard and Live mode pricing?
311: Standard API requests are processed in a queue and generally cost less, but results take longer to become available. Live requests are processed immediately through a single POST request, delivering results faster at a higher cost. Available modes and exact rates vary by API endpoint.
312: What payment methods does DataForSEO accept?
313: DataForSEO accepts credit and debit cards, PayPal, and Amazon Pay. For payments of $5,000 or more, bank wire transfers and ACH payments are also available. An invoice is provided for every transaction. If you need an alternative payment method or assistance with a bank transfer, contact our 24/7 support team.

164: DataForSEO MCP Server
165: This is the new v3 MCP server. The previous v2+ MCP server is deprecated and lives at dataforseo/mcp-server-typescript-deprecated.
166: MCP server and CLI for LLM agents to browse DataForSEO API documentation and make authenticated API requests. By default the binary starts an MCP server on stdio; CLI commands are an optional second mode.
167: Quick Start
168: Start the MCP server on stdio (default mode; set DATAFORSEO_LOGIN / DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD):
169: npx dataforseo-mcp-server@latest
170: HTTP transport (port 3000; override with PORT):
171: npx dataforseo-mcp-server@latest --mode http
172: Authentication
173: OAuth 2.0 (default for HTTP MCP): works out of the box. MCP clients discover the DataForSEO authorization server via Protected Resource metadata and send Authorization: Bearer tokens.
174: Fallback: API login/password via environment variables (HTTP Basic). Required for CLI and stdio MCP; on HTTP it is used when no Authorization header is present.
175: # bash / macOS / Linux
176: export DATAFORSEO_LOGIN="your_api_login"
177: export DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD="your_api_password"
178: # PowerShell
179: $env:DATAFORSEO_LOGIN="your_api_login"
180: $env:DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD="your_api_password"
181: REM CMD
182: set DATAFORSEO_LOGIN=your_api_login
183: set DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD=your_api_password
184: DATAFORSEO_USERNAME is accepted as an alias for DATAFORSEO_LOGIN. Get API keys at https://app.dataforseo.com/api-access.
185: MCP Server
186: The same tool implementations power both the MCP server and the CLI. One binary serves both modes; MCP is the default.
187: How the binary chooses a mode:
188: MCP stdio — default when no CLI command is passed
189: MCP HTTP — pass --mode http (Streamable HTTP on port 3000; override with PORT)
190: CLI — when the first command is docs or request, or when --cli / --help / --version is passed
191: MCP stdio (default):
192: npx dataforseo-mcp-server
193: MCP HTTP:
194: npx dataforseo-mcp-server --mode http
195: CLI:
196: npx dataforseo-mcp-server docs index
197: MCP client config (Cursor, Claude Desktop, and similar clients that use mcpServers):
198: Via URL — use the hosted remote MCP server, or start a local HTTP server (npx dataforseo-mcp-server --mode http) and point the client at it. OAuth works out of the box; env credentials are optional fallback only.
199: Public remote MCP server URL: https://mcp.dataforseo.com/v3/mcp
200: {
201: "mcpServers": {
202: "dataforseo": {
203: "url": "https://mcp.dataforseo.com/v3/mcp"
204: }
205: }
206: }
207: Local server (default port 3000):
208: {
209: "mcpServers": {
210: "dataforseo": {
211: "url": "http://localhost:3000/mcp"
212: }
213: }
214: }
215: Via command (stdio) — the client starts the binary itself (stdio is the default mode). OAuth is not used on this transport — set env credentials (or pass them in the MCP client env block):
216: {
217: "mcpServers": {
218: "dataforseo": {
219: "command": "npx",
220: "args": [
221: "dataforseo-mcp-server",
222: // Optional additional args:
223: // "--docs-cache-dir", "D:\\my-docs-cache",
224: // "--configuration", "field-config.json"
225: ],
226: "env": {
227: "DATAFORSEO_LOGIN": "your_api_login",
228: "DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD": "your_api_password",
229: // Optional additional env:
230: // "FIELD_CONFIG_PATH": "field-config.json"
231: }
232: }
233: }
234: }
235: From the repo root during development:
236: {
237: "mcpServers": {
238: "dataforseo": {
239: "command": "npx",
240: "args": ["tsx", "src/index.ts"],
241: "cwd": "/path/to/mcp-server-typescript"
242: }
243: }
244: }
245: MCP Tools
246: Tool
247: Title
248: Description
249: docs_index
250: Docs Index
251: Fetch documentation index, optionally filtered by section (24h cache)
252: docs_list_sections
253: Docs List Sections
254: Return available documentation section names
255: docs_search
256: Docs Search
257: Fetch documentation from a documentation URL (needCodeExample, 24h cache)
258: api_request
259: API Request
260: Make an authenticated API request
261: api_request uses .ai paths by default. Set noAiMode to true in MCP requests, or pass --no-ai-mode in the CLI, to use the standard path. Request body is passed as data (JSON object or array). The --param option is CLI-only.
262: HTTP transport
263: Streamable HTTP endpoints:
264: POST /mcp
265: POST /http
266: OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource metadata (RFC 9728) is always exposed so MCP clients can discover the authorization server and authenticate with Bearer tokens:
267: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
268: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp
269: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/http
270: Behind a reverse proxy, set TRUST_PROXY=true so metadata URLs use https.
271: Auth priority on HTTP requests:
272: Authorization: Basic header
273: Authorization: Bearer header (OAuth access token)
274: Env credentials (DATAFORSEO_LOGIN / DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD) — fallback when no Authorization header is sent
275: CLI (optional)
276: In addition to MCP, the same binary exposes docs and request as CLI commands.
277: Commands
278: Command
279: Description
280: npx dataforseo-mcp-server docs index
281: Fetch full API documentation index
282: npx dataforseo-mcp-server docs index --section "SERP API"
283: Filter index by API section
284: npx dataforseo-mcp-server docs index --list-sections
285: List available sections
286: npx dataforseo-mcp-server docs search <url>
287: Fetch documentation from a documentation URL or path (cURL example only by default)
288: npx dataforseo-mcp-server docs search <url> --need-code-example
289: Fetch documentation with PHP, Node.js, Python, and C# examples
290: npx dataforseo-mcp-server request -X <method> -p <path>
291: Make an authenticated API request (.ai path by default)
292: From a built local clone you can also use npx . instead of npx dataforseo-mcp-server.
293: Examples
294: # Browse SERP API endpoints
295: npx dataforseo-mcp-server docs index --section "SERP API"
296: # Read endpoint documentation (path or full docs URL)
297: npx dataforseo-mcp-server docs search serp/google/organic/live/regular
298: npx dataforseo-mcp-server docs search https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/serp/google/organic/live/regular
299: # Include multi-language code examples (PHP, Node.js, Python, C#)
300: npx dataforseo-mcp-server docs search backlinks/referring_networks/live --need-code-example
301: # Live SERP request (recommended: use --param)
302: npx dataforseo-mcp-server request -X POST -p /v3/serp/google/organic/live/regular \
303: --param keyword=dataforseo --param language_code=en --param location_code=2840
304: # Same request via JSON body
305: npx dataforseo-mcp-server request -X POST -p /v3/serp/google/organic/live/regular \
306: -d '[{"keyword":"dataforseo","location_code":2840,"language_code":"en"}]'
307: Documentation responses are cached for 24 hours. Default cache directory:
308: Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\dataforseo-mcp-server\docs-cache
309: macOS: ~/Library/Caches/dataforseo-mcp-server/docs-cache
310: Linux: ~/.cache/dataforseo-mcp-server/docs-cache (or $XDG_CACHE_HOME)
311: Override with --cache-dir <path> on CLI docs commands. For MCP, pass --docs-cache-dir <path> in server startup args.
312: API responses are returned as the response body only (parsed JSON when possible). When a field configuration is loaded, api_request / request responses are trimmed to the configured fields for that endpoint path (see Field configuration).
313: Field configuration
314: Optionally limit which fields are returned from API responses. Unlike the previous multi-tool MCP server (keys = tool names), this package keys the config by API endpoint path.
315: # MCP stdio (default when no CLI command is passed)
316: npx dataforseo-mcp-server --configuration field-config.json
317: # MCP HTTP
318: npx dataforseo-mcp-server --mode http --configuration field-config.json
319: # CLI
320: npx dataforseo-mcp-server --configuration field-config.json request -X POST -p /v3/backlinks/summary/live --param target=example.com
321: Or set env:
322: FIELD_CONFIG_PATH — path to a JSON file (Node)
323: FIELD_CONFIG_JSON — inline JSON string (Node / Cloudflare Worker)
324: Minimal example (see field-config.example.json for a fuller sample):
325: {
326: "supported_fields": {
327: "/v3/serp/google/organic/live/advanced": ["id", "items.title", "items.url", "status_code"],
328: "/v3/backlinks/summary/live": ["id", "items.backlinks", "items.referring_domains", "status_code"]
329: }
330: }
331: Behavior:
332: Built-in defaults always apply for /v3/on_page/lighthouse/live/json (shrunk Lighthouse payload). Custom config merges on top and can override any path.
333: Path match ignores .ai suffix, trailing slash, and host (full URLs work).
334: If the path is configured with a non-empty field list → only those fields are kept (applied to each tasks[].result[] item).
335: If the path has an empty field list [] → full response for that path (disables filtering).
336: If the path is missing from both defaults and custom config → full response.
337: Copy the example and trim to the endpoints you use:
338: cp field-config.example.json my-config.json
339: Architecture
340: src/
341: ├── index.ts # Unified entry (MCP by default stdio; CLI if docs/request/--cli)
342: ├── config/ # URLs, sections, auth server
343: ├── core/
344: │ ├── api/ # auth, client, path, request-body
345: │ ├── cli/ # program, error, output
346: │ ├── config/ # field configuration + defaults
347: │ ├── docs/ # path, section, cache
348: │ ├── http/ # fetch
349: │ ├── mcp/ # startup args (--configuration, --docs-cache-dir)
350: │ ├── tools/ # shared CLI + MCP tool implementations
351: │ ├── utils/ # field filter
352: │ ├── env.ts
353: │ └── version.ts
354: ├── mcp/
355: │ ├── init-mcp-server.ts
356: │ ├── tool-definition.ts
357: │ ├── auth-middleware.ts
358: │ ├── http-routes.ts
359: │ ├── index.ts # stdio transport
360: │ └── index-http.ts # streamable HTTP
361: └── worker/ # Cloudflare Worker entry (built separately)
362: Build outputs

579: FAQ
580: Q
581: What is an SEO API?
582: A
583: An SEO API gives teams programmatic access to SEO data, including keyword rankings, backlinks, domain metrics, site audits, and competitor insights. This means you can assess that information without going through the platform interface manually. Instead, you can pull data directly into your own tools, or connect via SEO MCP to access it from inside an AI assistant.
584: Show more
585: Show less
586: Q
587: Why is it ideal to use an API for SEO?
588: A
589: For agencies and teams working at scale, manual data collection creates a bottleneck. You need to log in, export files, connect them with other sources, and repeat the process across multiple clients. An API removes those steps. Data flows directly into your dashboards, analytics platforms, CRMs, and BI tools without manual intervention at each stage. It also means running analyses at a volume that manual work can’t match.
590: Show more
591: Show less
592: Q
593: What SEO data can I access with this API?
594: A
595: SE Ranking’s API is structured across two layers. The Data API covers keyword research, backlink analysis, domain performance, SERP data, site audits, and AI visibility research. The Project API lets you manage and automate SEO workflows within the platform, including rank tracking, keyword grouping, and competitor monitoring at the project level. All data is returned as structured JSON.
596: Show more
597: Show less
598: Q
599: Is SE Ranking’s API data accurate?
600: A
601: Yes, SE Ranking’s API pulls from its large database and real-time analysis to provide accurate data. It collects and updates new SEO data daily, with a database that employs in-depth tracking to cover global and local search results. It also uses a vast link index to provide accurate data on backlinks.
602: Show more
603: Show less
604: Q
605: What are the limitations?
606: A
607: A few things worth knowing before you integrate. SE Ranking doesn’t currently offer first-party SDKs and integration is done via the REST API reference and a Postman collection for endpoint testing. Also, default requests-per-second limits are lower than some competitors’, though these can be increased by contacting the support team. If you’re migrating from another API provider, you’ll need to remap your endpoints
608: Show more
609: Show less
610: Q
611: How do I access SE Ranking’s API?
612: A
613: Accessing our API is straightforward. Just log in to your SE Ranking account, navigate to the API tab under the Settings section, and retrieve your unique API key. Once you have your API key, you can use it for different purposes. For more information, refer to our API documentation.
614: Show more
615: Show less
616: Q
617: How do I get an SE Ranking API key?
618: A
619: API is included with every SE Ranking subscription. To get your key, log in to your SE Ranking account, go to the API section. From there, you can copy your API key and use it to integrate SE Ranking’s data into your applications, dashboards, or reports.
620: Show more
621: Show less
622: Q
623: What is the cost of API access?
624: A
625: API access comes with any SE Ranking plan (Core at $129/mo and Growth at $279/mo). You can even test it in the free trial account. For higher volume, the API Add-On starts at $149/month and can be added to any existing subscription. Pay-as-you-go is also available with a $50 minimum deposit.
626: Show more
627: Show less
628: Q
629: Can I use this API without technical expertise?
630: A
631: Yes, you don’t need a development team to use the SE Ranking’s API. One method is to run a pre-written code in Google Colab to gather data, then apply specific formulas within Google Sheets to clean the results. Use our code as an example and adjust it as needed. MCP is another path. Once connected, you can query keyword rankings, backlink data, site audit results directly from Claude, Codex, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible AI assistant in plain language. No code required.
632: Show more
633: Show less
634: Q
635: What is an MCP server?
636: A
637: MCP is a bridge between AI models like Claude and external tools, data sources, and services. SE Ranking’s MCP server connects SE Ranking’s data directly to AI assistants like Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and any other client. Once connected, you can query keyword rankings, backlink data, site audits, and more in plain language, without switching between tools or writing code.
638: Show more
639: Show less
640: Q
641: How does MCP differ from the API?
642: A
643: API and MCP server serve different use cases. The API gives you programmatic access to SE Ranking’s data for building custom integrations, automated workflows, and data pipelines. The MCP server is for querying SE Ranking data conversationally from inside an AI assistant. You can run research, analyses, and AI-assisted workflows without switching context. Both are included in every SE Ranking plan.

437: New to SE Ranking MCP? What it does, pricing and use cases
438: Start with 100K free credits → SE Ranking SEO MCP
439: New · MCP Hub
440: Explore the MCP Hub
441: Whether you’re connecting MCP for the first time or building advanced workflows, the MCP Hub brings every useful resource into one place, so you can start simple and level up at your own pace.
442: Setup Use cases Skills library Prompt library Blueprints Video guides
443: Go to MCP Hub →
444: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides a standardized interface that allows any compatible AI model to access your SE Ranking and SE Visible data simply and securely.
445: MCP server server follows the authenticated remote MCP spec, so it’s centrally hosted and managed. Connect in one click in Claude or ChatGPT, natively in Cursor and other clients, or use the mcp-remote module for clients that don’t support remote servers.
446: What you can access
447: Through the MCP server, your AI assistant can work with data from these SE Ranking and SE Visible products*:
448: Data API: keyword research, backlinks, domain analysis, SERP, and more
449: Project API: your projects, rank tracking, audits, and competitors
450: Local Marketing API: your locations, local rankings, Google Business Profile, business listings, and reviews
451: SE Visible API: your AI visibility projects, brands, topics, prompts, and sources
452: *The data available to you depends on your subscription. Not every API endpoint is available through MCP. Setup is the same for every product. Use your SE Ranking account, or an API key generated in the API Dashboard of your SE Ranking or SE Visible account.
453: Setup Instructions
454: General
455: Our MCP server supports Streamable HTTP transports. This transport uses OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration for authentication at the following address:
456: Copy
457: https://api.seranking.com/mcp
458: Jump to your client: Claude · ChatGPT · Codex · Cursor · VS Code · v0 · Windsurf · Zed · Gemini CLI · Others.
459: Sub-accounts
460: If you’re a sub-account on a shared SE Ranking workspace, the Sign in with SE Ranking button won’t connect any tools. API access lives with the master account, not with sub-accounts. Sub-account API keys are on the way; until they’re released, use the workaround below.
461: To connect a sub-account:
462: Get the API key from your account administrator.
463: In the connection dialog, choose Enter API keys manually.
464: Paste the key when prompted.
465: Claude
466: Claude (Web & Desktop)
467: Add the official SE Ranking connector and click Connect. In Claude Desktop, you can also find it under Customize → Connectors by searching for SE Ranking.
468: Claude Code
469: Two options. Pick one.
470: Option A: OAuth (recommended) — opens a browser on first connect, stores the token locally, and reuses it across sessions.
471: Copy
472: claude mcp add --transport http se-ranking https://api.seranking.com/mcp
473: Then run /mcp once you’ve opened a Claude Code session to go through the authentication flow.
474: Option B: API key — skip the OAuth flow and pass your key as headers. Right for headless environments, CI runners, shared dev boxes, or when the browser handoff is awkward.
475: Copy
476: claude mcp add --transport http se-ranking https://api.seranking.com/mcp \
477: --header "X-Api-Key: *****"
478: Grab the key from the API Dashboard in your SE Ranking or SE Visible account. Available tools depend on your subscription.
479: ChatGPT
480: Open the official SE Ranking plugin, click Install plugin, and sign in to authorize. You can also find it in ChatGPT under Plugins by searching for SE Ranking.
481: Codex
482: The setup steps for the MCP server are the same regardless of whether you use the IDE Extension or the CLI since the configuration is shared.
483: Configuration via CLI:
484: Run the following command in Terminal:
485: Copy
486: codex mcp add se-ranking --url https://api.seranking.com/mcp
487: This will automatically prompt you to log in with your SE Ranking account and connect it to your Codex.
488: Note: If this is the first time you are using an MCP in Codex you will need to enable the rmcp feature for this to work. Add the following into your ~/.codex/config.toml:
489: Copy
490: [features]
491: experimental_use_rmcp_client = true
492: Configuration through environment variables:
493: 1. Open the ~/.codex/config.toml file in your preferred editor.
494: 2. Add the following:
495: Copy
496: [features]
497: experimental_use_rmcp_client = true
498: [mcp_servers.se-ranking]
499: url = "https://api.seranking.com/mcp"
500: 3. Run codex mcp login se-ranking to move through the authentication flow.
501: Cursor
502: Add the following to .cursor/mcp.json (project) or ~/.cursor/mcp.json (global):
503: Copy
504: {
505: "mcpServers": {
506: "se-ranking": {
507: "url": "https://api.seranking.com/mcp"
508: }
509: }
510: }
511: Cursor supports Streamable HTTP and OAuth natively. An OAuth window will open on first use to authenticate with your SE Ranking account.
512: Visual Studio Code
513: Copy
514: {
515: "mcpServers": {
516: "se-ranking": {
517: "command": "npx",
518: "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://api.seranking.com/mcp"]
519: }
520: }
521: }
522: 1. Ctrl+P / Cmd+P and search for MCP: Add Server.
523: 2. Select Command (stdio).
524: 3. Enter the following configuration, and hit enter:
525: Copy
526: npx -y mcp-remote https://api.seranking.com/mcp
527: 4. Enter the name SE Ranking and hit enter.
528: 5. Activate the server using MCP: List Servers, selecting se-ranking, and selecting Start Server.
529: v0 by Vercel
530: To add the MCP to v0, you can install from the connections page.
531: Windsurf
532: 1. Ctrl+, / Cmd+, to open Windsurf settings.
533: 2. Scroll to Cascade > MCP servers.
534: 3. Select Add Server > Add custom server.
535: 4. Add the following:
536: Copy
537: {
538: "mcpServers": {
539: "se-ranking": {
540: "command": "npx",
541: "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://api.seranking.com/mcp"]
542: }
543: }
544: }
545: Zed
546: Cmd+, to open Zed settings. Add the following:
547: Copy
548: {
549: "context_servers": {
550: "se-ranking": {
551: "source": "custom",
552: "command": "npx",
553: "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://api.seranking.com/mcp"],
554: "env": {}
555: }
556: }
557: }
558: Gemini CLI
559: Add to ~/.gemini/settings.json:
560: Copy
561: {
562: "mcpServers": {
563: "se-ranking": {
564: "command": "npx",
565: "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://api.seranking.com/mcp"]
566: }
567: }
568: }
569: Save and launch Gemini CLI. Authorize when prompted.
570: Others
571: Hundreds of other tools now support MCP servers. You can configure them to use our MCP server with the following settings:
572: Command: npx
573: Arguments: -y mcp-remote https://api.seranking.com/mcp
574: Environment: None
575: FAQ
576: Why am I seeing an internal server error when trying to connect?
577: Enter the following in the Terminal to clear saved auth info: rm -rf ~/.mcp-auth then try again to connect.
578: Additionally you may need to update to a newer version of Node if required.
579: What happens when I connect?
580: A browser window opens to seranking.com where you log in with your SE Ranking account and approve access. After approval, you’re redirected back to your client and the connection is established. If the window doesn’t open automatically, check your client for a URL to paste into a browser manually.
581: How do I know the connection worked?
582: Claude.ai / Desktop: SE Ranking moves out of Not connected and its tools become available in chats.
583: Claude Code: Run /mcp and confirm se-ranking shows as connected and its tools are listed.
584: Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed: The server appears as connected in the MCP panel and tools are listed.
585: All clients: Try a prompt like “Using SE Ranking MCP, give me traffic for seranking.com in the US.” If it returns real data, it works.
586: I’m using WSL on Windows, and seeing an error
587: WSL can have issues with the OAuth redirect. Configure the server in your client’s Windows-side config file instead, or run the setup from PowerShell:
588: {
589: "mcpServers": {
590: "se-ranking": {
591: "command": "npx",
592: "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://api.seranking.com/mcp"]
593: }
594: }
595: }
596: Does the MCP support Streamable HTTP?
597: Yes, at the https://api.seranking.com/mcp endpoint.
598: Can I authenticate with my own API key?
599: Yes. Instead of using the interactive authentication flow, you can pass your API key in the X-Api-Key header. See Claude Code, Option B for an example. This works well for headless environments, CI runners, and shared dev boxes.
600: A key passed this way has the same access as your account. Restricted or read-only API keys aren’t available yet.
601: No tools appearing after connecting?
602: Verify your SE Ranking or SE Visible account has API access at the API Dashboard.
603: Run /mcp in Claude Code to check live connection status.
604: Try removing and re-adding the server.
605: If you need further assistance, contact us at [email protected].

436: Keyword Research
437: Keyword Research API provides programmatic access to keyword metrics and discovery. Data is refreshed on a monthly basis.
438: Using the API, you can:
439: retrieve keyword metrics such as search volume, CPC, competition, difficulty, and historical trends
440: discover similar keywords with the same user intent
441: find related keywords based on overlapping search results
442: get question keywords associated with a seed keyword
443: discover long-tail keywords that are lower-volume and more specific
444: Get Keyword Metrics (Bulk)
445: POST https://api.seranking.com/v1/keywords/export
446: Cost: 100 credits per request
447: Retrieves various data points for a list of specified keywords within a given regional database. It’s designed for bulk analysis and returns metrics like search volume, CPC, competition, keyword difficulty, search intent, and historical search volume trends for each submitted keyword.
448: By default, the returned history_trend covers the 12 most recent months, ending at the current month. Use the optional history_to parameter to end the window at an earlier month, and history_from to start it later — together they return a custom date range (e.g. to reconstruct a keyword’s seasonality as of a past date). The window is always capped at 12 months.
449: Request
450: Send source in the query string and all other inputs in a JSON request body (Content-Type: application/json).
451: Note: The source parameter must be provided as a query parameter in the endpoint URL.
452: Query parameters
453: ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
454: sourceStringYes—Country code of the regional keyword database (e.g., us). For acceptable values, see Regional database codes.
455: Body parameters
456: ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
457: keywordsString[]Yes—Array of keywords to analyze, e.g. ["seo platform", "seranking.com"]. Between 1 and 5,000 keywords per request.
458: sortStringNocpcField the results are sorted by: volume, cpc, difficulty, or competition.
459: sort_orderStringNodescSorting order: asc (ascending) or desc (descending).
460: history_fromStringNo—Start month of the history_trend window, YYYY-MM-DD (the day is ignored). Only takes effect together with history_to — sent on its own it is ignored. The window then runs from history_from through history_to inclusive, capped at the most recent 12 months. Must not be later than history_to.
461: history_toStringNoCurrent monthEnd month of the history_trend window, YYYY-MM-DD (the day is ignored). On its own it returns the 12 months ending at this month — e.g. 2024-05-01 returns 2023-06-01 through 2024-05-01. Combine with history_from for a shorter range. Must not be a future month.
462: Request example
463: Copy
464: curl -X POST 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/keywords/export?source=us' \
465: -H 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY' \
466: -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
467: -d '{
468: "keywords": ["seo platform", "seranking.com"],
469: "sort": "cpc",
470: "sort_order": "desc"
471: }'
472: Request example — custom history window
473: Copy
474: curl -X POST 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/keywords/export?source=us' \
475: -H 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY' \
476: -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
477: -d '{
478: "keywords": ["seo platform"],
479: "history_from": "2024-01-01",
480: "history_to": "2024-05-01"
481: }'
482: Omit history_from to get the full 12 months ending at history_to.
483: Response parameters
484: If successful, the server returns a JSON array. Each object in this array corresponds to one of the keywords submitted in the request and contains the requested data points.
485: ParameterTypeDescription
486: is_data_foundBooleanIndicates whether data was successfully found and retrieved for this specific keyword: true (found) / false (otherwise).
487: keywordStringKeyword phrase as submitted in the request.
488: volumeIntegerAverage monthly search volume for this keyword in the specified source database.
489: cpcFloatAverage Cost Per Click for this keyword.
490: competitionFloatPaid-search competition level for this keyword, on a 0–1 scale (higher = more competition).
491: difficultyIntegerKeyword difficulty — how hard it is to rank organically for this keyword, on a 0–100 scale (higher = harder).
492: intentsArrayArray of search intent codes. Possible values: I (Informational — user is looking for information), C (Commercial — user is investigating products, services, or brands), T (Transactional — user wants to complete an action or purchase), L (Local — user is looking for a location or something nearby), N (Navigational — user is looking for a specific website or page).
493: history_trendObjectObject containing historical search volume data for the keyword. Each key is a YYYY-MM-DD string representing the first day of a month, and the value is the search volume for that month. By default the window covers the 12 months ending at the current month; it is shifted by history_to and narrowed by history_from (see Request).

544: Get similar keywords
545: GET https://api.seranking.com/v1/keywords/similar
546: Cost: 10 credits per returned keyword
547: Retrieves keywords similar to a specified seed keyword within a regional database. Semantically similar keywords include synonyms, close variations, or different phrasings with the same intent.
