435: Project API / Website Audit
436: Website Audit
437: The Website Audit API crawls sites on demand and surfaces technical SEO issues: broken links, missing tags, slow pages, indexability problems, and more. Results are retrieved on demand.
438: Plan limits apply to the total number of pages crawled. Creating an audit and rechecking an audit both count crawled pages against that plan limit. All other operations (reads and configuration updates) are free.
439: Create audit
440: POST https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits
441: Creates a website audit that crawls the HTML of a target site. Suitable for static and server-side-rendered sites. Enable csr in settings for JavaScript-rendered pages.
442: Note: Page crawl limit depends on your subscription plan.
443: Request parameters
444: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
445: domainStringYesDomain to be audited (e.g., domain.com).
446: titleStringNoCustom title of the audit report (max 300 characters). Defaults to domain.
447: settingsObjectNoAudit configuration settings. Only include parameters you want to override (see settings object below).
448: Request example
449: Copy
450: curl --location 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits' \
451: --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
452: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY' \
453: --data '{
454: "domain": "example.com",
455: "title": "Full Audit - example.com",
456: "settings": {
457: "source_site": 1,
458: "source_sitemap": 1,
459: "source_subdomain": 1,
460: "source_file": 0,
461: "check_robots": 1,
462: "ignore_noindex": 1,
463: "ignore_nofollow": 1,
464: "ignore_params": 2,
465: "custom_params": "utm_source, utm_medium, utm_term, utm_content, utm_campaign, cid, PHPSESSID, fbclid, gclid",
466: "csr": 0,
467: "user_agent": 0,
468: "login": "",
469: "password": "",
470: "max_pages": 10000,
471: "max_depth": 15,
472: "max_req": 300,
473: "max_redirects": 10,
474: "max_size": 5000,
475: "min_title_len": 30,
476: "max_title_len": 60,
477: "min_description_len": 50,
478: "max_description_len": 160,
479: "min_words": 300,
480: "max_h1_len": 70,
481: "max_h2_len": 80,
482: "allow": "/blog\n/products",
483: "disallow": "/admin\n/staging",
484: "hide": "/cdn-cgi\n/wp-json",
485: "schedule_type": "week",
486: "schedule_wdays": [1, 2],
487: "schedule_hour": 6,
488: "schedule_day": 1,
489: "schedule_repeat": 1,
490: "schedule_repeat_interval": 1,
491: "send_report": 1,
492: "report_emails": "[email protected], [email protected]"
493: }
494: }'
495: Response parameters
496: If successful, the server returns a JSON object containing the unique ID for the newly created audit.
497: ParameterTypeDescription
498: idIntegerUnique identifier of the audit report.
499: Response example
500: Copy
501: {
502: "id": 700237036
503: }
504: List audits
505: GET https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits
506: Returns all audits associated with the account, with pagination and filtering.
507: Request parameters
508: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
509: limitIntegerNoNumber of audits to return. Defaults to 100.
510: offsetIntegerNoNumber of audits to skip before starting to collect the result set. Defaults to 0.
511: searchStringNoFilters audits by matching title or URL.
512: date_startStringNoStart date for filtering audits (in YYYY-MM-DD).
513: date_endStringNoEnd date for filtering audits (in YYYY-MM-DD).
514: Request example
515: Copy
516: curl --location 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits?limit=10&offset=0&search=booking.com&date_start=2025-07-01&date_end=2025-07-31' \
517: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY'
518: Response parameters
519: If successful, the server returns a JSON object containing the total number of audits and an array of audit objects.
520: ParameterTypeDescription
521: totalIntegerNumber of audits matching the filter criteria.
522: itemsArrayArray of audit objects.
523: Each object in the items array has the following structure:
524: ParameterTypeDescription
525: idIntegerUnique identifier of the audit report.
526: group_idIntegerAudit group identifier.
527: urlStringURL of the audited website.
528: titleStringTitle of the audit report.
529: has_projectBooleanIndicates whether the audit is linked to a project.
530: site_idIntegerInternal site identifier.
531: last_updateStringDate of last audit update ( in YYYY-MM-DD).
532: statusStringCurrent audit status (for example, finished, processing).
533: errorStringError message if the audit failed, otherwise null.
534: error_paramsObjectError details if available.
535: statsObjectLatest audit statistics.
536: prev_statsObjectStatistics from the previous audit run (can be null).
537: versionStringAudit engine version.
538: owner_account_idIntegerOwner account identifier.
539: is_newIntegerIndicates whether the audit is newly created (1 – yes, 0 – no).
540: Response example
541: Copy
542: {
543: "items": [
544: {
545: "id": 700138456,
546: "group_id": 0,
547: "url": "http://booking.com",
548: "title": "booking.com",
549: "has_project": true,
550: "site_id": 10113599,
551: "last_update": "2025-07-08",
552: "status": "finished",
553: "error": null,
554: "error_params": null,
555: "stats": {
556: "score": 69,
557: "errors": 2303,
558: "warnings": 3710,
559: "notices": 10875,
560: "crawled": 1830
561: },
562: "prev_stats": null,
563: "version": "2.0",
564: "owner_account_id": 4242308,
565: "is_new": 1
566: }
567: ],
568: "total": 1
569: }
570: Get audit status
571: GET https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/status
572: Returns the real-time status of a specific audit. Useful for monitoring crawl progress before fetching the full report.
573: Request parameters
574: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
575: audit_idIntegerYesUnique audit ID (path parameter).
576: Request example
577: Copy
578: curl --location 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/status?audit_id=123' \
579: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY'
580: Response parameters
581: If successful, the server returns a JSON object containing the current audit status and key metrics.
582: ParameterTypeDescription
583: statusStringCurrent audit status. Possible values: queued, processing, finished, cancelled, expired.
584: total_pagesIntegerNumber of pages crawled.
585: total_errorsIntegerNumber of errors found.
586: total_warningsIntegerNumber of warnings found.
587: total_passedIntegerNumber of passed checks.
588: start_timeStringAudit start timestamp.
589: audit_timeStringAudit completion timestamp. Present if the audit is finished.
590: Response example
591: Copy
592: {
593: "total_pages": 1009,
594: "total_warnings": 979,
595: "total_errors": 346,
596: "total_passed": 77,
597: "status": "finished",
598: "start_time": "2025-07-29 11:06:23",
599: "audit_time": "2025-07-29 11:19:33"
600: }
601: Get audit report
602: GET https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/report
603: Returns a complete audit report, including health score, domain properties, and issues.
604: Request parameters
605: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
606: audit_idIntegerYesUnique audit ID (path parameter).
607: Request example
608: Copy
609: curl --location 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/report?audit_id=123' \
610: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY'
611: Response parameters
612: If successful, the server returns a JSON object containing the complete audit report.
613: ParameterTypeDescription
614: is_finishedBooleanIndicates whether the audit is completed.
615: score_percentIntegerOverall website health score (0–100).
616: total_pagesIntegerNumber of pages crawled.
617: total_errorsIntegerNumber of errors found.
618: total_warningsIntegerNumber of warnings found.
619: total_noticesIntegerNumber of notices found.
620: total_passedIntegerNumber of passed checks.
621: audit_timeStringAudit completion timestamp.
622: domain_propsObjectDomain properties and metadata (see domain_props object below).
623: sectionsArrayAn array of objects, where each object represents a category of audit checks (see sections array below).
624: domain_props object
625: ParameterTypeDescription
626: dtIntegerDomain trust score.
627: domainStringDomain name.
628: domainsStringNumber of referring domains.
629: expdateStringExpiration date of domain registration.
630: updatedStringLast update timestamp.
631: backlinksStringNumber of backlinks pointing to the domain.
632: index_googleStringNumber of pages indexed in Google.
633: all_checkedBooleanIndicates whether all domain checks are completed.
634: sections array
635: ParameterTypeDescription
636: uidStringSection identifier.
637: nameStringSection name.
638: propsObjectSection checks and results.
639: Object where each key is a check identifier and the value is a check result object (see structure below).
640: Each props object has the following structure:
641: ParameterTypeDescription
642: codeStringUnique check identifier.
643: statusStringCheck result. Possible values: error, warning, notice, passed.
644: nameStringCheck name.
645: valueIntegerNumber of affected pages.
646: Response example
647: Copy
648: {
649: "total_pages": 1009,
650: "total_warnings": 979,
651: "total_errors": 346,
652: "total_passed": 77,
653: "total_notices": 3915,
654: "is_finished": true,
655: "domain_props": {
656: "dt": 44,
657: "domain": "www.vitality.co.uk",
658: "domains": "3401",
659: "expdate": "2025-08-30",
660: "updated": "2025-07-29 12:07:28",
661: "backlinks": "212249",
662: "index_bing": 15500,
663: "all_checked": true,
664: "index_yahoo": 15500,

721: If successful, the server returns the 200 HTTP status code with an empty response body. Returns HTTP 404 if the audit is not found (for more information, see Error handling).

1183: Get found links
1184: GET https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/found-links
1185: Returns every hyperlink found across the site. Supports filter chains for advanced queries (e.g., all nofollow external links returning 4xx).
1186: Request parameters
1187: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
1188: audit_idIntegerYesUnique audit ID (path parameter).
1189: page_typeObjectNoFields to change. See Audit settings object.
1190: limitIntegerNoNumber of links to return.
1191: offsetIntegerNoStarting position for pagination.
1192: filterArrayNoFilter chain. Each entry is { param, value, type? }. See below.
1193: filter object
1194: To build complex queries, add an array of filter parameters to the URL query string. This allows you to chain multiple conditions together using logical operators. Each filter consists of three parts, formatted with an index in brackets (e.g., filter[0], filter[1]).
1195: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
1196: paramStringYesLink field to filter by. Possible values: status, type, source_noindex, nofollow, anchor_type.
1197: valueStringYesValue to match.
1198: typeStringNoLogical operator used to combine conditions. Possible values: and, or. Required starting from the second filter condition.
1199: Example 1: OR Logic
1200: To find all internal links that have a status code of either 301 OR 302:
1201: Copy
1202: curl --location 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/issue-pages?audit_id=123&page_type=internal&limit=10&filter[0][param]=status&filter[0][value]=301&filter[1][param]=status&filter[1][value]=302&filter[1][type]=or' \
1203: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY'
1204: filter[0] sets the base condition (status = 301).
1205: filter[1][type]=or explicitly connects the next condition (status = 302) with an OR.
1206: Example 2: AND Logic
1207: To find all broken (404) image links (anchor_type = image).
1208: Copy
1209: curl --location 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/issue-pages?audit_id=123&page_type=internal&limit=10&filter[0][param]=status&filter[0][value]=404&filter[1][param]=anchor_type&filter[1][value]=image&filter[1][type]=and' \
1210: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY'
1211: filter[0] sets the base condition (status = 404).
1212: filter[1][type]=and must be included to connect the second condition (anchor_type = image) with an AND. Omitting it would result in an error.
1213: Request example
1214: Example without filters:
1215: Copy
1216: curl --location 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/issue-pages?audit_id=123&page_type=all&limit=4&offset=0' \
1217: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY'
1218: Example with filters:
1219: Copy
1220: curl --location 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/issue-pages?audit_id=123&page_type=internal&limit=10&filter[0][param]=status&filter[0][value]=404&filter[1][param]=anchor_type&filter[1][value]=image&filter[1][type]=and' \
1221: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY'
1222: Response parameters
1223: If successful, the server returns the 200 HTTP status code and an object containing the total number of matching links and a list of link objects. Returns HTTP 404 if the audit is not found (for more information, see Error handling).
1224: ParameterTypeDescription
1225: totalIntegerTotal number of links matching the request criteria.
1226: itemsArrayArray of link objects.
1227: Each object in the items array has the following structure:
1228: ParameterTypeDescription
1229: urlStringDestination URL.
1230: idStringUnique link identifier.
1231: statusStringHTTP status code of the destination URL.
1232: typeStringLink type (for example, hyperlink or canonical).
1233: source_urlStringURL of the page where the link was found.
1234: source_noindexStringIndicates whether the source page has a noindex directive (1 –yes, 0 – no).
1235: nofollowStringIndicates whether the link has a nofollow attribute (1 –yes, 0 – no).
1236: anchorStringVisible anchor text of the link.
1237: anchor_typeStringAnchor type (for example, text or image).
1238: altStringAlt attribute of the link, if available.
1239: titleStringTitle attribute of the link, if available.

1299: Get audit history
1300: GET https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/history
1301: Retrieves historical data for a specific audit run, including audit settings, domain metrics, and issue summaries.
1302: Request parameters
1303: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
1304: audit_idIntegerYesUnique audit ID (path parameter).
1305: dateStringYesThe specific date of the historical audit to retrieve (YYYY-MM-DD).
1306: Request example
1307: Copy
1308: curl --location 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/history?audit_id=123&date=2025-07-29' \
1309: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY'
1310: Response parameters
1311: If successful, the server returns the 200 HTTP status code and an object containing historical audit data. Returns HTTP 404 if the audit or specified date is not found (for more information, see Error handling).
1312: ParameterTypeDescription
1313: audit_timeStringDate and time when the audit was completed.
1314: domain_dataObjectDomain metrics at the time of the audit.
1315: settingsObjectAudit configuration used for this historical run.
1316: pages_dataObjectNumber of affected pages grouped by issue code.
1317: totalsObjectSummary statistics of the audit results.
1318: versionStringAudit engine version.
1319: domain_data object
1320: ParameterTypeDescription
1321: domainStringAudited domain.
1322: backlinksStringNumber of backlinks.
1323: index_googleStringNumber of pages indexed by Google.
1324: dtIntegerDomain trust score.
1325: totals object
1326: ParameterTypeDescription
1327: total_pagesIntegerTotal number of audited pages.
1328: total_warningsIntegerTotal number of warnings found.
1329: total_errorsIntegerTotal number of errors found.
1330: total_passedIntegerTotal number of passed checks.
1331: Response example
1332: Copy

1362: }
1363: List audit sitemaps
1364: GET https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/sitemaps
1365: Returns every sitemap configured as a crawl source for an audit, with per-sitemap page counts. Sitemaps are only used when settings.source_sitemap is 1. The flag auto-enables when a sitemap is added.
1366: Request parameters
1367: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
1368: audit_idIntegerYesUnique audit ID (path parameter).
1369: Request example
1370: Copy
1371: curl --location --request GET 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/sitemaps?audit_id=123' \
1372: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY'
1373: Response parameters
1374: ParameterTypeDescription
1375: itemsArraySource-pages list records.
1376: items[].idIntegerList identifier. Use in deleteAuditSourcePages.
1377: items[].nameStringUploaded filename.
1378: items[].pages_countIntegerURLs contained in the list.
1379: Response example
1380: Copy
1381: {
1382: "items": [
1383: {
1384: "id": 8421,
1385: "url": "https://example.com/sitemap.xml",
1386: "pages_count": 1820
1387: }
1388: ]
1389: }
1390: Add audit sitemap
1391: POST https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/sitemaps
1392: Registers a sitemap URL as a crawl source. Auto-sets settings.source_sitemap to 1 so the next run uses it.
1393: Request parameters
1394: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
1395: audit_idIntegerYesUnique audit ID (path parameter).
1396: urlStringYesAbsolute sitemap URL (e.g., https://example.com/sitemap.xml).
1397: Request example
1398: Copy
1399: curl --location --request POST 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/sitemaps?audit_id=123' \
1400: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY' \
1401: --data '{
1402: "url": "https://example.com/sitemap.xml"
1403: }'
1404: Response parameters
1405: ParameterTypeDescription
1406: idIntegerNew sitemap identifier.
1407: Response example
1408: Copy
1409: {
1410: "id": 8421
1411: }
1412: Delete audit source pages
1413: DELETE https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/sitemaps
1414: Removes a sitemap from an audit’s crawl sources. Does not toggle settings.source_sitemap off. Use updateAuditSettings if you want to disable sitemap crawling entirely.
1415: Request parameters
1416: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
1417: audit_idIntegerYesUnique audit ID (path parameter).
1418: sitemap_idIntegerYesSitemap identified from List Audit Sitemaps.
1419: Request example
1420: Copy
1421: curl --location --request DELETE 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/sitemaps?audit_id=123&sitemap_id=456' \
1422: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY'
1423: Response
1424: HTTP 204 No Content on success.
1425: List audit source pages
1426: GET https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/source-pages
1427: Returns every uploaded custom page list used as a crawl source. Source-pages lists are only used when settings.source_file is 1. The flag auto-enables when a list is added.
1428: Request parameters
1429: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
1430: audit_idIntegerYesUnique audit ID (path parameter).
1431: Request example
1432: Copy
1433: curl --location --request GET 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/source-pages?audit_id=123' \
1434: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY'
1435: Response parameters
1436: ParameterTypeDescription
1437: itemsArraySource-pages list records.
1438: items[].idIntegerList identifier. Use in deleteAuditSourcePages.
1439: items[].nameStringUploaded filename.
1440: items[].pages_countIntegerURLs contained in the list.
1441: Response example
1442: Copy
1443: {
1444: "items": [
1445: {
1446: "id": 1732,
1447: "name": "priority-pages.txt",
1448: "pages_count": 240
1449: }
1450: ]
1451: }
1452: Add audit source pages
1453: POST https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/source-pages
1454: Uploads a custom list of URLs to crawl. The list is submitted as a multipart text file with one URL per line. Auto-sets settings.source_file to 1.
1455: Request parameters
1456: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
1457: audit_idIntegerYesUnique audit ID (path parameter).
1458: fileStringYesUTF-8 text file with one URL per line.
1459: Request example
1460: Copy
1461: curl --location --request POST 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/source-pages?audit_id=123' \
1462: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY' \
1463: -F "[email protected]"
1464: Response parameters
1465: ParameterTypeDescription
1466: idIntegerNew source-pages list identifier.
1467: Response example
1468: Copy
1469: {
1470: "id": 1732
1471: }
1472: Delete audit source pages
1473: DELETE https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/source-pages
1474: Removes an uploaded custom page list. Does not toggle settings.source_file off. Use updateAuditSettings to disable custom-list crawling entirely.
1475: Request parameters
1476: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
1477: audit_idIntegerYesUnique audit ID (path parameter).
1478: list_idStringYesList identifier from List Audit Source Pages.
1479: Request example
1480: Copy
1481: curl --location --request DELETE 'https://api.seranking.com/v1/project-management/audits/source-pages?audit_id=123&list_id=789' \
1482: --header 'Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY'
1483: Response
1484: HTTP 204 No Content on success.
1485: Audit settings object
1486: Used by createAudit, updateAuditSettings, getAuditSettings, and getAuditHistory. Every field is optional. Send only the fields to change; other values stay untouched (exceptions are called out below).
1487: Crawl sources
1488: ParameterTypeDescription
1489: source_siteIntegerScan pages by following internal links from the homepage (1 – yes, 0 – no). If 0, scans only from the sitemap or a provided list. Defaults to 1.
1490: source_sitemapIntegerScan pages from the sitemap.xml file (1 – yes, 0 – no). Defaults to 1.
1491: source_subdomainIntegerScan subdomains (1 – yes, 0 – no). If 0, subdomain links are treated as external. Defaults to 0.
1492: source_fileIntegerScan only URLs from a custom list (1 – yes, 0 – no). Defaults to 0.
1493: Crawl behavior
1494: ParameterTypeDescription
1495: check_robotsIntegerFollow robots.txt directives (1 – yes, 0 – no). Defaults to 1.
1496: ignore_noindexIntegerIgnore pages with a noindex tag (1 – yes, 0 – no). Defaults to 0.
1497: ignore_nofollowIntegerIgnore links with a nofollow attribute (1 – yes, 0 – no). Defaults to 0.
1498: ignore_paramsIntegerIgnore URL parameters (0 – none, 1 – all, 2 – custom list). Defaults to 0.
1499: custom_paramsStringCustom URL parameters to ignore when ignore_params is set to 2. Defaults to:
1500: utm_source,utm_medium,utm_term,utm_content,utm_campaign,cid,PHPSESSID
1501: user_agentIntegerUser-Agent header to use for the crawl. Defaults to 0.
1502: Possible values:
1503: • 0 – SE Ranking bot
1504: • 1 – Googlebot
1505: • 2 – Googlebot Image
1506: • 3 – Bingbot
1507: • 4 – Yahoo! Slurp
1508: • 5 – YandexBot
1509: • 6 – BaiduSpider
1510: • 7 – Chrome on Windows
1511: • 8 – Chrome on macOS
1512: • 9 – Chrome on iOS
1513: • 10 – Firefox on Windows
1514: • 11 – Firefox on Linux
1515: • 12 – Safari on macOS
1516: • 13 – Opera on Windows
1517: csrIntegerEnable JavaScript rendering (1 – enabled, 0 – disabled). Defaults to 0.
1518: Essential for SPAs and sites with dynamically loaded content.
1519: csr_delayIntegerDelay in milliseconds before capturing the rendered page when csr is 1. Range 0–6,000.
1520: loginStringUsername for Basic HTTP Authentication. Defaults to null.
1521: passwordStringPassword for Basic HTTP Authentication. Defaults to null.
1522: Crawl limits
1523: ParameterTypeDescription
1524: max_pagesIntegerMaximum number of pages to crawl (1–300,000). Defaults to 1000.
1525: max_depthIntegerMaximum crawl depth (1–100). Defaults to 10.
1526: max_reqIntegerMaximum number of requests per second (1–500). Defaults to 500.
1527: max_redirectsIntegerMaximum number of redirects to follow (1–50). Defaults to 5.
1528: max_sizeIntegerMaximum page size in kilobytes (1–100,000). Defaults to 3000.
1529: On-page thresholds
1530: ParameterTypeDescription
1531: min_title_lenIntegerMinimum title length (1–10,000). Defaults to 20.
1532: max_title_lenIntegerMaximum title length (1–10,000). Defaults to 65.
1533: min_description_lenIntegerMinimum meta description length (1–10,000). Defaults to 1.
1534: max_description_lenIntegerMaximum meta description length (1–10,000). Defaults to 158.
1535: min_wordsIntegerMinimum word count per page (1–10,000). Defaults to 250.
1536: max_h1_lenIntegerMaximum H1 length (1–10,000). Defaults to 100.
1537: max_h2_lenIntegerMaximum H2 length (1–10,000). Defaults to 100.
1538: URL filtering
1539: Note: Multiple paths must be separated by newline.
1540: ParameterTypeDescription
1541: allowStringCrawl only URLs that start with the specified path. Defaults to null.
1542: disallowStringExclude URLs that start with the specified path. Defaults to null.
1543: disallow_extStringExternal URLs or domains to ignore when checking outbound links. Newline-separated. REPLACE operation.
1544: hideStringHide URLs and resources that start with the specified path. Defaults to null.
1545: Issue management
1546: ParameterTypeDescription
1547: disaled_issuesArrayIssue codes to disable (e.g., ["slow_loading", "speed_index"]). REPLACE operation: the array sent replaces the full list. Read the current list with getAuditSettings first. Issue codes match those in getAuditReport.
1548: Scheduling
1549: ParameterTypeDescription
1550: schedule_typeStringAudit execution frequency. Possible values: manual, week, month. Defaults to manual.
1551: schedule_dayIntegerDay of month for the scheduled audit when schedule_type is month (1-31). Defaults to 1.
1552: schedule_wdayIntegerSingle day of the week (1–7, Monday–Sunday) when schedule_type is week. Legacy; prefer schedule_wdays.
1553: schedule_wdaysArrayDays of week for the scheduled audit when schedule_type is week (array of integers 1-7). Defaults to [].
1554: schedule_hourIntegerHour of day (UTC) for the scheduled audit (0-23). Defaults to 0.
1555: schedule_repeatIntegerEnable repeated audits (1 – yes, 0 – no). Defaults to 0.
1556: schedule_repeat_intervalIntegerInterval in weeks between repeated audits (when schedule_repeat is 1). Defaults to 2.
1557: Reporting
1558: Note: Multiple emails must be comma-separated.
1559: ParameterTypeDescription
1560: send_reportIntegerSend the audit report via email (1 – yes, 0 – no). Defaults to 1.
1561: report_emailsStringEmail addresses to receive the audit report. If empty "", the report is sent to the account owner.

437: New to SE Ranking MCP? What it does, pricing and use cases
438: Start with 100K free credits → SE Ranking SEO MCP
439: New · MCP Hub
440: Explore the MCP Hub
441: Whether you’re connecting MCP for the first time or building advanced workflows, the MCP Hub brings every useful resource into one place, so you can start simple and level up at your own pace.
442: Setup Use cases Skills library Prompt library Blueprints Video guides
443: Go to MCP Hub →
444: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides a standardized interface that allows any compatible AI model to access your SE Ranking and SE Visible data simply and securely.
445: MCP server server follows the authenticated remote MCP spec, so it’s centrally hosted and managed. Connect in one click in Claude or ChatGPT, natively in Cursor and other clients, or use the mcp-remote module for clients that don’t support remote servers.
446: What you can access
447: Through the MCP server, your AI assistant can work with data from these SE Ranking and SE Visible products*:
448: Data API: keyword research, backlinks, domain analysis, SERP, and more
449: Project API: your projects, rank tracking, audits, and competitors
450: Local Marketing API: your locations, local rankings, Google Business Profile, business listings, and reviews
451: SE Visible API: your AI visibility projects, brands, topics, prompts, and sources
452: *The data available to you depends on your subscription. Not every API endpoint is available through MCP. Setup is the same for every product. Use your SE Ranking account, or an API key generated in the API Dashboard of your SE Ranking or SE Visible account.
453: Setup Instructions
454: General
455: Our MCP server supports Streamable HTTP transports. This transport uses OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration for authentication at the following address:
456: Copy
457: https://api.seranking.com/mcp
458: Jump to your client: Claude · ChatGPT · Codex · Cursor · VS Code · v0 · Windsurf · Zed · Gemini CLI · Others.
459: Sub-accounts
460: If you’re a sub-account on a shared SE Ranking workspace, the Sign in with SE Ranking button won’t connect any tools. API access lives with the master account, not with sub-accounts. Sub-account API keys are on the way; until they’re released, use the workaround below.
461: To connect a sub-account:
462: Get the API key from your account administrator.
463: In the connection dialog, choose Enter API keys manually.
464: Paste the key when prompted.
465: Claude
466: Claude (Web & Desktop)
467: Add the official SE Ranking connector and click Connect. In Claude Desktop, you can also find it under Customize → Connectors by searching for SE Ranking.
468: Claude Code
469: Two options. Pick one.
470: Option A: OAuth (recommended) — opens a browser on first connect, stores the token locally, and reuses it across sessions.
471: Copy
472: claude mcp add --transport http se-ranking https://api.seranking.com/mcp
473: Then run /mcp once you’ve opened a Claude Code session to go through the authentication flow.
474: Option B: API key — skip the OAuth flow and pass your key as headers. Right for headless environments, CI runners, shared dev boxes, or when the browser handoff is awkward.
475: Copy
476: claude mcp add --transport http se-ranking https://api.seranking.com/mcp \
477: --header "X-Api-Key: *****"
478: Grab the key from the API Dashboard in your SE Ranking or SE Visible account. Available tools depend on your subscription.
479: ChatGPT
480: Open the official SE Ranking plugin, click Install plugin, and sign in to authorize. You can also find it in ChatGPT under Plugins by searching for SE Ranking.
481: Codex
482: The setup steps for the MCP server are the same regardless of whether you use the IDE Extension or the CLI since the configuration is shared.
483: Configuration via CLI:
484: Run the following command in Terminal:
485: Copy
486: codex mcp add se-ranking --url https://api.seranking.com/mcp
487: This will automatically prompt you to log in with your SE Ranking account and connect it to your Codex.
488: Note: If this is the first time you are using an MCP in Codex you will need to enable the rmcp feature for this to work. Add the following into your ~/.codex/config.toml:
489: Copy
490: [features]
491: experimental_use_rmcp_client = true
492: Configuration through environment variables:
493: 1. Open the ~/.codex/config.toml file in your preferred editor.
494: 2. Add the following:
495: Copy
496: [features]
497: experimental_use_rmcp_client = true
498: [mcp_servers.se-ranking]
499: url = "https://api.seranking.com/mcp"
500: 3. Run codex mcp login se-ranking to move through the authentication flow.
501: Cursor
502: Add the following to .cursor/mcp.json (project) or ~/.cursor/mcp.json (global):
503: Copy
504: {
505: "mcpServers": {
506: "se-ranking": {
507: "url": "https://api.seranking.com/mcp"
508: }
509: }
510: }
511: Cursor supports Streamable HTTP and OAuth natively. An OAuth window will open on first use to authenticate with your SE Ranking account.
512: Visual Studio Code
513: Copy
514: {
515: "mcpServers": {
516: "se-ranking": {
517: "command": "npx",
518: "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://api.seranking.com/mcp"]
519: }
520: }
521: }
522: 1. Ctrl+P / Cmd+P and search for MCP: Add Server.
523: 2. Select Command (stdio).
524: 3. Enter the following configuration, and hit enter:
525: Copy
526: npx -y mcp-remote https://api.seranking.com/mcp
527: 4. Enter the name SE Ranking and hit enter.
528: 5. Activate the server using MCP: List Servers, selecting se-ranking, and selecting Start Server.
529: v0 by Vercel
530: To add the MCP to v0, you can install from the connections page.
531: Windsurf
532: 1. Ctrl+, / Cmd+, to open Windsurf settings.
533: 2. Scroll to Cascade > MCP servers.
534: 3. Select Add Server > Add custom server.
535: 4. Add the following:
536: Copy
537: {
538: "mcpServers": {
539: "se-ranking": {
540: "command": "npx",
541: "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://api.seranking.com/mcp"]
542: }
543: }
544: }
545: Zed
546: Cmd+, to open Zed settings. Add the following:
547: Copy
548: {
549: "context_servers": {
550: "se-ranking": {
551: "source": "custom",
552: "command": "npx",
553: "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://api.seranking.com/mcp"],
554: "env": {}
555: }
556: }
557: }
558: Gemini CLI
559: Add to ~/.gemini/settings.json:
560: Copy
561: {
562: "mcpServers": {
563: "se-ranking": {
564: "command": "npx",
565: "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://api.seranking.com/mcp"]
566: }
567: }
568: }
569: Save and launch Gemini CLI. Authorize when prompted.
570: Others
571: Hundreds of other tools now support MCP servers. You can configure them to use our MCP server with the following settings:
572: Command: npx
573: Arguments: -y mcp-remote https://api.seranking.com/mcp
574: Environment: None
575: FAQ
576: Why am I seeing an internal server error when trying to connect?
577: Enter the following in the Terminal to clear saved auth info: rm -rf ~/.mcp-auth then try again to connect.
578: Additionally you may need to update to a newer version of Node if required.
579: What happens when I connect?
580: A browser window opens to seranking.com where you log in with your SE Ranking account and approve access. After approval, you’re redirected back to your client and the connection is established. If the window doesn’t open automatically, check your client for a URL to paste into a browser manually.
581: How do I know the connection worked?
582: Claude.ai / Desktop: SE Ranking moves out of Not connected and its tools become available in chats.
583: Claude Code: Run /mcp and confirm se-ranking shows as connected and its tools are listed.
584: Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed: The server appears as connected in the MCP panel and tools are listed.
585: All clients: Try a prompt like “Using SE Ranking MCP, give me traffic for seranking.com in the US.” If it returns real data, it works.
586: I’m using WSL on Windows, and seeing an error
587: WSL can have issues with the OAuth redirect. Configure the server in your client’s Windows-side config file instead, or run the setup from PowerShell:
588: {
589: "mcpServers": {
590: "se-ranking": {
591: "command": "npx",
592: "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://api.seranking.com/mcp"]
593: }
594: }
595: }
596: Does the MCP support Streamable HTTP?
597: Yes, at the https://api.seranking.com/mcp endpoint.
598: Can I authenticate with my own API key?
599: Yes. Instead of using the interactive authentication flow, you can pass your API key in the X-Api-Key header. See Claude Code, Option B for an example. This works well for headless environments, CI runners, and shared dev boxes.
600: A key passed this way has the same access as your account. Restricted or read-only API keys aren’t available yet.
601: No tools appearing after connecting?
602: Verify your SE Ranking or SE Visible account has API access at the API Dashboard.
603: Run /mcp in Claude Code to check live connection status.
604: Try removing and re-adding the server.
605: If you need further assistance, contact us at [email protected].

1: # Introduction
2: With Ahrefs API, you can use data from your Ahrefs workspace to create custom integrations and automations. Currently, API v3 allows you to pull data from the Site Explorer, Keywords Explorer, SERP Overview, Rank Tracker, Site Audit, Brand Radar, Social Media Management and Content Helper endpoints, as well as manage your Rank Tracker projects and Keywords Explorer lists:
3: - **Site Explorer**: Overview stats and historical charts, Backlinks, Organic and paid traffic reports
4: - **Keywords Explorer**: Metrics for a single keyword or a list of keywords, Search volume history and volume by country, Keyword ideas reports
5: - **Site Audit**: Projects' Health Scores, full issue reports and content of crawled pages
6: - **SERP Overview**: Top 100 SERP results
7: - **Rank Tracker**: Project overview, Competitor reports and Rank Tracker SERPs
8: - **Batch Analysis**: Metrics for up to 100 targets per request
9: - **Brand Radar**: Brand overview stats, historical performance charts, and real prompts with citations across multiple AI agents
10: - **Social Media Management**: Channels, posts, activity history and metrics for connected social media accounts
11: - **Content Helper**: The core topics covered by the pages ranking for a keyword, with per-page coverage scores
12: - **Management**: Endpoints to manage your Rank Tracker projects and Keywords Explorer lists
13: - **Subscription information**: Your API limits and usage
14: - **Public endpoints**: Our crawler's IP addresses and ranges
15: ## Eligibility
16: Ahrefs API is available on [eligible paid plans](https://ahrefs.com/pricing). On all other plans, you'll still have access to a [limited set of free test queries](./free-test-queries.md).
17: ## Plan limits
18: All requests besides [free test queries](./free-test-queries.md) and the *Rank Tracker*, *Management*, *Public* and *some other* endpoints consume **API units**. The cost depends on the number of rows in a response and the fields requested. The minimum cost for any request is **50 units**. If an endpoint is free, you'll see a note about that on its documentation page; otherwise, it consumes units.
19: Related guide: [Limits consumption](./limits-consumption.md)
20: > **INFO**
21: > Please be advised that API units once consumed are non-refundable. We strongly encourage the use of our [complimentary test queries](./free-test-queries.md) for all development and testing purposes to mitigate any unintended usage of API units.
22: >
23: > We also recommend [putting limits](./api-keys-creation-and-management.md) on your API keys, especially when you are in the testing and development stage.
24: [Eligible paid plans](https://ahrefs.com/pricing) include a monthly API unit allowance. On plans that support pay-as-you-go usage, additional units are automatically charged once the included limit is exceeded.
25: See also: [Pricing page](https://ahrefs.com/pricing) and [Account settings / Limits & usage](https://app.ahrefs.com/account/limits-and-usage/web).
26: ![Limits and Usage](../images/limits-and-usage.png)
27: ## API keys
28: To send requests to Ahrefs API, you'll need an API key. Only workspace owners and admins can create and manage API keys. This can be done in [Account settings / API keys](https://app.ahrefs.com/account/api-keys).
29: Related guide: [API keys creation and management](./api-keys-creation-and-management.md)
30: ## Basic usage
31: Get a quick start with these API buttons in [Ahrefs reports](https://app.ahrefs.com/).
32: Click on them to display the request as a cURL command.
33: ![API button](../images/Xnip2023-04-20_11-49-41.jpg)
34: These buttons can be used as a query builder since the cURL command will be updated dynamically with any filters you apply to the report.
35: Note that cURL contains all the fields and metrics shown in the current report. You can remove the fields you don't need to reduce the cost of a request.
36: For full usage details, view our API reference in these docs. The reference contains an OpenAPI-compatible specification of each endpoint's request and response format.
37: ## Rate limiting
38: Ahrefs API is limited to 60 requests per minute by default. If this limit is exceeded, the API will respond with an HTTP 429 status code (`Too Many Requests`).
39: Additionally, to maintain optimal performance and system stability, API requests may occasionally be rejected with the same HTTP 429 status code due to throttling. Throttling occurs dynamically based on real-time system load, resource availability, and the computational demands of your requests.
40: ## Links
41: - [Full OpenAPI spec](https://docs.ahrefs.com/openapi.json)
42: - [Privacy policy](https://ahrefs.com/privacy-policy)
43: - [Terms of use](https://ahrefs.com/terms)

1: # Free test queries
2: Users on any paid plan can test Ahrefs API by running a limited set of free test queries. Note that you still need to [create an API key](./api-keys-creation-and-management.md) to run free test queries.
3: ## Site Explorer
4: For Site Explorer endpoints, requests will not consume API units if you use the `ahrefs.com`, `yep.com` or `firehose.com` domains, or any URL from these domains, in the `target` query parameter.
5: For example, these requests will be free:
6: ```json
7: https://api.ahrefs.com/v3/site-explorer/domain-rating?date=2023-05-18&target=firehose.com
8: https://api.ahrefs.com/v3/site-explorer/all-backlinks?limit=3&mode=prefix&target=ahrefs.com/blog&select=url_from,url_rating_source,traffic,url_to
9: ```
10: ## Keywords Explorer and SERP Overview
11: For Keywords Explorer and SERP Overview endpoints, requests will not consume API units if you use only `ahrefs`, `yep` or `firehose` in the `keywords` or `keyword` query parameter, depending on the endpoint.
12: For example, these requests will be free:
13: ```json
14: https://api.ahrefs.com/v3/keywords-explorer/overview?country=us&keywords=ahrefs&select=keyword,volume,traffic_potential,difficulty
15: https://api.ahrefs.com/v3/serp-overview/serp-overview?country=us&date=2023-05-16&keyword=yep&select=url,position,url_rating,backlinks,traffic&top_positions=3
16: ```
17: Note that if you include other keywords along with `ahrefs`, `yep` or `firehose` in the query, that request will consume the usual number of API units. Also, if the `keyword_list_id` parameter is specified in the query, that query will also consume API units regardless of which keywords are included in the list or in the `keywords` query parameter.
18: For example, these requests will consume the usual amount of API units:
19: ```json
20: https://api.ahrefs.com/v3/keywords-explorer/overview?country=us&keywords=ahrefs,seo&select=keyword,volume,traffic_potential,difficulty
21: https://api.ahrefs.com/v3/keywords-explorer/overview?country=us&keywords=ahrefs&keywords_list_id=123&select=keyword,volume,traffic_potential,difficulty
22: ```
23: > **INFO**
24: > The `limit` parameter is capped at 100 in free test requests. Even if you request more, the response will contain 100 results max.

1: # API keys creation and management
2: You'll need an API key to send requests via Ahrefs API v3. Provide it in the Authorization header when making requests: `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`.
3: ## Creating API keys
4: Create and manage existing API keys in [Account settings / API keys](https://app.ahrefs.com/account/api-keys). Note that only workspace owners and admins have access to this section.
5: You can create up to 1,000 API keys. When creating or editing a key, choose an expiration date between today and 10 years from today. After that date, the key becomes inactive. You can see the expiration date for each key and who created it on this page.
6: A key will also be invalidated if the user who created it is removed from the workspace.
7: ![](<../images/API keys1.png>)
8: ## Controlling usage
9: To control the monthly usage of API units in your workspace, limit the usage of particular API keys in [Account settings / API keys](https://app.ahrefs.com/account/api-keys).
10: ![](<../images/API keys2.png>)
11: If your subscription plan allows pay-as-you-go charges, you can also limit the maximum number of API units that can be added on a pay-as-you-go basis or disable pay-as-you-go API units altogether in [Account settings / Limits & usage](https://app.ahrefs.com/account/limits-and-usage/web).
12: ![Limits & usage](<../images/Limits & usage 2.png>)

1: # Limits consumption
2: Ahrefs API is available on [eligible paid plans](https://ahrefs.com/pricing). On all other plans, you'll still have access to a [limited set of free test queries](./free-test-queries.md).
3: All requests besides [free test queries](./free-test-queries.md) and the *Rank Tracker*, *Management*, *Public* and *some other* endpoints consume **API units**. If an endpoint is free, you'll see a note about that on its documentation page; otherwise, it consumes units.
4: The units consumption per request is calculated as follows:
5: ```
6: max(base_cost, per_row_cost * num_rows)
7: ```
8: The `base_cost` of each request is **50 units**. The `per_row_cost` is the sum of the costs of each unique field that appears in either the returned result, or in the `where` or `order_by` parameters. If a field appears in multiple parameters, it is counted once.
9: The default cost of a field is **1 unit**. However, certain metrics are more expensive and may consume **5** or **10 units**. Such exceptions are noted in the each endpoint's field description. Requests served from cache do not consume units.
10: Each API request indicates its units consumption behavior via the following response headers:
11: - `x-api-rows` The number of rows returned.
12: - `x-api-units-cost-row` The per-row units cost.
13: - `x-api-units-cost-total` The overall units that the request should consume based on the number of rows and per-row cost.
14: - `x-api-units-cost-total-actual` The overall units that the request actually consumed.
15: - `x-api-cache` Whether the request was served from cache. One of: `hit` `miss` `no_cache`
16: > **INFO**
17: > A good way to estimate the cost of a request is to run it with a [free target](./free-test-queries.md) and check the `x-api-units-cost-total` field value. To display the response headers when using the `curl` command, you can use the `-v` or `--verbose` option.
18: ## Example 1
19: Consider a request to the *Site Explorer - Domain rating* endpoint (`/site-explorer/domain-rating`).
20: It does not accept a `select`, `where`, or `order_by` parameter, and it returns a single row containing two fields - `domain_rating` and `ahrefs_rank`, for a per-row cost of 2 units.
21: The total row cost (per-row cost multiplied by the number of rows) is less than the base cost. Therefore, this request costs the base amount of **50 units**.
22: ## Example 2
23: Consider a more complex request to the *Site Explorer - Backlinks* endpoint (`/site-explorer/all-backlinks`), which allows the configuration of the `select`, `where`, and `order_by` parameters.
24: Suppose this request has two fields selected:
25: ```
26: select=title,traffic
27: ```
28: two fields in the filter expression:
29: ```
30: where={"and":[{"field":"traffic","is":["gt",1000]},{"field":"refdomains_source","is":["gt",10]}]}
31: ```
32: and an ordering field:
33: ```
34: order_by=traffic:desc
35: ```
36: Across these parameters, there are three unique fields, of which `title` and `refdomains_source` cost 1 unit each, while `traffic` costs 10 units. Thus, the per-row cost is 1 + 1 + 10 = 12 units.
37: Suppose the request returns 500 rows. Then, the total row cost (12 * 500 = 6000 units) exceeds the base cost. Therefore, the cost of this request is **6000 units**.

1: # What is Ahrefs MCP
2: **Ahrefs MCP** lets AI agents securely access the Ahrefs API and enrich their answers with real Ahrefs data.
3: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard that allows AI tools to connect with third-party APIs in a secure, consistent way. In our case, it connects AI tools with Ahrefs, enabling things like this:
4: ![](../images/mcp1-2.jpg)
5: ## Connect to Ahrefs MCP
6: Ahrefs provides a hosted MCP server that allows users with a Lite plan or higher to connect their Ahrefs account to supported AI tools. Once connected, your setup is synced and available across all devices linked to your personal or company account.
7: > **INFO**
8: > See our [Ahrefs MCP use cases and prompt ideas](https://ahrefs.com/blog/mcp-use-cases/) for real examples and prompting tips to help you get the most from your MCP connection.
9: ### Connection URL
10: - **Streamable HTTP**: `https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcp`
11: Most popular AI tools support connecting to the remote MCP directly. If you run into issues, check out our step-by-step setup guides:
12: - [Claude Web / Desktop](./claude-desktop-web.md)
13: - [Claude Mobile](./claude-mobile.md)
14: - [Claude Code](./claude-code.md)
15: - [Copilot Studio](./copilot-studio.md)
16: - [ChatGPT Web](./chatgpt-web.md)
17: - [Lovable](./lovable.md)
18: - [n8n](./n8n.md)
19: - [Manus](./manus.md)
20: - [Mistral's Le Chat](./mistral-le-chat.md)
21: - [OpenClaw](./openclaw.md)
22: ## API limits and usage
23: The remote MCP server is available on **paid plans starting from Lite.**
24: - Each plan has a **maximum number of rows per request** that an AI agent can access.
25: - Each plan also comes with a **limited amount of monthly API units.** The higher your plan tier, the more units are included. Enterprise customers can purchase additional unit add-ons if needed.
26: - When a third-party app makes an API call on your behalf, it consumes **API units** from your monthly allowance — the [same way as direct API usage](https://docs.ahrefs.com/docs/api/reference/limits-consumption).
27: You can track your current usage in **Account settings → [Limits and usage](https://app.ahrefs.com/account/limits-and-usage/web).**
28: ![](../images/mcp2.jpg)
29: See the [Ahrefs pricing page](https://ahrefs.com/pricing) for details on plan limits.
30: ## Keys and authorization
31: When you connect Ahrefs MCP to an AI agent:
32: - You’ll see an **authorization consent screen.**
33: - Once approved, the connection will appear in your account with a dedicated **API key** (tagged with `MCP` scope).
34: - New keys created through OAuth for MCP or Ahrefs Connect default to a monthly limit of 200,000 API units per key.
35: - Workspace admins can change or remove this limit in the [API keys report](https://app.ahrefs.com/account/api-keys).
36: Manually created keys have no per-key limit by default. Workspace plan limits still apply to all keys.
37: You can also:
38: - **Manually generate an MCP key** in your account and use it in your AI agent’s configuration.
39: - Enterprise customers may also connect with their **API keys.**
40: ![](../images/mcp3-2.jpg)
41: For details on how API units are calculated per call, see [API pricing and unit consumption guide](https://docs.ahrefs.com/docs/api/reference/limits-consumption).
42: ## Terms of use
43: {/* Legal terms live in a snippet so they are never AI-translated, see ../snippets/terms-of-use.mdx */}
44: <TermsOfUse />
45: Using the external MCP endpoint via custom scripts, bridges, or standalone HTTP/JSON-RPC clients is **unsupported and not permitted.** The external MCP server is not a general-purpose programmatic API.
46: For supported programmatic access to Ahrefs data, please use the [Ahrefs public API](https://docs.ahrefs.com/docs/api/reference/introduction).

1: # Tool Categories
2: Some MCP clients limit the amount of tools that an MCP server is allowed to advertise. Ahrefs' MCP server goes above this limit for many of them.
3: We provide a way to make sure that the MCP client doesn't remove access to tools that you need.
4: When connecting to the MCP server, you can use a URL query parameter `tools` to choose which groups you'd like to have access to. Separate multiple groups with a comma:
5: ```
6: https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcp?tools=site-explorer-overview,brand-radar-entities
7: ```
8: If you omit the `tools` parameter, **all** tools are advertised.
9: > **INFO**
10: > Documentation and rendering helper tools are always included, regardless of which groups you select.
11: ## Available tool groups
12: | Group | Description |
13: | --- | --- |
14: | `site-explorer-overview` | Core Site Explorer metrics — domain rating, backlink and outlink stats, organic/paid overview, metrics history. |
15: | `site-explorer-reports` | Detailed Site Explorer reports — backlinks, referring domains, anchors, organic keywords and competitors, top pages, linked domains. |
16: | `keywords-explorer` | Keyword research — overview, volume by country and history, matching/related terms, search suggestions. |
17: | `serp-overview` | SERP overview for a keyword. |
18: | `rank-tracker` | Rank Tracker — overview and competitor reports. |
19: | `site-audit` | Site Audit — projects, issues, page explorer, page content. |
20: | `brand-radar-simple` | Brand Radar reports (domain/URL level). |
21: | `brand-radar-entities` | Brand Radar reports (entity level). |
22: | `web-analytics-overview` | Web Analytics stats and charts. |
23: | `web-analytics-sources` | Web Analytics traffic sources, source channels, and referrers. |
24: | `web-analytics-geo` | Web Analytics geographic breakdowns — continents, countries, cities. |
25: | `web-analytics-user-agents` | Web Analytics device, browser, operating system, and language breakdowns. |
26: | `web-analytics-pages` | Web Analytics top pages, entry pages, and exit pages. |
27: | `gsc` | Google Search Console — keywords, pages, positions, and performance history. |
28: | `social-media` | Social media — channels, posts, authors, and their metrics. |
29: | `content-helper` | Content Helper — the core topics the pages ranking for a keyword cover. |
30: | `batch-analysis` | Batch analysis of multiple targets in a single request. |
31: | `management` | Account management — projects, keyword lists, locations, and Brand Radar configuration. |
32: | `public` | Public/free endpoints — crawler IP ranges and free domain rating. |
33: | `subscription-info` | Your subscription limits and usage. |
34: ## Essentials
35: If your client caps how many tools it accepts, use `tools=essentials` for a curated set of the most commonly used tools across all groups:
36: ```
37: https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcp?tools=essentials
38: ```
39: > **INFO**
40: > `essentials` is a standalone value, it can't be combined with other groups. `tools=essentials,site-audit` is rejected; request either `essentials` on its own, or a comma-separated list of the groups above.
41: > **INFO**
42: > If you request a group name that doesn't exist, the connection is rejected with an `invalid tool category` error. Double-check the spelling against the table above.
43: ## Search and exec
44: Add `tools=search-exec` to the MCP URL to advertise `search`, `doc`, `exec`, and the three rendering tools:
45: ```
46: https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcp?tools=search-exec
47: ```
48: In this mode:
49: - `search` finds operations from a few keywords describing the task, such as `backlinks referring domains`. Matching covers names, descriptions and parameter names. Every word is optional, words in the operation name count most, and an exact operation name ranks first. Omit `query` to browse the catalog, and set `category` to one of the groups above (or `render`) to narrow it. Each result carries `name`, `category`, `description`, `read_only` and `destructive`, without schemas.
50: - `doc` returns the input and output schemas for a selected operation.
51: - `exec` runs an operation with its exact name and JSON arguments.

1: # Ahrefs API
2: > Ahrefs API v3 gives programmatic access to Ahrefs' SEO, marketing, and AI-search data — backlinks, organic and paid traffic, keywords, SERPs, rank tracking, site audits, brand/AI-search visibility, web and social analytics, and account management.
3: The Ahrefs API is organized into **tools**, each a self-contained group of REST endpoints. The complete OpenAPI specification for every tool is at [/openapi.json](/openapi.json). Each tool also has its own spec — a machine-readable index of them is at [/reference/index.json](/reference/index.json).
4: ## Basics
5: - **Base URL:** `https://api.ahrefs.com/v3/{tool}/{endpoint}` (for example `https://api.ahrefs.com/v3/site-explorer/domain-rating`).
6: - **Authentication:** send your API key as a bearer token in the `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` header. Free "public" endpoints do not require a key. See [API keys creation and management](/api/docs/api-keys-creation-and-management.md).
7: - **Requests:** all data endpoints are `GET` with query-string parameters.
8: - **Responses:** JSON by default (`application/json`); most endpoints also support XML. Use the `output` parameter to choose the format.
9: - **Selecting fields:** most reports take a `select` parameter listing the columns to return; response cost depends on the rows and fields requested. See [Parameters](/api/docs/parameters.md).
10: - **Filtering:** rows can be filtered with a JSON filter expression via the `where` parameter. See [Filter syntax](/api/docs/filter-syntax.md).
11: ## Units and limits
12: Most requests consume **API units**; the minimum cost of any billable request is 50 units. Rank Tracker, Management, Public, and some other endpoints are free, and each tool's documentation marks free endpoints. During development, prefer the [free test queries](/api/docs/free-test-queries.md) to avoid spending units. See [Limits consumption](/api/docs/limits-consumption.md).
13: ## Monetary values
14: Monetary values across all endpoints (for example `value`, `org_cost`, `paid_cost`, `traffic_value`) are returned in **USD cents**. Divide by 100 to display dollars.
15: ## OpenAPI specification
16: - [Ahrefs API (complete OpenAPI spec)](https://docs.ahrefs.com/openapi.json): Every endpoint for every tool in one document
17: ## Per-tool OpenAPI specifications
18: - [Site Explorer](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/site-explorer.json): Fetch data from Site Explorer reports
19: - [Competitive Analysis](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/competitive-analysis.json): Fetch data from Competitive Analysis reports
20: - [Keywords Explorer](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/keywords-explorer.json): Fetch data from Keywords Explorer reports
21: - [Site Audit](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/site-audit.json): Site audit.
22: - [Rank Tracker](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/rank-tracker.json): Rank tracker.
23: - [SERP Overview](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/serp-overview.json): Fetch data from SERP Overview report
24: - [Batch Analysis](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/batch-analysis.json): Batch analysis.
25: - [Subscription Information](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/subscription-info.json): Subscription information.
26: - [Management](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/management.json): Project management.
27: - [Brand Radar](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/brand-radar.json): Brand radar.
28: - [Content Helper](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/content-helper.json): Fetch data from Content Helper reports
29: - [Web Analytics](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/web-analytics.json): Web_analytics.
30: - [GSC Insights](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/gsc.json): Fetch data from GSC Insights reports
31: - [Social Media](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/social-media.json): Social Media Management.
32: - [Public](https://docs.ahrefs.com/reference/public.json): Free endpoints that don't require an Ahrefs subscription, or require a free/public APIv3 key

Visits without such a referrer are left out. \ntype: string\n\n**referring_host**: The host of the page the visitor came from, without `www.`. \ntype: string\n\n**search_term**: The search term the visit came from. Case-insensitive; `phrase_match` matches whole words. Visits with an unknown search term are left out. \ntype: string\n\n**utm_source**: The UTM source of the visit. \ntype: string\n\n**utm_medium**: The UTM medium of the visit. \ntype: string\n\n**utm_campaign**: The UTM campaign of the visit. \ntype: string\n\n**utm_term**: The UTM term of the visit. \ntype: string\n\n**utm_content**: The UTM content of the visit. \ntype: string\n\n**landing_page**: The URL of the page the visit started on, as `traffic-landing-pages` lists it. \ntype: string\n\n**city**: The visitor's city, as `City, CC` with the country code, as `traffic-geography` lists it with `level=city`. \ntype: string\n\n**region**: The visitor's world region, as `traffic-geography` lists it with `level=region`. \ntype: string\n\n**continent**: The visitor's continent, as `traffic-geography` lists it with `level=continent`. \ntype: string\n\n**previous_page**: The page the visitor was on right before the visit, as `traffic-previous-pages` lists it. \ntype: string\n\n**referring_page**: The URL of the page the visitor came from, as `traffic-referring-pages` lists it. \ntype: string\n\nOf the filter grammar below, the report accepts this subset. 402: Questions? We have answers
403: Do you offer discounts or free trials?
404: We never run discounts. But if you're a website owner, you can sign up for Ahrefs Free to get free limited access to Site Explorer & Site Audit.
405: What payment methods do you offer?
406: We accept Visa, Mastercard, American Express and UnionPay. For Enterprise plans, we also support wire transfers on request.
407: Are there any automatic charges?
408: Yes. If not prepaid for, additional users are automatically charged on a pay-as-you-go basis. Also, if you enable additional pay-as-you-go credits and data, you’ll be automatically charged when consumption exceeds your plan’s limits.
409: Are there any contracts or setup fees?
410: There are no contracts or setup fees. You can switch your plan or cancel your Ahrefs subscription at any time.
411: How can I switch my plan?
412: Upgrade or downgrade your account anytime from your Account Settings. Upgrades take effect immediately, while downgrades and cancellations become effective at the end of your current billing period.
413: Can I purchase only one tool?
414: Yes, Brand Radar is available as a standalone tool. When you purchase it, you’ll also receive an Ahrefs Free account.
415: How can I cancel my plan?
416: Cancel your plan anytime from your Account Settings. When you cancel, you’ll still be able to use your plan until the end of your subscription period. After your paid subscription ends, you’ll be switched to a free Ahrefs Free plan with free limited access to Site Explorer & Site Audit.
417: How can I switch to annual billing?
418: Please contact our support team at [email protected].
419: How do you charge for additional data and credits?
420: Once you enable additional pay-as-you-go credits and data, you’ll be automatically charged when consumption exceeds your plan’s limits. If you’re on an annual plan, you can choose to prepay at a discounted rate.
421: Is unused additional data carried over to the next month?
422: Yes. PAYG purchases such as report credits, export rows, crawl credits, and API units, last for three billing months, including the current one. 1: # OAuth guide
2: All API calls require authorization and are made **on behalf of an authorized Ahrefs user**. To do this, your app must obtain an API **access token** for that user.
3: Ahrefs Connect uses **OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)**. The process has two main steps:
4: ## 1. Authorize the application
5: Redirect the user to:
6: ```html
7: https://app.ahrefs.com/web/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id={client_id}&scope=apiv3-integration-apps&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}&code_challenge={code_challenge}&code_challenge_method=s256&state={state}
8: ```
9: **Parameters:**
10: - `{client_id}` : URL-encoded Client ID from **Ahrefs Connect** section in your [Account settings](https://app.ahrefs.com/account/my-account).
11: - `{redirect_uri}` : URL-encoded Redirect URI you’ve registered in the same section.
12: - `{code_challenge}` : Derived from a **code verifier** using the S256 method:
13: - Generate a **code verifier** — a random string of 43–128 characters using a cryptographically secure generator. Allowed characters: `[A-Z] [a-z] [0-9] - . _ ~` (see [RFC7636 Section 4.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7636#section-4.1)).
14: - Compute the **SHA-256** hash of the code verifier.
15: - Base64-URL-encode the hash.
16: - Use this encoded value as the `code_challenge` (see [RFC7636 Section 4.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7636#section-4.2)).
17: - `{state}` : Generate an opaque value to maintain state between the request and callback. The authorization server will include this value when redirecting the user back to your app. (see [RFC6749 Section 4.1.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-4.1.1))
18: ![](<../images/Account settings-2.jpg>)
19: **User experience:**
20: 1. The user sees the Ahrefs authorization consent screen.
21: 2. They grant your app permission to access Ahrefs API on their behalf.
22: 3. Ahrefs redirects them to your **Redirect URI** with:
23: - `code` parameter — used in Step 2
24: - `state` parameter — verify it matches your original request.
25: ## **2. Retrieve the `access_token`**
26: Exchange the `code` for an `access_token` by sending a `POST` request to `https://ahrefs.com/oauth/token` .
27: **Send the parameters** in the request body using the `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` format (see [RFC6749 Section 4.1.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-4.1.3)):
28: - `grant_type`: `authorization_code`
29: - `client_id`: `{client_id}` (Must match the one in Step 1)
30: - `redirect_uri`: `{redirect_uri}` (Must match the one in Step 1)
31: - `code`: `{code}` (From Step 1)
32: - `code_verifier`: `{original_code_verifier}` (The untransformed value from Step 1)
33: - `client_secret`: `{client_secret}` (**Web apps only** — found in your **Ahrefs Connect** section in **Account settings**. Omit for desktop apps.)
34: **Example response:**
35: ```json
36: {
37: "access_token": "\<token to use in API requests>",
38: "expires_in": \<lifetime of the access token in seconds>,
39: "token_type": "Bearer",
40: "scope": "apiv3-integration-apps"
41: }
42: ```
43: **Token lifetime & re-connection**
44: - **No refresh tokens are issued.**
45: - Access tokens are valid for **1 year**. After expiry, the user must **reconnect (re-authorize)** via OAuth.
46: > **INFO**
47: > **Security note:**
48: > - **Never** expose `access_token` to end users, either during authorization or later (in UI, logs, URLs, or client-side code).
49: > - For **web apps**, store `client_secret` **server-side only**.
50: > - You will need to demonstrate secure token handling as part of the [Approval process](./approval-process.md).

7: - [Authentication](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/authentication): Learn how to authenticate requests to the MrScraper API using API tokens and request headers.

12: - [Get Screenshot](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/scraper-api/get-screenshot): Capture full-page or viewport screenshots of dynamic, JavaScript-rendered pages with the Get Screenshot endpoint, with real browser rendering enabled by default.
13: - [Listing Page](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/scraper-api/listing-page): Extract paginated item lists, catalog grids, and search results in one run with the Listing Page endpoint, handling numbered pages, scrolling, and Load More.
14: - [Scrape JSON](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/scraper-api/scrape-json): Extract structured, strongly-typed JSON from a single page with the Scrape JSON endpoint, using a natural language prompt instead of CSS selectors or XPath.
15: - [Scrape Markdown](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/scraper-api/scrape-markdown): Convert any web page into clean, LLM-friendly Markdown with the Scrape Markdown endpoint, stripping navigation, scripts, and ads for token-efficient AI input.
16: - [Scrape Sitemap](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/scraper-api/scrape-sitemap): Crawl target sites with the Scrape Sitemap endpoint to discover endpoints, map URL architecture, and generate seed URL lists before running bulk extraction jobs.
17: - [Get Brand](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/scraper-api/scrape-brand/get-brand): Read a brand you already scraped with the Get Brand endpoint, or download its HTML, screenshots, and ZIP page bundle by job ID.
18: - [Scrape Brand](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/scraper-api/scrape-brand/scrape-brand): Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, icons, social links, and metadata with the Scrape Brand endpoint, with an optional HTML, screenshot, and ZIP page bundle.
19: - [Get Proxy Requests Bandwidth](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/v3/analytic/proxy): Retrieve total proxy bandwidth usage aggregated per proxy username within a given date range using the MrScraper API.
20: - [Get Analytic Statuses](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/v3/analytic/status): Retrieve scrape status counts for a domain within a date range using the MrScraper API, with optional action and API token name filters.

25: Authentication
26: Learn how to authenticate requests to the MrScraper API using API tokens and request headers.
27: The MrScraper API uses API token authentication to secure all endpoints. Every request must include a valid API token in the HTTP request headers.
28: Getting Your API Token
29: API tokens are managed directly from your MrScraper dashboard.
30: Sign in to your MrScraper Dashboard.
31: Click your profile icon in the top-right corner and select API Tokens (or go to app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens).
32: Click New Token.
33: Enter a descriptive token name and choose an expiration date.
34: Click Create, then copy and securely store the generated token.
35: Keep Your Token Secure
36: Your API token grants access to your account and plan resources. Never expose your token in client-side code (like browsers or mobile apps), and store it securely in an environment variable or server configuration.
37: Authenticating Requests
38: Include your API token in the x-api-token HTTP header on every request:
39: x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>
40: Marketplace Endpoints
41: For Marketplace endpoints, authenticate using the standard RFC 6750 Authorization header with a Bearer token:
42: Authorization: Bearer <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>
43: Verify Token
44: To test your authentication and confirm that your token is valid, make a request to the /subscription-accounts endpoint:
45: curl -X GET "https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/subscription-accounts" \
46: -H "accept: application/json" \
47: -H "x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>"
48: Analytics Authentication
49: Analytics endpoints authenticate using the same x-api-token header as all other API endpoints.
50: When querying analytics, you can also pass the apiTokenName query parameter to filter status data for a specific token by the name you assigned when creating it:
51: curl -X GET "https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/analytic/statuses?domain=example.com&startDate=2026-04-12%2000:00:00&endDate=2026-04-13%2023:59:59&apiTokenName=YOUR_TOKEN_NAME" \
52: -H "accept: application/json" \
53: -H "x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>"
54: Note
55: The apiTokenName query parameter filters metrics by the token's name (e.g., production-worker).

26: Token Plan
27: Token Plan
28: Learn how plan tokens and API tokens work in MrScraper, why token usage varies between runs, and how to create your own API token for authentication.
29: MrScraper uses a token-based system for both usage and authentication.
30: Plan Tokens measure how much you can use MrScraper's features, such as running or rerunning scrapers.
31: API Tokens allow you to securely access the MrScraper API, for example, to rerun an existing scraper programmatically.
32: Why Token Usage Varies
33: Token consumption isn't fixed — a few key factors affect how many tokens any given scraper uses:
34: Website Complexity: Heavy JavaScript, dynamic content, or multiple requests increase runtime and token usage.
35: Page Size and Content Density: Larger pages with long articles or extensive metadata produce more input text for AI models to process.
36: Data Volume: Extracting large datasets (e.g., paginated listings) requires more compute and bandwidth.
37: AI Processing Load: Complex instructions or large expected outputs increase input and output token usage.
38: Keep these in mind as you read the pricing tables below — they explain why two runs on the same plan can consume different amounts of tokens.
39: Understanding Plan Tokens
40: Each MrScraper billing plan includes a specific number of tokens.
41: Tokens represent the compute resources your scraper consumes — similar to how minutes or data are counted in a phone plan.
42: The number of tokens used depends on the type of scraper you run.
43: AI Scraper Token Usage
44: AI Scrapers consume more tokens due to AI processing and additional factors such as:
45: Usage TypeDescriptionConversion Rate
46: Run TrackingEach AI agent run consumes 5 tokens for trace tracking. Reruns and workflows consume 0 tokens for this component.0 or 5 tokens per run
47: RuntimeTime spent processing your task.1 token per 30 seconds of runtime
48: Input TokensAmount of text data (prompts or instructions) sent to the AI model.1 token per ~1,000 input tokens
49: Output TokensAmount of text generated by the AI model (responses or extracted results).1 token per ~200 output tokens
50: Example
51: If your AI scraper runs for 90 seconds, processes 5,000 input tokens, and generates 1,000 output tokens, your total token usage would be:
52: ComponentCalculationTokens
53: Runtime90 ÷ 303
54: Input5,000 ÷ 1,0005
55: Output1,000 ÷ 2005
56: Run TraceFixed5
57: Total18
58: Note
59: Each run automatically includes trace tracking for debugging and performance monitoring.
60: Input and output tokens are based on how much text the AI model processes and generates.
61: AI Scrapers tend to consume more tokens due to model processing.
62: Runtime tokens are rounded up using the ceiling rule. For example, if your scraper runs for 40 seconds, it will count as 2 tokens (not 1).
63: Workflow and Scrape HTML Token Usage
64: Workflows and Scrape HTML consume tokens based on two factors: runtime and bandwidth.
65: Usage TypeDescriptionConversion Rate
66: RuntimeTime your scraper runs.1 token per 30 seconds
67: BandwidthAmount of data downloaded or uploaded.1 token per 0.25 MB
68: Example
69: If your workflow or Scrape HTML request runs for 40 seconds and uses 1.1 MB of bandwidth:
70: ComponentCalculationTokens
71: Runtime40 ÷ 30 = 1.33 → rounded up2
72: Bandwidth1.1 ÷ 0.25 = 4.4 → rounded up5
73: Total7
74: Note
75: Runtime tokens are rounded up using the ceiling rule. For example, if your
76: scraper runs for 40 seconds, it will count as 2 tokens (not 1).
77: Scraper API Token Cap
78: The Scraper API token cap limits how many tokens a single scrape can use in the Scraper API. It is available in Workflow and under Retry in every Scraper API use case. For Workflow and Scrape HTML, tokens are counted with the runtime and bandwidth calculations shown in Workflow and Scrape HTML Token Usage.
79: When Retry is enabled, a failed scrape retries automatically. Two limits control how far retrying goes:
80: Max retries: The maximum number of retry attempts (3 by default).
81: Token cap: The maximum total tokens all attempts can use (Unlimited by default).
82: Retrying stops at the first of these: the scrape succeeds, it reaches Max retries, or the running token total reaches the token cap. Each attempt's token cost is rounded up (ceiling rule) and added to a running total.
83: The token cap takes effect only when Retry is enabled, since its purpose is to limit how many tokens retries can consume. If Retry is off, the scrape runs once and returns a result or an error.
84: Example
85: The scrape succeedsStops at Max retriesStops at the Token Cap
86: Max retries 3, token cap 10.
87: AttemptRuntime + BandwidthRounded-up CostRunning TotalResult
88: 1 (initial)2.4 tokens33Failed, retrying
89: 2 (retry 1)1.6 tokens25Succeeded
90: The scrape succeeds on the second attempt, using 5 tokens. Because it succeeded, the Scraper API returns the result and stops even though max retries and tokens still remain (5 of 10 tokens left, and 2 retries unused).
91: Max retries 2, token cap 20.
92: AttemptRuntime + BandwidthRounded-up CostRunning TotalResult
93: 1 (initial)3.6 tokens44Failed, retrying
94: 2 (retry 1)3.8 tokens48Failed, retrying
95: 3 (retry 2)3.4 tokens412Failed, max retries reached
96: The scrape uses both retries without succeeding, so it stops even though 8 tokens still remain under the 20-token cap.
97: Max retries 3, token cap 12, about 4 tokens per run.
98: AttemptRuntime + BandwidthRounded-up CostRunning TotalResult
99: 1 (initial)3.5 tokens44Failed, retrying
100: 2 (retry 1)3.9 tokens48Failed, retrying
101: 3 (retry 2)3.7 tokens412Failed, cap reached
102: The running total reaches the 12-token cap on the second retry, so the scrape stops before using all 3 retries.
103: First attempt exceeds the cap
104: If the first attempt costs more than the cap (for example, a cap of 10 but a first scrape that needs 15 tokens), the scrape still runs once but doesn't retry.
105: It returns either a result or an error. Set the token cap high enough to allow for retries, especially on pages with variable load times or bandwidth. If a scrape hits the cap before completing, try increasing the cap.
106: Marketplace Scraper Token Usage
107: Marketplace Scrapers use a custom token cost based on factors such as the target domain, workflow complexity, proxy usage, infrastructure requirements, and scraper configuration. Each scraper may use either a fixed token cost or a custom usage calculation depending on how the scraper is designed.
108: For the complete list of Marketplace Scraper token costs, see the Marketplace catalog.
109: Scrape JSON
110: Extract structured, strongly-typed JSON from single pages with the general agent, using natural language prompts or a JSON schema instead of selectors.
111: CLI
112: Install, authenticate, and use the MrScraper CLI to retrieve pages as HTML, Markdown, or screenshots, extract brand details and structured JSON, search the web, and check account status.
