167: --- 168: ## Pricing and Free Tier 169: Every account includes a recurring monthly free tier. **No credit card or commitment required to start.** 170: **5,000 free requests per month**, renewing on the 1st of each month. Unused requests don't roll over. For team accounts, the free tier is shared across all users in the account. 171: What's included free: 172: - Fetch any webpage and extract as Markdown 173: - Access to 60+ pre-built scrapers for popular domains 174: - Web search (Bing, Google) 175: - Browser automation 176: - Geo-targeting 177: Beyond the free tier — pay as you go, no commitment: 178: | | Search & Scrape | Browser Navigation | 179: |---|---|---| 180: | **Pay as you go** | $1.50 / 1K results | $8 / GB | 181: - When free requests run out, requests stop. No surprise charges — unless you have deposited funds 182: - Adding a credit card is a verification step only; you are not charged unless your free tier is exhausted **and** you have funds deposited 183: - Set a spend cap in the [control panel](https://brightdata.com/cp) so pay-as-you-go usage never exceeds your budget 184: [Full pricing, volume plans and enterprise →](https://brightdata.com/pricing/mcp-server) 185: --- 186: ## Use Cases 187: ### Real-time research 188: Answer questions using live web data instead of training data. Search, then read the sources. 189: | Task | Tools | 190: |------|-------| 191: | Search the web for current information | `search_engine`, `search_engine_batch` | 192: | Read a specific page as clean Markdown | `scrape_as_markdown`, `scrape_batch` | 193: Example prompts: "What's Tesla's current stock price?", "Get today's weather forecast for New York", "Find the most cited sources on EU AI regulation from the last 6 months". 194: ### E-commerce intelligence 195: Read product data as structured JSON: price, availability, rating, review count, seller, images. 196: | Task | Tools | 197: |------|-------| 198: | Products and search results from Amazon, Walmart, eBay, Etsy, Home Depot and other stores. Reviews from Walmart | `search_scrapers` → `get_scraper_details` → `run_scraper` | 199: Example prompts: "Compare this laptop's price on Amazon vs Walmart vs eBay", "Get the rating and review count for ASIN B0D2Q9397Y", "Is this product in stock?". 200: ### Market and competitor analysis 201: Build competitor profiles from live data: funding, headcount, hiring, customer reviews, pricing pages. 202: | Task | Tools | 203: |------|-------| 204: | Find companies or people by criteria (industry, country, size, funding, title) | `business_search` | 205: | Company funding, size, employees, job postings (Crunchbase, ZoomInfo, LinkedIn) | `search_scrapers` → `run_scraper` | 206: | Customer sentiment (Facebook company reviews, app store reviews) | `search_scrapers` → `run_scraper` | 207: | Competitor pricing pages | `scrape_as_markdown`, `scrape_batch` | 208: | Market discovery | `search_engine_batch` | 209: Example prompt: "Analyze Notion as a competitor: pricing, funding, hiring focus, and what customers complain about". 210: ### AI agents with reliable web access 211: Replace built-in fetch and search tools. Pages that need JavaScript or clicks go to the remote browser tools. 212: | Task | Tools | 213: |------|-------| 214: | Drop-in replacement for built-in web search | `search_engine` | 215: | Drop-in replacement for built-in URL fetch | `scrape_as_markdown` | 216: | Parallel data collection (5 at a time) | `search_engine_batch`, `scrape_batch` | 217: | Interactive sites (infinite scroll, dynamic content, forms) | `scraping_browser_*` (14 tools) | 218: ### Coding agents 219: Package registry data on demand — no scraping, no stale caches. 220: | Task | Tools | 221: |------|-------| 222: | npm and PyPI package version, README, metadata | `run_scraper` with the npmjs or pypi scraper (find them with `search_scrapers`) | 223: | Read files from GitHub repositories | `run_scraper` with the GitHub repository scraper | 224: Example prompts: "What's the latest version of express on npm?", "Get the README for the langchain-brightdata PyPI package". 225: ### GEO and brand visibility 226: Send a prompt to ChatGPT or Perplexity and get the answer text back as Markdown. Each call sends one prompt. 227: | Task | Tools | 228: |------|-------| 229: | Send a prompt to ChatGPT (web search off) and get the answer text as Markdown | `chatgpt_ai_insights` | 230: | Send a prompt to Perplexity and get the answer text as Markdown | `perplexity_ai_insights` | 231: Example prompt: "Ask ChatGPT and Perplexity 'what is the best proxy provider' and compare how each one ranks us". 232: ### Social media monitoring 233: Structured data from every major platform: profiles, posts, comments, engagement metrics. Each platform has scrapers per data type (LinkedIn profiles, Instagram reels, TikTok comments, ...); find them with `search_scrapers` and run them with `run_scraper`. 234: | Platform | Examples of scrapers | 235: |----------|----------------------| 236: | LinkedIn | person profiles, company profiles, job listings, posts, people search | 237: | Instagram | profiles, posts, reels, comments | 238: | TikTok | profiles, posts, shop, comments | 239: | Facebook | profiles, posts, marketplace listings, company reviews, events | 240: | YouTube | videos, channels, comments | 241: | X (Twitter) | posts, posts by profile | 242: | Reddit | posts, comments | 243: Example prompt: "Get the last 10 posts from this TikTok profile and summarize the engagement". 244: ### Content creation and academic research 245: Gather source material from many pages at once, filtered by recency and relevance. 246: | Task | Tools | 247: |------|-------| 248: | Collect multiple sources in one call | `scrape_batch` (up to 5 URLs) | 249: | News | `search_engine` with news queries | 250: --- 251: ## Tool Selection: Groups 252: Tools are organized into groups so you only load what you need. Fewer tools means less context for your agent to process. 253: - With no `GROUPS` or `TOOLS`, all 31 tools are enabled. Setting either one limits the server to those tools only 254: - `GROUPS` enables tool bundles. Comma-separated: `GROUPS="scrapers,browser"` (local) or `&groups=scrapers,browser` (hosted URL) 255: - `TOOLS` adds individual tools on top: `TOOLS="scrape_batch,session_stats"`. On its own, it enables only the tools you list 256: - Every group also includes `search_engine`, `scrape_as_markdown` and `ask_brightdata_assistant` 257: - Group ID `custom` is reserved; use `TOOLS` for individual picks 258: | Group ID | Contents | Tool count | 259: |----------|----------|-----------| 260: | `scrapers` | Search and run any pre-built Web Scraper API scraper (Amazon, LinkedIn, TikTok, npm, ...) | 6 | 261: | `browser` | Remote browser automation | 14 | 262: | `geo` | ChatGPT and Perplexity response collection | 2 | 263: | `advanced_scraping` | Batch tools, session stats | 3 | 264: Older group IDs (`ecommerce`, `social`, `business`, `finance`, `research`, `app_stores`, `travel`, `code`) still work and enable the `scrapers` tools; `social` and `business` also add `business_search`, `search_dataset` and `list_dataset_fields`. Old `web_data_*` names in `TOOLS` enable the `scrapers` tools too. 265: ### Configuration examples 266: Local server with browser automation and batch tools: 267: ```json 268: { 269: "mcpServers": { 270: "Bright Data": { 271: "command": "npx", 272: "args": ["@brightdata/mcp"], 273: "env": { 274: "API_TOKEN": "", 275: "GROUPS": "browser,advanced_scraping" 276: } 277: } 278: } 279: } 280: ``` 281: Coding agent setup (Claude Code / Cursor / Windsurf) — npm, PyPI and GitHub data through the pre-built scrapers: 282: ```json 283: { 284: "mcpServers": { 285: "Bright Data": { 286: "command": "npx", 287: "args": ["@brightdata/mcp"], 288: "env": { 289: "API_TOKEN": "", 290: "GROUPS": "scrapers" 291: } 292: } 293: } 294: } 295: ``` 296: --- 297: ## Tools Reference (31 Tools) 298: ### Which tool to use 299: - **Known URL, need the content:** `scrape_as_markdown`. Multiple URLs (up to 5): `scrape_batch` 300: - **Need to find information:** `search_engine`. Multiple queries (up to 5): `search_engine_batch` 301: - **Structured data from a known platform (Amazon, LinkedIn, TikTok, npm, PyPI, etc.):** `search_scrapers` → `get_scraper_details` → `run_scraper`. Returns JSON records. If the run takes longer than 45 seconds, `run_scraper` returns a `snapshot_id`: check it with `get_scraper_progress`, then read the records with `get_scraper_results` 302: - **Find companies or people by description or criteria** (industry, location, size, title): `business_search`. One call, ranked records, no URL needed 303: - **Raw HTML:** `scrape_as_markdown` with `format: 'html'` 304: - **Page cut at 40,000 characters:** call `scrape_as_markdown` again with `snapshot_id` and `start` from the result's `next` field. The rest is read from the saved page at no extra cost 305: - **Page needs JavaScript or interaction (click, type, scroll):** `scraping_browser_*` tools. The scrape tools don't render JavaScript 306: - **How ChatGPT/Perplexity answer a prompt:** `chatgpt_ai_insights` / `perplexity_ai_insights` 307: - **Question about Bright Data itself (products, zones, errors, setup):** `ask_brightdata_assistant` 308: Notes on scraper runs: 309: - Return structured JSON, billed per record returned 310: - Records with an `error` field explain inputs that failed, e.g. a URL of the wrong type 311: - Results can be large. Keep `limit_per_input` low for `discover_by_*` methods and run bulk collection in a subagent where your framework supports it, so records don't flood the main context window 312: - If a run fails, `scrape_as_markdown` works on the same URL as a fallback 313:
314: Search and Scraping — 5 tools 315: | Tool | Description | Group | 316: |------|-------------|-------| 317: | `search_engine` | Search Bing (default) or Google. Returns JSON (link, title, description), 10 results per page. Params: `country`, `page` (from 0), `time_range` (`hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`, `any`; Bing supports only `day`, `week`, `year`). Times out after 55 s | default / every group | 318: | `search_engine_batch` | Up to 5 search queries in one call. Searches not done within 55 s return a timeout error | default / `advanced_scraping` | 319: | `scrape_as_markdown` | Any URL. Returns the content as markdown (default), text, html or ld_json. No JavaScript rendering. Pages over 40,000 characters are cut; to read the rest at no extra cost, call again with `snapshot_id` and `start` from the result's `next` field | default / every group | 320: | `scrape_batch` | Up to 5 URLs in one call. Returns the content as markdown (default), text, html or ld_json. 40,000 characters in total, shared between pages; each cut page has a `next` for `scrape_as_markdown` | default / `advanced_scraping` | 321: | `session_stats` | Tool usage counts for the current session | default / `advanced_scraping` | 322:
323:
324: Web Scraper API — 6 tools 325: Search and run any of Bright Data's 1,200+ pre-built scrapers. The scraper list is loaded from `docs.brightdata.com/scrapers.json` and refreshed daily. Available on both the hosted and the local server. Enabled by default when no tools or groups are selected; otherwise add the `scrapers` group (`&groups=scrapers` on the hosted URL, `GROUPS=scrapers` locally). 326: Typical flow: `search_scrapers` → `get_scraper_details` → `run_scraper`. Runs are billed per record; `discover_by_*` methods collect up to `limit_per_input` records per input (default 10). 327: | Tool | Description | Group | 328: |------|-------------|-------| 329: | `search_scrapers` | Find scrapers by site or data type (e.g. "amazon reviews", "linkedin.com"). Returns dataset ID, name, domain and collection methods | default / `scrapers` | 330: | `get_scraper_details` | Description, input fields, example input and main output fields for one scraper method | default / `scrapers` | 331: | `run_scraper` | Run a scraper method. Waits up to 45 seconds; if still running, returns a `snapshot_id` to check later | default / `scrapers` | 332: | `get_scraper_progress` | Status of a run: starting, running, ready, failed or canceled | default / `scrapers` | 333: | `get_scraper_results` | Records of a finished run | default / `scrapers` | 334: | `refresh_scrapers` | Reload the scraper list now instead of waiting for the daily refresh | default / `scrapers` | 335:
336:
337: Browser Automation — 14 tools 338: Remote browser session. Typical sequence: navigate → snapshot → interact by ref → extract or screenshot. 339: | Tool | Description | 340: |------|-------------| 341: | `scraping_browser_navigate` | Open or reuse a browser session and navigate to a URL | 342: | `scraping_browser_go_back` | Navigate back | 343: | `scraping_browser_go_forward` | Navigate forward | 344: | `scraping_browser_snapshot` | ARIA snapshot of the page listing interactive elements with refs. Required before ref-based actions | 345: | `scraping_browser_click_ref` | Click an element by ref from the latest snapshot | 346: | `scraping_browser_type_ref` | Type into an element by ref; optionally press Enter to submit | 347: | `scraping_browser_fill_form` | Fill several form fields by ref in one call | 348: | `scraping_browser_screenshot` | Screenshot of the current page; optional `full_page` | 349: | `scraping_browser_get_text` | Text content of the page body | 350: | `scraping_browser_get_html` | HTML of the current page | 351: | `scraping_browser_scroll` | Scroll to the bottom of the page | 352: | `scraping_browser_scroll_to_ref` | Scroll an element into view | 353: | `scraping_browser_wait_for_ref` | Wait for an element to become visible, with optional timeout | 354: | `scraping_browser_network_requests` | Network requests since page load: method, URL, status | 355: Refs come from the latest snapshot. If the page changes after a click or navigation, take a new snapshot before the next ref-based action. For static pages, `scrape_as_markdown` is faster and cheaper than a browser session. 356:
357:
358: GEO and LLM Visibility — 2 tools 359: | Tool | Input | Returns | 360: |------|-------|---------| 361: | `chatgpt_ai_insights` | Prompt | ChatGPT's answer as Markdown | 362: | `perplexity_ai_insights` | Prompt | Perplexity's answer as Markdown | 363: Use for Generative Engine Optimization (tracking how LLMs describe your brand) and LLM-as-a-judge workflows. 364:
365:
366: Business and Dataset Search — 3 tools 367: Search stored LinkedIn company and people data; returns matching records at once, with no scraper run. 368: | Tool | Description | Group | 369: |------|-------------|-------| 370: | `business_search` | Companies or people (`category`) by description or criteria. Up to 10 ranked records per call. Modes: `instant` (default, plain text), `smart` (plain text, AI reranking), `ludicrous` (exact JSON filters, can page past 100). Views: `summary` (default), `full` (`limit` 5 or less), or a field list | default / `social`, `business` | 371: | `list_dataset_fields` | Filterable fields of a dataset (name, type, description). Call before `search_dataset` | default / `social`, `business` | 372: | `search_dataset` | Exact filters on raw dataset fields, up to 10 records per call, with a cursor for more. Also the contact-enriched people dataset | default / `social`, `business` | 373: `business_search` examples: 374: ```json 375: {"category": "company", "query": "fintech startups in Berlin with 50 to 200 employees"} 376: {"category": "people", "query": "product managers at SaaS companies in London", "mode": "smart", "view": {"fields": ["name", "url", "current_title", "current_company_name"]}} 377: {"category": "company", "mode": "ludicrous", "query": {"and": [{"text": {"industry": "software"}}, {"in": {"headquarters_country_code": ["US", "GB"]}}, {"range": {"employees_in_linkedin": {">=": 50, "<=": 500}}}]}, "offset": 200} 378: ``` 379: Notes: 380: - `meta.matched` is a lower bound, not a total. `meta.coverage_percent` below 100 means a partial result 381: - `instant` and `smart` reach the first 100 matches only (`offset` + `limit` 100 or less). Use `ludicrous` to page further (`offset` up to 1000) 382: - To find people at the companies you found, search `company` first, then `people` 383: - Each call is billed. Business Search is in beta and needs an account with a business email; other accounts get `Business Search not enabled` and can use `search_dataset` 384:
385:
386: Bright Data Assistant — 1 tool 387: | Tool | Description | Group | 388: |------|-------------|-------| 389: | `ask_brightdata_assistant` | Ask Sophie, Bright Data's support assistant, about products, APIs, zones, errors or account setup. Pass the returned `dialog_id` to ask a follow-up in the same thread | default / every group | 390:
391: [Full tool reference in the docs →](https://docs.brightdata.com/ai/mcp-server/tools) 392: --- 393: ## Agent Skills 394: Bright Data's agent skills teach your agent when and how to use Bright Data. They live at [github.com/brightdata/skills](https://github.com/brightdata/skills). Start with `agent-onboarding`. 395: --- 396: ## Configuration 397: ### Basic setup (local) 398: ```json 399: { 400: "mcpServers": { 401: "Bright Data": { 402: "command": "npx", 403: "args": ["@brightdata/mcp"], 404: "env": { 405: "API_TOKEN": "your-token-here" 406: } 407: } 408: } 409: } 410: ``` 411: ### Advanced configuration 412: ```json 413: { 414: "mcpServers": { 415: "Bright Data": { 416: "command": "npx", 417: "args": ["@brightdata/mcp"], 418: "env": { 419: "API_TOKEN": "your-token-here", 420: "RATE_LIMIT": "100/1h", 421: "SERP_ZONE": "custom_serp", 422: "BROWSER_ZONE": "custom_browser" 423: } 424: } 425: } 426: } 427: ``` 428: ### Environment variables 429: | Variable | Description | Default | Example | 430: |----------|-------------|---------|---------| 431: | `API_TOKEN` | Your Bright Data API token (required) | - | `your-token-here` | 432: | `RATE_LIMIT` | Custom rate limiting | unlimited | `100/1h`, `50/30m` | 433: | `SERP_ZONE` | Custom SERP API zone name, used by the search tools | `mcp_serp` | `my_serp_zone` | 434: | `BROWSER_ZONE` | Custom Browser zone name | `mcp_browser` | `my_browser_zone` | 435: | `CONTENT_GATE` | When page content returned by a data tool looks like instructions to change the MCP configuration, the server asks the user (via MCP elicitation) before returning it. Set to `off` to disable | `on` | `off` | 436: | `CONTENT_GATE_TIMEOUT` | Seconds to wait for the user's answer before withholding the content | `120` | `60`, `300` | 437: | `BROWSER_FILTERED_SNAPSHOT` | `scraping_browser_snapshot` always lists only buttons, links and fields. Saves tokens, and stops page text posing as a clickable element (for sensitive tasks). If necessary, Page text can then be read with `scraping_browser_get_text` | `off` | `on` | 438: | `BASE_TIMEOUT` | Request timeout in seconds for the search and dataset tools (search also stops at 55 s) | No limit | `60`, `120` | 439: | `BASE_MAX_RETRIES` | Max retries for the search and dataset tools on transient errors (0-3) | `0` | `1`, `3` | 440: | `GROUPS` | Comma-separated tool group IDs. Limits the server to these groups | All tools | `scrapers,browser` | 441: | `TOOLS` | Comma-separated individual tool names. Limits the server to these tools | All tools | `scrape_batch,session_stats` | 442: ### Content gate 443: `scrape_as_markdown`, `search_engine` and their batch variants return whatever a web 444: page says. If that content contains text that reads like instructions to change your MCP 445: configuration — register a server, run an `npx -y` package, edit the MCP config file — the server 446: pauses and asks you, through your MCP client, before returning it. Approve and the content is 447: returned unchanged; decline and it is withheld with a short explanation to the assistant. Pages that 448: do not contain such text are returned exactly as before, with no prompt. For a batch call, only the 449: matching items are withheld. 450: Pages that are *about* MCP configuration (documentation, READMEs) will naturally prompt. Clients that 451: do not support MCP elicitation get the matching content withheld; set `CONTENT_GATE=off` if you 452: accept the risk. While the server waits for your answer it reports progress; clients that do not 453: extend their tool timeout on progress will cap the wait at their own limit — `CONTENT_GATE_TIMEOUT` 454: is the knob on the server side. Browser tools are not covered. 455: --- 456: ## Documentation 457: | Resource | Link | 458: |----------|------| 459: | API documentation | [docs.brightdata.com/ai/mcp-server/overview](https://docs.brightdata.com/ai/mcp-server/overview) | 460: | Full tools reference | [docs.brightdata.com/ai/mcp-server/tools](https://docs.brightdata.com/ai/mcp-server/tools) | 461: | Agent skills | [github.com/brightdata/skills](https://github.com/brightdata/skills) | 462: | Usage examples | [examples](https://github.com/brightdata/brightdata-mcp/blob/main/examples) | 463: | Changelog | [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/brightdata/brightdata-mcp/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) | 464: --- 465: ## Troubleshooting 466:
467: Common issues and solutions 468: ### "spawn npx ENOENT" error 469: Install Node.js, or use the full path to node: 470: ```json 471: "command": "/usr/local/bin/node" // macOS/Linux 472: "command": "C:\\Program Files\\nodejs\\node.exe" // Windows 473: ``` 474: ### Timeouts on complex sites 475: Increase the timeout in your client settings to 180s. 476: ### Authentication issues 477: Verify your API token is valid and has the required permissions. Tokens are managed in [account settings](https://brightdata.com/cp/setting/users). 478: ### run_scraper returns errors or no data 479: Records with an `error` field explain inputs that failed. Compare your input with `sample_input` from `get_scraper_details` (e.g., Amazon product URLs contain `/dp/`, Walmart ones `/ip/`) and check the page is publicly accessible. `scrape_as_markdown` works on the same URL as a fallback. 480: ### Remote server connection fails 481: Check your internet connection and firewall settings. 482:

36: pip install --user sherlock-project
37: That’s it! You can now run sherlock from anywhere.
38: sherlock --version
39: This package is not officially supported, but it’s maintained by a trusted packager.
40: brew install sherlock
41: That’s it! You can now run sherlock from anywhere.
42: sherlock --version
43: This package is not officially supported, but it’s maintained under the trusted purview of the Debian Security Tools Packaging Team. The ParrotOS image is maintained by the ParrotOS team.We may begin to officially support this package in the future.
44: Supported distributions are Kali and ParrotOS. Work is underway to support Debian, Ubuntu, and others.
45: sudo apt install sherlock
46: That’s it! You can now run sherlock from anywhere.
47: sherlock --version
48: This is an officially supported package, maintained by a member of the Sherlock Project itself.Sherlock has out-of-the-box support for Fedora. Enterprise Linux support through EPEL is planned.
49: Enterprise Linux distributions are RHEL, CentOS, Alma, Rocky, Oracle, and Scientific.
50: sudo dnf install sherlock-project
51: That’s it! You can now run sherlock from anywhere.
52: sherlock --version
53: This package is not officially supported, but still closely follows our release cycle.
54: sudo pacman -S sherlock
55: That’s it! You can now run sherlock from anywhere.
56: sherlock --version
57: This is an officially supported image, maintained by a member of the Sherlock Project itself.
58: docker pull sherlock/sherlock
59: Sherlock doesn’t yet have context detection. It’s recommended that Docker containers be ran with option -o /opt/sherlock/results/{user123}.txt (replace {user123}) when an output file is desired at the mounted volume (as seen in the compose). This has no effect on stdout, which functions as expected out of the box.
60: # One-off searches
61: docker run --rm -t sherlock/sherlock user123
62: # If you need to save the output file... (modify as needed)
63: # Output file will land in ${pwd}/results
64: docker run --rm -t -v "$PWD/results:/opt/sherlock/results" sherlock/sherlock -o /opt/sherlock/results/text.txt user123
65: # At any time, you may update the image via this command
66: docker pull sherlock/sherlock
67: Using compose
68: version: "3"

71: container_name: sherlock
72: image: sherlock/sherlock
73: volumes:
74: - ./sherlock/:/opt/sherlock/results/
75: docker compose run sherlock user123
76: Build image from source (useful for contributors)
77: # Assumes ${pwd} is repository root
78: docker build -t sherlock .
79: docker run --rm -t sherlock user123
80: While this method uses the official repository, it’s not an officially supported installation method. This method is recommended for contributors, packagers, and other users who need access to the source code.
81: git clone https://github.com/sherlock-project/sherlock.git

85: Build live package from source (useful for contributors)
86: Building an editable (or live) package links the entry point to your current directory, rather than to the standard install location. This is often useful when working with the code base, as changes are reflected immediately without reinstallation.Note that the version number will be 0.0.0 for pipx local builds unless manually changed in the pyproject file (it will prompt the user for an update).
87: pipx install -e .

1: > ## Documentation Index
2: > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.waterfall.io/llms.txt
3: > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
4: # One GTM API for contacts and companies
5: > Find prospects, enrich contact and company profiles, find emails and mobile numbers, verify emails, and check job changes with the Waterfall API.
6: Waterfall brings together 30+ data vendors through one B2B data API. Find people at target accounts, match emails to business profiles, find contact details, and check whether existing contacts have changed jobs.
7: Use it to build signup enrichment, prospecting, and CRM workflows with the data your team needs. [About Waterfall](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/about-waterfall.md) explains how it fits into your stack.
8: > [card] [Explore use cases](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/overview.md)
9: >
10: > Start with a signup, target account, or CRM record and see the workflow.
11: > [card] [Use with agents](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/skills-overview.md)
12: >
13: > Run a lookup with an agent or build Waterfall into your application.
14: > [card] [Evaluate Waterfall](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/evaluate-waterfall.md)
15: >
16: > Compare useful results, match quality, and cost on your own records.
17: > [card] [Make your first request](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/quickstart.md)
18: >
19: > Launch a contact enrichment job and retrieve its result.
20: Already know what you want to build? [Choose an API](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/introduction.md) to compare the inputs, results, and availability of each capability.
21: ## What do you want to build?
22: | Your task | Start here |
23: | - | - |
24: | See who is behind a signup email | [Signup enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/signup-enrichment.md) |
25: | Find people at your target accounts | [Account prospecting](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/account-prospecting.md) |
26: | Fill gaps in contact and company records | [CRM enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/crm-enrichment.md) |
27: | Check where existing contacts work | [Job changes](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/job-changes.md) |
28: | Check an email before outreach | [Email verification](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/email-verification.md) |
29: | Identify companies visiting your website | [Website company identification](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/website-company-identification.md) |
30: ## How the API works
31: Send requests to `https://api.waterfall.io` with your API key in the `x-api-key` header. [Authentication](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/authentication.md) covers access and key management.
32: Prospector and the contact, phone, and company enrichment APIs return a `job_id`. Use the matching Finder to retrieve the result, or provide a `webhook_url` to receive it. Search and verification APIs return results in the same request. The [API selection guide](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/introduction.md) lists the response pattern and availability for each capability.
33: Every reference page shows the supported inputs and outputs. Use [Usage Tracking](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/inline-usage.md) to read returned costs, and [Account Reporting](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/account-reporter-v2.md) for usage across a date range.
34: For API access, pricing, or help choosing the right workflow, [talk to the Waterfall team](mailto:support@waterfall.io). Common product and integration questions are covered in the [FAQ](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/faq.md).

4: # About Waterfall
5: > B2B contact and company data from 30+ providers, through one API.
6: Growth and revenue teams, developers, and AI agents use Waterfall to find people at target accounts, enrich contact and company records, find emails and phone numbers, verify email addresses, and check job changes. Build these capabilities into your prospecting, recruitment, CRM, or marketing workflows and products.
7: ## Why we bring together multiple data providers
8: No single provider has every contact or field you need. We combine providers to improve coverage and quality while keeping costs under control. Our team adds and removes providers as their performance changes.
9: We manage the provider connections. Your team maintains one Waterfall integration and one set of agreed rates. Changes to the provider mix do not change those rates; your total cost depends on the services and options you use and your request volume.
10: ## Who Waterfall is for
11: | Team | What you can build |
12: | - | - |
13: | GTM engineers | [Prospecting workflows](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/account-prospecting.md) that find relevant people at target accounts. |
14: | Revenue operations | [CRM enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/crm-enrichment.md) to fill missing contact and company fields, plus [job-change checks](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/job-changes.md). |
15: | Product-led growth teams | [Signup enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/signup-enrichment.md) that provides role and company context for lead scoring, segmentation, and routing. |
16: | Developers and product teams | Contact and company data for GTM tools, recruitment platforms, CRMs, marketing software, and [agent workflows](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/skills-overview.md). |
17: ## Teams we have worked with
18: Waterfall.io's current and past customers include Ramp, Gorgias, Zapier, Lightfield, JOIN, awork, Coverflex, Netic, 360Learning, Rippling, and ClickUp.
19: ## How we approach data quality
20: We verify every email we find in real time, just before delivering the enrichment result. Profiles are typically refreshed in under 14 days, with real-time updates when needed. We compare records across providers to check for conflicting or outdated details, then clean and structure the results. We also benchmark our providers every quarter.
21: What matters most depends on what you are building. A signup workflow may need a person's company and role; a recruitment platform may need work history. We help you benchmark the fields you care about using your own inputs, and can build custom data pipelines around those needs.
22: ## Security and assurance
23: Waterfall has undergone a SOC 2 Type II audit covering Security, Confidentiality, and Privacy. Our penetration tests are conducted by independent auditors who also work with Snowflake and T-Mobile.
24: Our infrastructure runs on AWS, with encryption in transit and at rest. We use the data you submit to the API to fulfil your requests. We do not resell those inputs, repurpose them for other customers, or add them to a shared enrichment database.
25: [Contact our team](mailto:support@waterfall.io) for audit scope and security documentation.
26: ## How Waterfall fits into your stack
27: Use Waterfall data in your CRM, Snowflake tables, Clay workflows, or your own product. Connect through the REST API; asynchronous enrichment results can arrive by webhook or be retrieved by polling. Your integration can write those results back to your tools, score leads, route signups, or power features in your product.
28: ## Who is behind Waterfall?
29: Waterfall.io has been operating since 2021, with 5+ years of experience building and running B2B data enrichment.
30: Waterfall.io was co-founded by [Guillaume Cabane](https://www.linkedin.com/in/cabane/), who previously served as interim CMO at Ramp and VP of Growth at Segment, Drift, and Gorgias.
31: Guillaume pioneered multi-vendor "waterfall enrichment" while building Segment's growth stack in 2016–2017, before the term became widely used.
32: ## How our team can help
33: API access is available by approval. We review each request individually and work with a limited number of customers so we can provide direct support and plan capacity around each team's needs.
34: When you work with Waterfall, you get a dedicated channel with our founders. Ask questions, share what you are building, and work directly with us on API selection, integration, benchmarks, and custom data pipelines.
35: * [Evaluate Waterfall](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/evaluate-waterfall.md) to plan a test on your own data.
36: * [Talk to the team](mailto:support@waterfall.io) about your use case, API access, and pricing.
37: ## Official links
38: * [Waterfall website](https://www.waterfall.io)
39: * [Waterfall on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/waterfall)
40: * [Waterfall API Skills on GitHub](https://github.com/Waterfall-io/api-skills)
41: ## Trademark
42: WATERFALL is a registered U.S. trademark for data enrichment SaaS in Class 42 (Reg. No. 8,508,955), registered on October 20, 2026.

4: # Authentication
5: > Get access to the Waterfall API, send your API key in the x-api-key header, and manage keys for separate workflows.
6: Authenticate data and account API requests with your Waterfall API key in the `x-api-key` header. [Contact the team](mailto:support@waterfall.io) for API access and pricing.
7: ```http theme={null}
8: x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
9: ```
10: > [!NOTE]
11: >
12: > The API host is `https://api.waterfall.io`. Data endpoints use `/v1/`; Account Reporter V2 uses `/v2/account`. Use the path shown on each reference page.
13: ## Best practices
14: * Store keys in server-side environment variables. Keep them out of browser code and public repositories.
15: * Rotate keys periodically.
16: * Use [dedicated sub-keys](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/api-keys-overview.md) to manage access and usage for separate teams or workflows. Creating and managing sub-keys requires a **master API key**.
17: Missing keys return `401`. Invalid keys return `403`; this status can also indicate that a feature or permission is unavailable to the key. Inspect the error `code` using the [Errors guide](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/errors.md).
18: Follow the [quickstart](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/quickstart.md) to make your first request, or use [Agent Skills](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/skills-overview.md) to build with an agent.

1: > ## Documentation Index
2: > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.waterfall.io/llms.txt
3: > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
4: # Enrich your first contact
5: > Make your first Waterfall API request: submit an email address, save the job ID, and retrieve the contact enrichment result.
6: Start with an email address and retrieve the available profile and contact data. This example uses Contact Enrichment, which runs as an asynchronous job.
7: ## 1. Set up your API key
8: You need a Waterfall API key with Contact Enrichment enabled. [Contact the team](mailto:support@waterfall.io) for access and pricing. Requests use your account's configured rates.
9: Store the key in an environment variable in your terminal:
10: ```bash theme={null}
11: export WATERFALL_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
12: ```
13: Keep the key on your server or in your local environment. See [Authentication](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/authentication.md) for key management.
14: ## 2. Submit an email address
15: Replace `person@company.com` with the contact you want to look up. This request leaves phone enrichment off.
16: ```bash theme={null}
17: curl --request POST 'https://api.waterfall.io/v1/enrichment/contact' \
18: --header "x-api-key: $WATERFALL_API_KEY" \
19: --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
20: --data '{
21: "email": "person@company.com",
22: "include_phones": false
23: }'
24: ```
25: The response gives you a `job_id` and `start_date`. An illustrative response:
26: ```json theme={null}
27: {
28: "job_id": "1a836daa-ec37-4c75-8a10-080ee9b28a13",
29: "start_date": "2026-10-12T09:00:00Z"
30: }
31: ```
32: Save the returned `job_id`. It identifies this lookup; the contact data arrives when the job finishes.
33: ## 3. Retrieve the result
34: Set `WATERFALL_JOB_ID` to the ID from your response, then call the Finder:
35: ```bash theme={null}
36: export WATERFALL_JOB_ID="YOUR_RETURNED_JOB_ID"
37: curl --get 'https://api.waterfall.io/v1/enrichment/contact' \
38: --header "x-api-key: $WATERFALL_API_KEY" \
39: --data-urlencode "job_id=$WATERFALL_JOB_ID"
40: ```
41: Read `status` before using the output:
42: | Status | What to do |
43: | - | - |
44: | `RUNNING` | Wait before checking the same job again. Respect the [rate limit](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/rate-limit.md). |
45: | `SUCCEEDED` | Inspect `output.person` for available data and `output.usage` for returned cost information. |
46: | `FAILED`, `TIMED_OUT`, or `ABORTED` | Stop polling this job and inspect the response before deciding what to do next. |
47: A successful response might look like this (fictional contact; other fields omitted):
48: ```json theme={null}
49: {
50: "status": "SUCCEEDED",
51: "output": {
52: "person": {
53: "first_name": "Jordan",
54: "last_name": "Lee",
55: "title": "Head of Sales",
56: "company_name": "Example Company"
57: }
58: }
59: }
60: ```
61: Available profile fields can include the person's name, role, location, employment history, and email information. Use the [Contact Enrichment Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/contact-enrichment-finder.md) reference for the full response shape. Keep missing fields unresolved rather than filling them with guesses.
62: ## 4. Connect the result to your workflow
63: Your application decides which fields to store or use. For a signup workflow, read [signup enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/signup-enrichment.md). For existing records, read [CRM enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/crm-enrichment.md).
64: For automated delivery, add a `webhook_url` to the launch request. You can also pass `custom_fields` to carry your own record identifier. See the [launcher reference](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/contact-enrichment-launcher.md) and [Webhook Verification](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/webhook-verification.md).
65: ## Other ways to start
66: * Have a LinkedIn identifier or a name and company domain? Contact Enrichment supports those input strategies too.
67: * Need people at a company rather than a known contact? [Choose an API](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/introduction.md) to compare Prospector and Search Contact.
68: * Working with an agent? [Agent Skills](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/skills-overview.md) covers direct calls and reusable integration code.
69: * Got an error? Check [Errors](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/errors.md) for validation, access, quota, and rate-limit guidance.
70: This documentation is built and hosted on [Mintlify](https://mintlify.com), a developer documentation platform.

1: > ## Documentation Index
2: > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.waterfall.io/llms.txt
3: > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
4: # Rate limits
5: > Plan Waterfall API request volume, handle HTTP 429 responses, and use Retry-After when polling or processing batches.
6: The default limit for Prospector, Search, Enrichment, Job Change, and Email Verification is **50 requests per 60 seconds**. Your key may have a different configured limit. Account Reporter is exempt from rate limiting.
7: ## Higher request volumes
8: > [!NOTE]
9: >
10: > Waterfall can support **more than 10× the default limit** with the right setup. Email [support@waterfall.io](mailto:support@waterfall.io) with your APIs and expected volume to arrange higher limits.
11: A sub-key's `per_interval` cannot exceed the master key's configured value. See [API Key Management](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/api-keys-overview.md) for key settings.
12: ## Handle a rate-limit response
13: When a request exceeds the limit, the API returns `429`. Rate-limit responses include these headers:
14: | Header | Meaning |
15: | - | - |
16: | `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Max requests allowed in interval |
17: | `X-RateLimit-Interval` | Interval duration in seconds |
18: | `Retry-After` | Seconds to wait before retry |
19: ## Retry guidance
20: * Wait for `Retry-After` before retrying a rate-limited request.
21: * Use exponential backoff if repeated attempts still receive `429`.
22: * Limit concurrency when processing a list of records.
23: * For asynchronous jobs, keep the returned `job_id` and poll the Finder. Do not start another job to check whether the first one finished.
24: For asynchronous workflows, a `webhook_url` can reduce polling. See [Webhook Verification](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/webhook-verification.md). A `402` quota error is different from a rate limit; use the [Errors guide](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/errors.md) to choose the next step.

1: > ## Documentation Index
2: > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.waterfall.io/llms.txt
3: > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
4: # Waterfall API FAQ
5: > What Waterfall does, who it serves, which API to choose, and how to evaluate, price, and use contact and company data in workflows and agents.
6: Find answers about Waterfall, the data you can get, and how to use it in your workflow. For an endpoint comparison, start with [Choose an API](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/introduction.md).
7: Jump to [About Waterfall](#about-waterfall), [choosing a capability](#choosing-a-capability), [data and results](#data-and-results), [access and pricing](#access-usage-and-pricing), or [building an integration](#building-an-integration).
8: ## About Waterfall
9: ### What is Waterfall used for?
10: Waterfall.io is a B2B data API for go-to-market workflows.
11: Use Waterfall to find people at target accounts, enrich contact and company records, match emails to business profiles, find phone numbers, verify email addresses, and check job changes.
12: ### Who is Waterfall for?
13: Waterfall serves growth, revenue, and go-to-market teams. GTM engineers build prospecting workflows, revenue operations teams fill gaps in CRM records, and product-led growth teams add business context to signups. Developers can also add contact and company data to GTM tools, recruitment platforms, CRMs, marketing software, and other products.
14: ### Who are Waterfall.io's customers?
15: Waterfall.io's current and past customers include Ramp, Gorgias, Zapier, Lightfield, JOIN, awork, Coverflex, Netic, 360Learning, Rippling, and ClickUp.
16: ### What does Waterfall's multi-vendor approach mean?
17: Waterfall combines 30+ data vendors through one API. Coverage varies by provider, so a contact or field missing from one source may be available from another. We evaluate providers on coverage, accuracy, freshness, and cost, and add or remove them as their performance changes.
18: Your team maintains one integration and one set of agreed Waterfall rates, without managing separate vendor connections and contracts. Changes to the vendor mix do not change those rates. Your total cost depends on the services and options you use and your request volume.
19: ### Is Waterfall a CRM or an outreach platform?
20: The Waterfall API supplies data for your CRM, product, or outreach workflow. Your integration decides where to save that data, which records to update, and when to send a message. Calling an enrichment endpoint does not create a CRM automation or send outreach.
21: ### Is Waterfall secure?
22: Waterfall has undergone a SOC 2 Type II audit covering Security, Confidentiality, and Privacy. Independent auditors also conduct our penetration tests.
23: Those auditors also work with Snowflake and T-Mobile. Our infrastructure runs on AWS, with encryption in transit and at rest. The API supports signed webhooks so your receiving system can verify that a delivery came from Waterfall and that its payload was not changed.
24: Webhook signing depends on the signing configuration. Your receiver should verify the signature and reject unsigned deliveries when your workflow requires verification. The [Webhook Verification guide](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/webhook-verification.md) explains the checks. For audit scope and security documentation, [contact our team](mailto:support@waterfall.io).
25: ### Does Waterfall reuse or resell the data I submit?
26: We use the data you submit to the API to fulfil your requests. We do not resell those inputs, repurpose them for other customers, or add them to a shared enrichment database. Job results are saved so you can retrieve them later. For retention requirements, [contact our team](mailto:support@waterfall.io).
27: ## Choosing a capability
28: ### What information do I need to get started?
29: The starting input depends on the Waterfall capability:
30: | Task | Accepted starting fields | Result |
31: | - | - | - |
32: | Enrich a known person | `email`, `linkedin`, `full_name` + `domain`, or `first_name` + `last_name` + `domain` | Available profile and contact data |
33: | Find people at a target account | `domain` plus `title_filter` or `title_filters` for Prospector | Contacts matching your targeting criteria |
34: | Enrich a known company | `domain`, `linkedin`, or `name` | Available company details |
35: | Verify an email | `email` | The address's verification status |
36: | Check a contact's employment | For example, `company_domain` + `contact_linkedin`; a `professional_email` alone is also supported | Job-change outcome and available profile |
37: | Identify a company from an IP | `ip` containing an IPv4 address | Available company context and confidence |
38: Use [Choose an API](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/introduction.md) to select the endpoint, then follow its reference for the accepted field names and combinations.
39: ### Can I turn an email address into a professional profile?
40: Yes. [Contact Enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/contact-enrichment-launcher.md) accepts an `email` and returns available profile data after the job completes. The result can include name, title, company, LinkedIn, location, and employment history. The person may no longer work at the email's domain, so the result can show that company as a past experience. Use the returned fields in your own qualification rules; see [signup enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/signup-enrichment.md) for the workflow.
41: ### Can I enrich a personal email address, such as Gmail?
42: Yes. Waterfall Contact Enrichment accepts professional and personal email addresses. A professional email generally gives better enrichment quality. Personal email support does not guarantee a match or every profile field, so test the types of signups you receive. See the [Contact Enrichment reference](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/contact-enrichment-launcher.md).
43: ### Can I find an email address if I only have a name or LinkedIn profile?
44: You can search with a LinkedIn profile. A name also needs a company domain. [Contact Enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/contact-enrichment-launcher.md) accepts `linkedin`, `full_name` + `domain`, or `first_name` + `last_name` + `domain`. It returns available contact data, including a professional email and its verification fields.
45: ### Should I send all the identifiers I have for a person?
46: Choose the identifier strategy for the endpoint. [Contact Enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/contact-enrichment-launcher.md#input-strategies) uses email first, then LinkedIn, then name and domain. [Phone Enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/phone-enrichment-launcher.md#input-strategies) uses LinkedIn first, then email, then name and domain. Supplying several identifiers does not ask these endpoints to cross-check them or try each one in sequence. Your integration controls any later attempt with another supported identifier.
47: ### How do I find decision-makers at a company?
48: Use Waterfall [Prospector](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-launcher.md) with the company domain and a `title_filter` or named `title_filters`. Add location filters if your target roles are limited to a region. Prospector returns matching contacts with available email data and optional phone enrichment. Review the person's role against your buying criteria; a title match alone does not establish purchasing authority. See [account prospecting](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/account-prospecting.md).
49: ### What is the difference between Search Contact and Prospector?
50: Waterfall [Search Contact](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/search-contact-launcher.md) finds professional profiles and returns results in the same response. It supports a LinkedIn lookup, searches within a company, and searches across company sets with the required filters. It does not return email addresses or phone numbers.
51: [Prospector](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-launcher.md) finds contacts at a company domain using title filters and optional location filters. It runs asynchronously and returns available contact details, with optional phone enrichment. Use Search Contact when you want to select profiles first; use Prospector when your task calls for contacts and their contact details. See [account prospecting](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/account-prospecting.md).
52: ### Can I search for people across companies by role or hire date?
53: Yes. Use [Search Contact](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/search-contact-launcher.md) in company-set mode. Supply a company filter (`company_location_countries`, `company_industries`, or `company_employee_ranges`), a date (`experience_start_date` or `experience_start_date_new_hire`), and `title_filters` or `title_lists`. The result contains profiles without email or phone channels. See [company-set searches and hiring dates](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/search-contact-filters.md#company-set-searches-and-hiring-dates) for a complete request.
54: ### Can I see the job titles available at a company?
55: Yes. [Company Titles](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/company-titles-launcher.md) accepts `domain` or `company_linkedin` and returns the active titles available in Waterfall's data. Select relevant titles and pass them in `title_lists` to Search Contact to find matching profiles. Company Titles is in Preview. It returns role names, not open job vacancies or an employee directory.
56: ### How do I get emails or phones for Search Contact results?
57: Waterfall Search Contact returns profiles with email and phone channels redacted. Pass an available `linkedin_url` from a result as `linkedin` to [Contact Enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/contact-enrichment-launcher.md). Set `include_phones: true` if you also need phone enrichment. Phone enrichment may add charges when numbers are found.
58: ### Which API should I use if I only need phone numbers?
59: Use [Phone Enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/phone-enrichment-launcher.md) for a known person. It accepts `linkedin`, `email`, `full_name` + `domain`, or `first_name` + `last_name` + `domain` and returns available phone numbers in E.164 format. If you also need broader profile data, use [Contact Enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/contact-enrichment-launcher.md) with `include_phones: true`.
60: ### How is Email Verification different from Contact Enrichment?
61: Waterfall [Email Verification](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/email-verifier.md) checks an address you already have and returns `valid`, `invalid`, `risky`, or `unknown`. It does not find a person or discover a new email address. [Contact Enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/contact-enrichment-launcher.md) looks up a person and returns available profile and contact data.
62: The status fields also differ: Email Verification uses `output.email.email_status`, while enriched person records use `email_verified_status` with `safe`, `risky`, `invalid`, `unknown`, or `provider_error`. Interpret the field for the endpoint you called.
63: ### Can I enrich companies as well as people?
64: Yes. Waterfall [Company Enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/company-enrichment-launcher.md) starts with a domain, company LinkedIn identifier, or company name. It returns available company details such as headcount, industry, location, and description. Prefer a domain or LinkedIn identifier when available, since names can be shared by several businesses. See [CRM enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/crm-enrichment.md) for using contact and company data together.
65: ### Can I find prospects before I have a target account list?
66: Yes. Waterfall [Search Company](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/search-company-launcher.md) finds companies by industry, headquarters country, and headcount range. Provide at least one of those filters. Then use a returned company's domain with Search Contact for profiles or Prospector for contacts with email data. Search Company is in Preview. See [account prospecting](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/account-prospecting.md) for the next steps.
67: ### Does Waterfall automatically monitor job changes?
68: Waterfall [Job Change](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/job-change-launcher.md) checks employment when you call it. Your application chooses which contacts to check, when to repeat the check, and what to do with the result. It returns `moved`, `left`, `no_change`, or `unknown`, plus a profile when available. Email and phone channels are redacted from that profile. See [job-change workflows](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/job-changes.md).
69: ### Do I need a LinkedIn URL to check a job change?
70: No. You can send a `professional_email` on its own, or a `contact_full_name` with `company_domain`. You can also pair `company_domain` with `contact_linkedin`, `professional_email`, or `personal_email`. A name or personal email alone is not enough. The [Job Change input table](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/job-change-launcher.md#supported-inputs) lists all supported combinations, including those using a company LinkedIn identifier.
71: ### Does an unknown job-change result mean the contact still works there?
72: No. `unknown` means [Job Change](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/job-change-finder.md) could not establish the outcome. Keep the employment check unresolved rather than treating it as `no_change`. Review any returned profile and the evidence you already have. Retrieving the same job returns its saved result; a later employment check requires a new request.
73: ## Data and results
74: ### How do I check that a result is the right person or company?
75: Compare the returned identifiers and profile with independent information about the intended person or company. A person's LinkedIn profile or a company's domain provides a more specific comparison than a similar name. Review conflicting details and keep the match unresolved when the evidence is insufficient. The [evaluation guide](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/evaluate-waterfall.md#3-review-identity-before-counting-fields) explains how to separate incorrect matches from incomplete profiles.
76: ### Will every request return a complete profile?
77: No. Waterfall's available data depends on the input and the matching record. A returned profile can have missing fields, and a search can return no results. Check the fields your workflow needs before scoring, routing, or updating a record. The [evaluation guide](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/evaluate-waterfall.md) shows how to measure useful results separately from match coverage.
78: ### How fresh is the data?
79: We verify every email we find in real time, just before delivering the enrichment result. Profiles are typically refreshed in under 14 days, with real-time updates when needed. We compare records across providers to check for conflicting or outdated details, clean and structure the results, and benchmark our providers every quarter.
80: Read the returned email verification status before using an address; a completed check can still have a risky or unresolved result. The profile-update window describes typical behavior, not a guaranteed refresh time for every field. To recheck an address already in your database, use [Email Verification](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/email-verifier.md).
81: ### How can I identify companies visiting my website?
82: Use Waterfall Company Reveal to add company context to website visits. Your integration sends the visitor's IPv4 address, and Waterfall returns available company details, a result type, and a confidence label. Use an acceptable match to connect the visit to an account and decide what to do next. Some visits will not resolve to a company. The [website company identification guide](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/website-company-identification.md) includes a request and the fields to review.
83: ### Can Company Reveal identify the person visiting my website?
84: Waterfall [Company Reveal](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/company-reveal-launcher.md) accepts an IPv4 address and returns company context when a company match is available. It does not identify an individual visitor or prove their employer. Inspect the result type and confidence before using the company association. See [website company identification](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/website-company-identification.md).
85: ### How should I compare Waterfall with another data provider?
86: Start with a sample of records from your real workflow and decide which fields matter. A signup flow might need company and role; a recruitment platform might need work history. Give each provider the same inputs, then compare correct matches, missing fields, freshness, completion time, and actual cost. We can help you design the test and review the results. The [evaluation guide](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/evaluate-waterfall.md) provides a practical checklist.
87: ### Can Waterfall help with records my existing provider could not resolve?
88: You can use Waterfall as an additional enrichment step for unresolved records that have a supported input. Run that subset through the relevant endpoint and measure newly correct, useful results and their cost. Additional coverage depends on the records; do not count a duplicate profile as a new match. See [incremental coverage](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/evaluate-waterfall.md#5-measure-cost-per-useful-result).
89: ## Access, usage, and pricing
90: ### How do I get an API key and pricing?
91: API access is available by approval. Enter your work email on the [Waterfall website](https://www.waterfall.io/) to request a key, or [book a call](https://www.waterfall.io/book-a-call) to discuss your workflow and pricing. A member of our team reviews every access request; we aim to reply within a couple of hours. We work with a limited number of customers so we can provide direct support and plan capacity around each team's needs.
92: Once you have a key, send it in the `x-api-key` header. Follow [Authentication](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/authentication.md) and the [Quickstart](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/quickstart.md).
93: ### Does my API key enable every capability?
94: Waterfall API access depends on the features enabled for your key. A valid key can receive a permission error for an unavailable capability, and adding `include_phones: true` requires phone enrichment access. Confirm the capabilities your workflow needs with [the Waterfall team](mailto:support@waterfall.io), and use the [Errors guide](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/errors.md) to interpret the returned code.
95: ### How do I see what a request cost?
96: When `output.usage` is present in a Waterfall result, it reports `total_usd`, counts and costs by category, and `balance_remaining_usd`. For an asynchronous job, retrieve the result before reading its cost. [Usage Tracking](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/inline-usage.md) explains the fields. Count each job once when totaling costs; prices in example responses are illustrative, not a price list.
97: ### Am I charged when nothing is found?
98: Waterfall billing rules differ by endpoint. [Phone Enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/phone-enrichment-launcher.md) charges only when a number is returned. [Email Verification](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/email-verifier.md) does not charge for results where `output.email.email_status` is `unknown`. For other operations, follow the endpoint's billing guidance, your agreed rates, and the result's [usage breakdown](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/inline-usage.md). [Contact our team](mailto:support@waterfall.io) to confirm how missing or partial results are charged in your planned workflow.
99: ### Can I track usage separately for teams or workflows?
100: Yes. Use a Waterfall master key to create labeled sub-keys for different integrations. Authenticate [Account Reporter](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/account-reporter-v2.md) with a sub-key to compare its `key_usage` with overall `account_usage`. Product prices are returned only to master-key requests. See [API key management](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/api-keys-overview.md) for creating keys and managing their request limits.
101: ### Can I set a spending cap for an agent?
102: Set the agent's authorized budget in your execution workflow. Waterfall's `output.usage` helps you track reported job costs, but a balance snapshot does not reserve money for requests already in flight. A sub-key's `per_interval` limits request rate, not dollars spent. See [Usage Tracking](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/inline-usage.md) before designing spending controls for parallel calls.
103: ### Can I process a list of records?
104: Yes. Your integration can process a list through individual Waterfall requests within your account's [rate limits](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/rate-limit.md). Contact Enrichment, Company Enrichment, Phone Enrichment, and Email Verification accept one subject per request. Search endpoints have their own result limits or pagination. See [CRM enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/crm-enrichment.md) for connecting results to a list of records.
105: ### Can Waterfall support higher request volumes?
106: Yes. The default for Prospector, Search, Enrichment, Job Change, and Email Verification is 50 requests per 60 seconds. It is not Waterfall's maximum capacity: we can support volumes more than 10 times higher with the right account and workflow configuration. Email [support@waterfall.io](mailto:support@waterfall.io) with your APIs and expected volume so we can agree on limits for your setup. Your integration must follow the limits configured for its key.
107: ### Which endpoints are in Preview?
108: Search Company and Company Titles are marked Preview in these guides. Their behavior may change; discuss your requirements with our team before using them in a critical workflow. See their endpoint references for supported inputs and results.
109: ## Building an integration
110: ### Can Waterfall help build a custom data pipeline?
111: Yes. We can help you choose APIs, benchmark the fields your product needs, and build a custom data pipeline. Bring your starting inputs, required outputs, expected volume, and destination, such as a CRM, Snowflake, or a Clay table. Customers work directly with our founders in a dedicated channel to plan the integration and review results.
112: ### Can Waterfall work with Clay, Freckle, or Deepline?
113: Yes. Connect Waterfall to Clay, Freckle, or Deepline through an HTTP/API step or integration code to enrich leads, find contacts, and verify emails in your workflows. Requests use your Waterfall API key in the `x-api-key` header.
114: For Prospector and contact, phone, or company enrichment, include a `webhook_url` for a compatible receiver to get the completed result. If your setup cannot receive callbacks, save the returned `job_id` and retrieve the result through the matching Finder. Use `custom_fields` to carry your source record ID. Your workflow maps the returned fields and writes them back to the right record.
115: ### Which calls return results immediately?
116: Waterfall Search Contact, Search Company, Company Titles, Company Reveal, Job Change, and Email Verification return results in the response. Prospector, Contact Enrichment, Phone Enrichment, and Company Enrichment return a `job_id`; retrieve the completed result through the matching Finder or provide a supported `webhook_url`. See [Choose an API](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/introduction.md).
117: A synchronous [Contact Enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/contact-enrichment-launcher.md) option is also available by arrangement for enterprise customers. [Contact our team](mailto:support@waterfall.io) for access details.
118: ### Can I receive enrichment results without polling?
119: Yes. Waterfall Prospector, Contact Enrichment, Phone Enrichment, and Company Enrichment accept a `webhook_url`. Waterfall sends the Finder payload to that URL when processing completes. Your integration hosts the receiving endpoint and handles the delivery. Follow [Webhook Verification](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/webhook-verification.md) for checking signed deliveries, including the documented behavior when the signature header is absent.
120: ### Does a successful HTTP response mean enrichment found a match?
121: No. A successful Waterfall enrichment launch means the job was accepted. Inspect the job status, completed output, and the fields needed for your task. A completed request can still leave fields unavailable or produce no useful match. The [Quickstart](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/quickstart.md) and Finder pages explain how to retrieve results.
122: ### How do I connect enrichment results to my own records?
123: Use `custom_fields` on supported Waterfall requests to pass your CRM record ID, signup ID, or another source label. Waterfall returns that metadata in `input.task.custom_fields` on job retrieval. Keep the returned `job_id` with the source record too. See [CRM enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/crm-enrichment.md) for an example.
124: ### Can I use Waterfall with ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Grok Bot, or Cursor?
125: Yes. ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Claude Code, [Grok Bot by xAI](https://x.ai/news/introducing-grok-bot), and Cursor can use Waterfall's API documentation to help plan and build integrations. Follow [Build an integration](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/skills-integration.md) to create reusable code. To run live lookups, the agent needs HTTP-capable code or tool execution and an authorized Waterfall API key.
126: ### What does an agent need to run a Waterfall lookup?
127: To [run a lookup](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/skills-direct-api.md), the agent needs an environment that can make HTTP requests and an authorized Waterfall API key. Give it the [published OpenAPI file](https://waterfall-io-public.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/api_specs.yaml), the relevant endpoint reference, and your task, starting inputs, required fields, and criteria for a useful result. [Choose an API](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/introduction.md) helps you select the reference.
128: Store the authorized API key in the agent's execution environment rather than in its prompt. Define the records, actions, and budget allowed for live calls, which follow your account's usage and billing terms. Have the agent retrieve the completed output and check it against your criteria before claiming a match. [Skills](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/skills-overview.md) provide optional request and integration guidance; installing them does not provide API access.
129: ### Will Waterfall overwrite fields in my CRM?
130: Waterfall returns data through the API. Your integration controls which CRM fields to update, whether to replace an existing value, and how to handle missing results. Set those rules before writing results back to your CRM. See the [CRM enrichment workflow](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/crm-enrichment.md) for a starting point.
131: This documentation is built and hosted on [Mintlify](https://mintlify.com), a developer documentation platform.

1: > ## Documentation Index
2: > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.waterfall.io/llms.txt
3: > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
4: # Evaluate Waterfall
5: > Compare Waterfall on your own inputs: useful results, accurate matches, freshness, and actual cost. Get help planning the test and building your data pipeline.
6: Evaluate Waterfall on the job you need the data to do. A useful result matches the right person or company and includes the fields you need for your next step.
7: We've spent five years benchmarking data vendors and refining our methodology. We also offer [benchmarking as a service](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/book-demo.md) if you'd like us to run the evaluation.
8: ## 1. Define a useful result
9: Choose a workflow and its [API](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/introduction.md):
10: * **Replace a provider:** compare what you keep, gain, or lose across your usual records.
11: * **Fill gaps:** test records your current provider leaves unresolved. This measures additional coverage, not the match rate across your whole database.
12: * **Build a new workflow:** check whether the fields support the action you want to take.
13: For signup routing, that might mean the right person, company, and role. For prospecting, it means someone at the target account who fits your role filters and has the contact details you need. Set required fields, an acceptable error rate, a completion-time target, and a spending limit before testing.
14: ## 2. Use a representative sample
15: Use authorized inputs from your real workflow, including common and difficult records. Cover your target countries, roles, and company sizes. Review professional and personal emails separately, along with different identifiers and previously unresolved records.
16: Compare providers using the same inputs and criteria. Record settings and dates, and report unsupported inputs separately. Looking up known people and discovering people through search are different tests; use the path you plan to build.
17: ## 3. Review identity before counting fields
18: Check identity first. A complete profile for the wrong person is still a wrong match, even if its email is deliverable.
19: | Outcome | Meaning |
20: | - | - |
21: | Correct and useful | Right entity; required fields meet your criteria. |
22: | Correct but incomplete | Right entity; a required field is missing or unsuitable. |
23: | Incorrect match | A different person or company. |
24: | No result | Completed request with no matching record. |
25: | Unresolved | Not enough evidence to judge. |
26: | Technical failure | Request did not complete successfully. |
27: Keep recent, independent evidence and its review date. Your CRM or current provider can be outdated too; disagreement alone does not show which result is wrong.
28: ## 4. Measure the fields you will use
29: For **one-person or one-company lookups**, divide inputs with a correct, useful result by all attempted inputs. For field coverage, divide inputs with the right entity and a usable value for that field by all attempted inputs. Count each input once.
30: For **search**, measure the share of returned records that meet your criteria. For account prospecting, also measure target accounts with at least one useful contact divided by all target accounts. Keep contact and account counts separate. Show counts alongside percentages and split results by input type and segment.
31: Freshness depends on the fact: the employer may be right while the title is outdated. A working mailbox does not prove current employment. Request timestamps describe processing, not when each fact was verified. Compare verification status meanings across providers, not just labels.
32: ## 5. Measure cost per useful result
33: Read completed results' `output.usage` and record actual charges, including optional phone enrichment or separate verification. Count each job's cost once, regardless of retrievals. Compare the same required outputs across providers. Use a consistent result unit: resolved inputs for lookups or useful contacts for prospecting.
34: ```text theme={null}
35: Cost per useful result = total evaluation cost / correct and useful results
36: ```
37: With zero useful results, report the spend and zero results. See [Usage Tracking](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/inline-usage.md).
38: For a second provider filling gaps:
39: ```text theme={null}
40: Incremental coverage = newly resolved input records meeting your criteria / previously unresolved input records
41: ```
42: Report this second pass's cost separately. Use unique input records and count each once; duplicates are not additional coverage.
43: ## 6. Check the whole workflow
44: Start small. Measure time to a usable result, including asynchronous completion and retrieval; a successful launch is not a completed lookup. Check slow jobs, record matching, empty results, and failures.
45: For agents, check endpoint selection and accurate answers, including when the data is insufficient. Keep some examples aside to check prompt or integration changes.
46: ## Share a reviewable result
47: Save dates, sample size and segments, settings, criteria, outcome counts, completion times, and cost. State which workflow and inputs the results cover.
48: ## Can Waterfall help structure an evaluation?
49: Yes. We help structure tests, review results, and build custom data pipelines. Bring your workflow, inputs, required fields, and the gaps you want to solve. [Talk to our team](mailto:support@waterfall.io) about a test plan, API access, and pricing, or start with the [Quickstart](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/quickstart.md).
50: This documentation is built and hosted on [Mintlify](https://mintlify.com), a developer documentation platform.

4: # API Keys Management
5: > Create and manage separate API keys for teams, environments, and integrations.
6: Use a Waterfall master API key to create, list, and modify sub-keys for your account. Separate keys let you track usage by team, environment, or integration and manage each key's active status and request rate limit.
7: > [!NOTE]
8: >
9: > These operations require a master API key. Contact your account manager if you need key management enabled for your account.
10: ## Available operations
11: | Operation | Endpoint | Use it to |
12: | - | - | - |
13: | [List keys](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/api-keys-list.md) | `GET /v1/api-keys` | Review keys and their current settings. |
14: | [Create a key](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/api-keys-create.md) | `POST /v1/api-keys` | Add a sub-key with a label and request rate limit. |
15: | [Modify a key](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/api-keys-modify.md) | `PUT /v1/api-keys` | Update a sub-key's label, active status, or request rate limit. |
16: Authenticate these requests with your master key in `x-api-key`. The master key cannot be modified through these endpoints.
17: ## Track usage by integration
18: Give each sub-key a clear `notes` label, such as `crm-production` or `signup-enrichment`. Authenticate [Account Reporter](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/account-reporter-v2.md) with that key to compare its `key_usage` with overall `account_usage`.
19: `per_interval` controls requests per 60-second interval. It is a request rate limit, not a spending limit. A sub-key's value cannot exceed the master key's limit.

4: # Use Waterfall with an agent

6: Use an agent to look up contact and company data, verify emails, or build Waterfall into your application. Waterfall provides two skills: one for making API calls during a task, and one for creating integration code you maintain.
7: ## What do you want to do?
8: | Your goal | Skill | Start here |
9: | - | - | - |
10: | Retrieve data for a lookup, sample, or current task | `waterfall-direct-api` guides API calls over HTTP. | [Run a lookup](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/skills-direct-api.md) |
11: | Add Waterfall to an application or recurring workflow | `waterfall-integration` guides the creation of code in your own repository. | [Build an integration](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/skills-integration.md) |
12: The skills install independently. Choose the one that matches your task.
13: ## Give your agent a clear task
14: Specify the inputs you have, the fields you need, and the number of records to process. State whether you need phone enrichment, which can add charges. Ask the agent to preserve missing results instead of filling gaps with guesses.
15: Use [Choose an API](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/introduction.md) to match the task to a capability. For example, a known signup email starts with Contact Enrichment. Finding people at a target account may need Prospector. Search Contact returns profiles without emails or phones.
16: ## API access and results
17: A skill supplies instructions for the agent. Live API calls still require an authorized Waterfall API key and follow your account's usage and billing terms. Installing a skill does not create an account or provide API access.
18: Keep the key in your execution environment. See [Authentication](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/authentication.md) for access and [Usage Tracking](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/inline-usage.md) for returned costs. The result may be incomplete or empty; check the fields needed for your task.
19: ## Get the current skills
20: The [Waterfall API Skills repository](https://github.com/Waterfall-io/api-skills) contains both skills and their installation instructions. The guides above include the command for each skill.
21: The endpoint references and [OpenAPI specification](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/openapi-spec.md) define the API contract. If a skill's guidance conflicts with the current docs, follow the docs. Browse [use cases](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/overview.md) for workflow examples or the [FAQ](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/faq.md) for product questions.
