1: # Waterfall.io API Documentation
2: > One GTM API to find prospects, enrich contacts and companies, verify emails, and check job changes. Explore use cases and API references.
3: - [Waterfall API introduction](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/introduction.md): Explore Waterfall's APIs and compare their inputs, results, and use cases to choose the right endpoint for your workflow.
4: - [Enrich your first contact](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/quickstart.md): Make your first Waterfall API request: submit an email address, save the job ID, and retrieve the contact enrichment result.
5: - [Authentication](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/authentication.md): Get access to the Waterfall API, send your API key in the x-api-key header, and manage keys for separate workflows.
6: - [Rate limits](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/rate-limit.md): Plan Waterfall API request volume, handle HTTP 429 responses, and use Retry-After when polling or processing batches.
7: - [Errors](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/errors.md): Resolve Waterfall API validation, authentication, quota, rate-limit, and job errors using HTTP status and machine-readable error codes.
8: - [Usage Tracking](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/inline-usage.md): Read Waterfall per-job costs and balance snapshots from output.usage, and compare usage across a date range with Account Reporter.
9: - [Webhook Verification](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/webhook-verification.md): Verify Waterfall webhook deliveries using Ed25519 signatures.
10: - [Prospector Launcher](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-launcher.md): Find contacts at a target company by role, with verified emails and optional phone enrichment.
11: - [Prospector Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-finder.md): Retrieve prospector results and job status using the job_id returned at launch.
12: - [Prospector title filter](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-title-filter.md): How to build boolean expressions for `title_filter`.
13: - [Prospector multiple title filters](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-multiple-title-filters.md): Try up to five groups of job titles in priority order when finding contacts at a company.
14: - [Prospector location filter](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-location-filter.md): How location_country, location_countries, and location_name work.
15: - [Search Contact Launcher](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/search-contact-launcher.md): Find professional profiles by LinkedIn, company, role, location, or hiring date, without email or phone enrichment.
16: - [Search Contact Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/search-contact-finder.md): Retrieve a previous contact search with its original filters and profile results.
17: - [Search Contact filters](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/search-contact-filters.md): Filter contact searches by role, department, seniority, location, company criteria, and hiring date.
18: - [Search Company Launcher](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/search-company-launcher.md): Discover companies by industry, country, and employee size, with paginated company profiles.
19: - [Search Company Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/search-company-finder.md): Retrieve a previous company search with its original filters and company results.
20: - [Contact Enrichment Launcher](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/contact-enrichment-launcher.md): Enrich a known contact from a work or personal email, LinkedIn profile, or name and company domain.
21: - [Contact Enrichment Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/contact-enrichment-finder.md): Retrieve contact enrichment results and job status using the job_id returned at launch.
22: - [Phone Enrichment Launcher](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/phone-enrichment-launcher.md): Find phone numbers for a known contact using LinkedIn, email, or name and company domain.
23: - [Phone Enrichment Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/phone-enrichment-finder.md): Retrieve phone enrichment results and job status using the job_id returned at launch.
24: - [Company Enrichment Launcher](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/company-enrichment-launcher.md): Add company profile data to a known account using its domain, LinkedIn profile, or name.
25: - [Company Enrichment Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/company-enrichment-finder.md): Retrieve company enrichment results and job status using the job_id returned at launch.
26: - [Job Change Launcher](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/job-change-launcher.md): Check whether a known contact has moved to another company, left a company, or stayed in place.
27: - [Job Change Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/job-change-finder.md): Retrieve a previous job change check and interpret moved, left, no_change, or unknown results.
28: - [Company Reveal Launcher](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/company-reveal-launcher.md): Look up company information associated with an IPv4 address, with IP location and confidence fields.
29: - [Company Reveal Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/company-reveal-finder.md): Retrieve a previous IPv4-to-company lookup using its job_id.
30: - [Company Titles Launcher](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/company-titles-launcher.md): List job titles associated with a company before choosing roles for a contact search.
31: - [Company Titles Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/company-titles-finder.md): Retrieve a previous company title list with the pagination and raw title mode used at launch.
32: - [Email Verifier](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/email-verifier.md): Check an existing email address and receive a valid, invalid, risky, or unknown result in one call.

Start with a company domain, LinkedIn profile, or company name. Available output includes headcount, industry, headquarters, description, founding year, and LinkedIn data. 7: For a workflow that fills missing account fields, see [CRM enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/crm-enrichment.md). 8: > [!NOTE] 9: > 10: > This is an asynchronous endpoint. Use the returned `job_id` with [Company Enrichment Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/company-enrichment-finder.md), or pass `webhook_url` to receive the result when the job completes. 11: ## Choose an identifier 12: | Identifier | Field | Guidance | 13: | - | - | - | 14: | Domain | `domain` | Accepts a domain or full URL; Waterfall extracts the domain. | 15: | LinkedIn | `linkedin` | Use the company profile URL or slug. | 16: | Company name | `name` | Use when a domain or LinkedIn profile is unavailable. | 17: > [!WARNING] 18: > 19: > Name-based enrichment has a higher risk of matching the wrong company. Prefer a domain or LinkedIn identifier when available. 20: ## Example request 21: ```json theme={null} 22: { 23: "domain": "waterfall.io", 24: "custom_fields": { 25: "account_id": "acct_8821" 26: } 27: } 28: ``` 29: ## Company Enrichment or Search Company 30: Company Enrichment starts with a company you already know. Use [Search Company](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/search-company-launcher.md) to discover companies by industry, location, or size. Use [Company Reveal](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/company-reveal-launcher.md) when your starting input is an IPv4 address. 31: ## Retrieve results 32: Call [Company Enrichment Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/company-enrichment-finder.md) with the returned `job_id`. Check the returned company before updating your records; individual fields may be unavailable. When `output.usage` is present, it contains the job's cost breakdown. 33: ## OpenAPI 34: ````yaml api_specs.yaml POST /v1/enrichment/company 35: openapi: 3.1.0 36: info: 37: title: Waterfall 38: version: 1.7.0 39: description: >- 40: Waterfall API provides a broad set of capabilities in V1. Most endpoints are 41: asynchronous: you start a job (POST) and then retrieve results (GET). Some 42: endpoints return immediate responses. Webhooks are also available to 43: simplify asynchronous integrations. Below is an overview of the available 44: endpoints: 45: #### 1\. Prospector 46: Find contacts at target accounts using filters like job titles and location. 47: Get contact details such as titles, real-time verified emails, social 48: profiles, and phone numbers. 49: - **Prospector Launcher:** Start a contact search using a domain name, 50: LinkedIn profile, or company name. Returns a `job_id`. 51: - **Prospector Finder:** Retrieve results using the `job_id` from the 52: Prospector Launcher. 53: #### 2\. Contact Enrichment 54: Enrich contact information by inputting professional/personal emails, 55: LinkedIn URL/slug, or name + domain. Get enriched data like verified emails, 56: job titles, and locations. 57: - **Contact Enrichment Launcher**: Start a contact enrichment process. 58: Returns a `job_id`. 59: - **Contact Enrichment Finder**: Retrieve results using the `job_id` from 60: the Contact Enrichment Launcher. 61: #### 3\. Company Enrichment 62: Enrich company data by inputting a domain, LinkedIn URL/slug, or company 63: name. Receive details like headcount, industry, and headquarters. 64: - **Company Enrichment Launcher**: Start a company search using a domain 65: name, LinkedIn URL/slug, or company name. Returns a `job_id`. 66: - **Company Enrichment Finder**: Retrieve results using the `job_id` from 67: the Company Enrichment Launcher. 68: #### 4\. Phone Number Enrichment 69: Get mobile numbers by inputting an email, LinkedIn URL/slug, or name + 70: domain. 71: - **Phone Enrichment Launcher**: Start a phone number enrichment process. 72: Returns a `job_id`. 73: - **Phone Enrichment Finder**: Retrieve results using the `job_id` from the 74: Phone Enrichment Launcher. 75: #### 5\. Search Contact 76: Search contacts using either a specific contact LinkedIn, a specific 77: company, or company-set filters, with optional title, seniority, department, 78: location, and hiring-date constraints. 79: - **Search Contact Launcher**: Start a search contact job and get the result 80: payload. 81: - **Search Contact Finder**: Retrieve search contact job state and output by 82: `job_id`. 83: #### 6\. Search Company 84: Search companies by industry, country, and company size filters with 85: pagination support. 86: - **Search Company Launcher**: Start a search company job and get the result 87: payload. 88: - **Search Company Finder**: Retrieve search company job state and output by 89: `job_id`. 90: #### 7\. Job Change 91: Detect whether a contact has changed jobs using company and/or contact 92: identifiers. 93: - **Job Change Launcher**: Start a job change check and get the result 94: payload. 95: - **Job Change Finder**: Retrieve job change job state and output by 96: `job_id`. 97: #### 8\. Company Reveal 98: Reveal company information from an IPv4 address and retrieve persisted 99: reveal jobs by `job_id`. 100: - **Company Reveal Launcher**: Submit an IPv4 and get the reveal job 101: envelope immediately. 102: - **Company Reveal Finder**: Retrieve a persisted company reveal job state 103: and output by `job_id`. 104: #### 9\. Email Verification 105: Verify emails with high accuracy, reducing bounce rates. This endpoint works 106: asynchronously, providing results in a single API call. You can start an 107: email verification process and get the verification status of a given email. 108: #### 10\. Account Reporter 109: Provides information about your account's usage. 110: #### 11\. API Keys Management 111: Use a single master key to manage all your API keys: create new keys, 112: activate/deactivate them, and view all your keys in one place. See [API Keys 113: Management](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/api-keys-overview). 114: --- 115: # Versioning 116: Waterfall API versioning follows Semantic Versioning (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`): 117: - **Patch** (`1.1.x`): Non-breaking revisions and fixes only. No existing 118: contract changes. 119: - **Minor** (`1.x.0`, for example `1.2.0`): Backward-compatible additions. 120: Adding new services/endpoints uses a minor version increase when existing 121: services are unchanged. 122: - **Major** (`x.0.0`, for example `2.0.0`): Breaking changes to existing 123: contracts/behavior and major platform overhauls. 124: ## Endpoint Lifecycle Stages 125: Waterfall uses modern launch stages aligned with Google Cloud terminology: 126: - **Preview** 127: - Meaning: Early public version available for testing and feedback (equivalent to older Alpha/Beta phases). 128: - Production use: Not recommended for critical production workloads. 129: - SLA: No. 130: - Stability: API behavior may change. 131: - **GA (General Availability)** 132: - Meaning: Fully released and production-ready service or API. 133: - Production use: Yes. 134: - SLA: Yes. 135: - Stability: Backward compatibility is guaranteed within the version. 136: - **Deprecated** 137: - Meaning: Feature or API is scheduled for retirement and a newer alternative exists. 138: - Production use: Should migrate away. 139: - SLA: Limited. 140: - Stability: No new features; removal date announced. 141: - **Decommissioned / End of Life** 142: - Meaning: Feature or API has been shut down and is no longer available. 143: - Production use: No. 144: - SLA: No. 145: - Stability: Endpoint disabled or removed. 146: Current mapping in this API spec: all endpoints are `GA` except 147: `/v1/company-reveal`, `/v1/search/company`, `/v1/job/change`, and 148: `/v1/company-titles`, which are `Preview`. 149: --- 150: # Authentication 151: To access the API, you need the API key provided in your contract. You can 152: ask for multiple API keys for different teams' usage. 153: All API request URLs start with 154: [https://api.waterfall.io/v1/](https://api.waterfall.io/v1/). Provide your 155: API key in the `x-api-key` header. 156: --- 157: # Rate limit 158: The Prospector, Search, Enrichment, Job Change and Verify Email APIs allow a 159: maximum of 50 requests per minute (60 seconds). Should you encounter rate 160: limit errors or anticipate a need for increased capacity, please reach out 161: to your account manager for assistance. There are no rate limits for the 162: Account Reporter API. 163: ##### X-RateLimit-Limit 164: The maximum number of requests you can make per interval. Only sent when the 165: rate limit is reached. 166: ##### X-RateLimit-Interval 167: The length of the interval in seconds. Only sent when the rate limit is 168: reached. 169: ##### Retry-After 170: The number of seconds to wait until the rate limit window resets. Only sent 171: when the rate limit is reached. 172: --- 173: # Filters 174: Waterfall offers three filtering options for prospect requests: 175: ## 1. Title Filter 176: The `title_filter` parameter allows requesting specific titles with each 177: request. 178: - If `title_filter` is present, it must not be empty. 179: - If `title_filter` is present and not empty (for example `"title_filter": 180: "((accountant) OR (accounting)) AND NOT (intern)"`), Waterfall will use that 181: filter. 182: - If `title_filter` is not present, Waterfall will try 183: [title_filters](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-multiple-title-filters). 184: - At least one of `title_filter` or `title_filters` must be provided. 185: The filter can be any Boolean expression. Accepted operators are `AND`, 186: `OR`, and `NOT`. Operators must be uppercase and separated by spaces. 187: There is no need to enclose multi-word titles in parentheses. 188: Matching for each title is inclusive. For example: 189: - `manager` will match `program manager`, `senior manager` and `account 190: manager sales` 191: - `vp data` will match `vp innovation, data science, co-founder`, `vp 192: information and data` and `vp data science` 193: - `head product` will match `global head of product` and `head of product 194: management office` 195: - `data lead` will match `lead data scientist`, `data lead engineer`, `data 196: lead` and `data engineering lead` 197: A few valid filter examples: 198: - manager 199: - manager AND NOT project manager 200: - manager AND NOT (project manager OR sales manager) 201: - ( (manager OR director) AND (sales OR marketing) ) AND NOT ( project 202: manager OR sales manager) 203: - (accountant OR accounting) AND NOT intern 204: - ( (ceo) OR (c.e.o) OR (co-ceo) OR (coceo) OR (chief executive officer) OR 205: (founder) OR (co-founder) OR (cofounder) OR (owner) OR (co-owner) OR 206: (coowner) OR (cmo) OR (c.m.o) OR (chief marketing officer) OR (cco) OR 207: (c.c.o) OR (chief commercial officer) OR (chief e-commerce officer) OR 208: (chief ecommerce officer) ) OR ( ( (chief) OR (cheffe) OR (director) OR (vp) 209: OR (svp) OR (vice) OR (president) OR (vicepresident) OR (executive) OR 210: (head) ) AND ( (marketing) OR (growth) OR (e-commerce) OR (ecommerce) ) AND 211: NOT ( (assistant) OR (analyst) OR (intern) OR (apprenticeship) OR (sales) OR 212: (finance) OR (recruitment) OR (project manager) OR (hr) OR (human resources) 213: OR (talent) OR (design) OR (logistic) OR (warehouse) OR (engineer) OR 214: (developer) OR (student) OR (merchandising) OR (digital) OR (brand) OR 215: (trade) OR (influencer) OR (export) OR (wholesale) OR (whole sale) OR 216: (information) OR (specialist) ) ) 217: A few invalid filter examples: 218: - `mangerANDdirector`: spaces must be used around operators 219: - `manager NOT (project manager)`: invalid boolean expression 220: - `(accountant OR accounting AND NOT intern`: missing closing parenthesis 221: before AND 222: We recommend using parentheses to make sure operator precedence is what you 223: intend. 224: For example filter `(CFO) OR (Cofounder) AND NOT ((Vice) OR (Assistant) OR 225: (Executive Assistant))` will match title `Assistant CFO.` The Boolean 226: expression is `True OR False AND NOT True` and is evaluated as `True OR 227: False AND NOT True = True OR False AND False = True OR False = True` 228: In this case, the intended filter is `((CFO) OR (Cofounder)) AND NOT ((Vice) 229: OR (Assistant) OR (Executive Assistant))`. Note the extra parenthesis around 230: the first part. 231: If you need help with writing title filters, contact your account manager to 232: schedule a call with the support team. 233: --- 234: ## 2. Multiple Title Filters 235: The `title_filters` parameter allows requesting multiple title filters in a 236: specific order. It is used when 237: [title_filter](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-title-filter) 238: is not present. 239: Example: 240: ``` json 241: "title_filters": [ 242: { 243: "name": "ceo level", 244: "filter": "ceo OR founder OR owner" 245: }, 246: { 247: "name": "sales", 248: "filter": "revenue OR growth OR sales" 249: }, 250: { 251: "name": "marketing or operations", 252: "filter": "marketing OR operations" 253: } 254: ] 255: ``` 256: Waterfall will try each filter in the order provided up to the requested 257: `limit`. 258: You can provide up to 5 `title_filters` entries per request. 259: --- 260: ## 3. Location Filter 261: The location-based search is performed with `location_name`, 262: `location_country`, and `location_countries`. 263: #### location_country 264: The `location_country` parameter represents the country of the contact's 265: current address. Use full country names such as `United States` or `France`. 266: Partial values such as `United` or `Saudi` should be avoided. The country 267: list is available 268: [here](https://waterfall-io-public.s3.amazonaws.com/waterfall_location_country.txt). 269: Empty values are ignored. 270: #### location_countries 271: The `location_countries` parameter is a list of countries where the 272: contact's current address can be. If it is present and non-empty, it is used 273: instead of `location_country`. 274: - \["France"\] 275: - \["France", "Germany"\] 276: You can provide up to 50 countries. The full list is available 277: [here](https://waterfall-io-public.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/waterfall_location_country.txt). 278: #### location_name 279: The `location_name` parameter represents the location of the contact's 280: current address. Typical locations are: 281: - `San Francisco, California, United States` 282: - `Paris, Ile-De-France, France` 283: A location can include city, region/state, and country. Partial matches are 284: possible. Common partial formats are: 285: - city, region: `San Francisco, California`, `Paris, Ile-De-France` 286: - region, country: `California, United States`, `Ile-De-France, France` 287: - city: `San Francisco`, `Paris` 288: - region: `California`, `Ile-De-France` 289: - country:`United States`, `France` 290: In many cases, the best results are obtained using only the region. 291: Empty values are ignored. 292: --- 293: # Errors 294: The waterfall API uses conventional HTTP response codes to indicate the 295: success or failure of a request, with detailed information in case of error. 296: Error payload structure: 297: - `category` is the high-level classification (`AUTH`, `VALIDATION`, 298: `NOT_FOUND`, etc.). 299: - `code` is the stable machine-readable identifier for a specific failure 300: case. 301: - Every `code` is namespaced by category using the format `CATEGORY_DETAIL` 302: (for example `VALIDATION_BAD_REQUEST`). 303: - The `category` field must always match the prefix of the `code` field. 304: - Use `category` for broad handling (retry/auth/permissions) and `code` for 305: precise logic and analytics. 306: | Status Code | Description | 307: | --- | --- | 308: | 200 OK | The request was successful. | 309: | 400 Bad Request | Your request was not valid. | 310: | 401 Unauthorized | Missing API key. | 311: | 403 Forbidden | Bad API key. | 312: | 404 Not Found | The requested endpoint does not exist. | 313: | 500 Internal Server Error | Something went wrong on our end. | 314: --- 315: # Contact Support 316: Contact Support: Email: 317: [felix@waterfall.io](https://mailto:felix@waterfall.io) 318: termsOfService: https://www.waterfall.io/#FAQs 319: contact: 320: email: felix@waterfall.io 321: servers: 322: - sources.numbered_text: 1: > ## Documentation Index 2: > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.waterfall.io/llms.txt 3: > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further. 4: # Email Verifier 5: > Check an existing email address and receive a valid, invalid, risky, or unknown result in one call. 6: Use Waterfall Email Verifier to check an email address you already have. It accepts work or personal email addresses and returns a verification result in one call. For finding a contact's email from a profile or name, use [Contact Enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/contact-enrichment-launcher.md). 7: > [!NOTE] 8: > 9: > This endpoint returns the result synchronously. Read `output.email.email_status` in the response. No separate Finder call is needed. 10: ## Example request 11: ```json theme={null} 12: { 13: "email": "jane.doe@example.com", 14: "custom_fields": { 15: "crm_id": "001ABC" 16: } 17: } 18: ``` 19: ## Interpret the result 20: | `email_status` | How to handle it | 21: | - | - | 22: | `valid` | The address passed verification. Use it according to your sending policy. | 23: | `invalid` | Exclude the address from sending. | 24: | `risky` | Keep separate from `valid` results and review against your sending policy. | 25: | `unknown` | Verification was inconclusive. Keep the address unresolved; a later check may return a result. | 26: The top-level `status` describes the API job. The email's verification outcome is in `output.email.email_status`. Do not treat `SUCCEEDED` as proof that an address is valid. 27: Email Verification results with `email_status: unknown` are not billed. 28: ## Use verification in your workflow 29: See [email verification before outreach](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/email-verification.md) for handling these outcomes. Verification does not guarantee delivery to the inbox. 30: Responses can include `output.usage`; see [usage tracking](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/inline-usage.md) for the cost breakdown. Person records returned by enrichment use a different field, `email_verified_status`, with a different set of values. 31: ## OpenAPI 32: ````yaml api_specs.yaml POST /v1/verify/email 33: openapi: 3.1.0 34: info: 35: title: Waterfall 36: version: 1.7.0 37: description: >- 38: Waterfall API provides a broad set of capabilities in V1. Most endpoints are 39: asynchronous: you start a job (POST) and then retrieve results (GET). Some 40: endpoints return immediate responses. Webhooks are also available to 41: simplify asynchronous integrations. Below is an overview of the available 42: endpoints: 43: #### 1\. Prospector 44: Find contacts at target accounts using filters like job titles and location. 45: Get contact details such as titles, real-time verified emails, social 46: profiles, and phone numbers. 47: - **Prospector Launcher:** Start a contact search using a domain name, 48: LinkedIn profile, or company name. Returns a `job_id`. 49: - **Prospector Finder:** Retrieve results using the `job_id` from the 50: Prospector Launcher. 51: #### 2\. Contact Enrichment 52: Enrich contact information by inputting professional/personal emails, 53: LinkedIn URL/slug, or name + domain. Get enriched data like verified emails, 54: job titles, and locations. 55: - **Contact Enrichment Launcher**: Start a contact enrichment process. 56: Returns a `job_id`. 57: - **Contact Enrichment Finder**: Retrieve results using the `job_id` from 58: the Contact Enrichment Launcher. 59: #### 3\. Company Enrichment 60: Enrich company data by inputting a domain, LinkedIn URL/slug, or company 61: name. Receive details like headcount, industry, and headquarters. 62: - **Company Enrichment Launcher**: Start a company search using a domain 63: name, LinkedIn URL/slug, or company name. Returns a `job_id`. 64: - **Company Enrichment Finder**: Retrieve results using the `job_id` from 65: the Company Enrichment Launcher. 66: #### 4\. Phone Number Enrichment 67: Get mobile numbers by inputting an email, LinkedIn URL/slug, or name + 68: domain. 69: - **Phone Enrichment Launcher**: Start a phone number enrichment process. 70: Returns a `job_id`. 71: - **Phone Enrichment Finder**: Retrieve results using the `job_id` from the 72: Phone Enrichment Launcher. 73: #### 5\. Search Contact 74: Search contacts using either a specific contact LinkedIn, a specific 75: company, or company-set filters, with optional title, seniority, department, 76: location, and hiring-date constraints. 77: - **Search Contact Launcher**: Start a search contact job and get the result 78: payload. 79: - **Search Contact Finder**: Retrieve search contact job state and output by 80: `job_id`. 81: #### 6\. Search Company 82: Search companies by industry, country, and company size filters with 83: pagination support. 84: - **Search Company Launcher**: Start a search company job and get the result 85: payload. 86: - **Search Company Finder**: Retrieve search company job state and output by 87: `job_id`. 88: #### 7\. Job Change 89: Detect whether a contact has changed jobs using company and/or contact 90: identifiers. 91: - **Job Change Launcher**: Start a job change check and get the result 92: payload. 93: - **Job Change Finder**: Retrieve job change job state and output by 94: `job_id`. 95: #### 8\. Company Reveal 96: Reveal company information from an IPv4 address and retrieve persisted 97: reveal jobs by `job_id`. 98: - **Company Reveal Launcher**: Submit an IPv4 and get the reveal job 99: envelope immediately. 100: - **Company Reveal Finder**: Retrieve a persisted company reveal job state 101: and output by `job_id`. 102: #### 9\. Email Verification 103: Verify emails with high accuracy, reducing bounce rates. This endpoint works 104: asynchronously, providing results in a single API call. You can start an 105: email verification process and get the verification status of a given email. 106: #### 10\. Account Reporter 107: Provides information about your account's usage. 108: #### 11\. API Keys Management 109: Use a single master key to manage all your API keys: create new keys, 110: activate/deactivate them, and view all your keys in one place. See [API Keys 111: Management](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/api-keys-overview). 112: --- 113: # Versioning 114: Waterfall API versioning follows Semantic Versioning (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`): 115: - **Patch** (`1.1.x`): Non-breaking revisions and fixes only. No existing 116: contract changes. 117: - **Minor** (`1.x.0`, for example `1.2.0`): Backward-compatible additions. 118: Adding new services/endpoints uses a minor version increase when existing 119: services are unchanged. 120: - **Major** (`x.0.0`, for example `2.0.0`): Breaking changes to existing 121: contracts/behavior and major platform overhauls. 122: ## Endpoint Lifecycle Stages 123: Waterfall uses modern launch stages aligned with Google Cloud terminology: 124: - **Preview** 125: - Meaning: Early public version available for testing and feedback (equivalent to older Alpha/Beta phases). 126: - Production use: Not recommended for critical production workloads. 127: - SLA: No. 128: - Stability: API behavior may change. 129: - **GA (General Availability)** 130: - Meaning: Fully released and production-ready service or API. 131: - Production use: Yes. 132: - SLA: Yes. 133: - Stability: Backward compatibility is guaranteed within the version. 134: - **Deprecated** 135: - Meaning: Feature or API is scheduled for retirement and a newer alternative exists. 136: - Production use: Should migrate away. 137: - SLA: Limited. 138: - Stability: No new features; removal date announced. 139: - **Decommissioned / End of Life** 140: - Meaning: Feature or API has been shut down and is no longer available. 141: - Production use: No. 142: - SLA: No. 143: - Stability: Endpoint disabled or removed. 144: Current mapping in this API spec: all endpoints are `GA` except 145: `/v1/company-reveal`, `/v1/search/company`, `/v1/job/change`, and 146: `/v1/company-titles`, which are `Preview`. 147: --- 148: # Authentication 149: To access the API, you need the API key provided in your contract. You can 150: ask for multiple API keys for different teams' usage. 151: All API request URLs start with 152: [https://api.waterfall.io/v1/](https://api.waterfall.io/v1/). Provide your 153: API key in the `x-api-key` header. 154: --- 155: # Rate limit 156: The Prospector, Search, Enrichment, Job Change and Verify Email APIs allow a 157: maximum of 50 requests per minute (60 seconds). Should you encounter rate 158: limit errors or anticipate a need for increased capacity, please reach out 159: to your account manager for assistance. There are no rate limits for the 160: Account Reporter API. 161: ##### X-RateLimit-Limit 162: The maximum number of requests you can make per interval. Only sent when the 163: rate limit is reached. 164: ##### X-RateLimit-Interval 165: The length of the interval in seconds. Only sent when the rate limit is 166: reached. 167: ##### Retry-After 168: The number of seconds to wait until the rate limit window resets. Only sent 169: when the rate limit is reached. 170: --- 171: # Filters 172: Waterfall offers three filtering options for prospect requests: 173: ## 1. Title Filter 174: The `title_filter` parameter allows requesting specific titles with each 175: request. 176: - If `title_filter` is present, it must not be empty. 177: - If `title_filter` is present and not empty (for example `"title_filter": 178: "((accountant) OR (accounting)) AND NOT (intern)"`), Waterfall will use that 179: filter. 180: - If `title_filter` is not present, Waterfall will try 181: [title_filters](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-multiple-title-filters). 182: - At least one of `title_filter` or `title_filters` must be provided. 183: The filter can be any Boolean expression. Accepted operators are `AND`, 184: `OR`, and `NOT`. Operators must be uppercase and separated by spaces. 185: There is no need to enclose multi-word titles in parentheses. 186: Matching for each title is inclusive. For example: 187: - `manager` will match `program manager`, `senior manager` and `account 188: manager sales` 189: - `vp data` will match `vp innovation, data science, co-founder`, `vp 190: information and data` and `vp data science` 191: - `head product` will match `global head of product` and `head of product 192: management office` 193: - `data lead` will match `lead data scientist`, `data lead engineer`, `data 194: lead` and `data engineering lead` 195: A few valid filter examples: 196: - manager 197: - manager AND NOT project manager 198: - manager AND NOT (project manager OR sales manager) 199: - ( (manager OR director) AND (sales OR marketing) ) AND NOT ( project 200: manager OR sales manager) 201: - (accountant OR accounting) AND NOT intern 202: - ( (ceo) OR (c.e.o) OR (co-ceo) OR (coceo) OR (chief executive officer) OR 203: (founder) OR (co-founder) OR (cofounder) OR (owner) OR (co-owner) OR 204: (coowner) OR (cmo) OR (c.m.o) OR (chief marketing officer) OR (cco) OR 205: (c.c.o) OR (chief commercial officer) OR (chief e-commerce officer) OR 206: (chief ecommerce officer) ) OR ( ( (chief) OR (cheffe) OR (director) OR (vp) 207: OR (svp) OR (vice) OR (president) OR (vicepresident) OR (executive) OR 208: (head) ) AND ( (marketing) OR (growth) OR (e-commerce) OR (ecommerce) ) AND 209: NOT ( (assistant) OR (analyst) OR (intern) OR (apprenticeship) OR (sales) OR 210: (finance) OR (recruitment) OR (project manager) OR (hr) OR (human resources) 211: OR (talent) OR (design) OR (logistic) OR (warehouse) OR (engineer) OR 212: (developer) OR (student) OR (merchandising) OR (digital) OR (brand) OR 213: (trade) OR (influencer) OR (export) OR (wholesale) OR (whole sale) OR 214: (information) OR (specialist) ) ) 215: A few invalid filter examples: 216: - `mangerANDdirector`: spaces must be used around operators 217: - `manager NOT (project manager)`: invalid boolean expression 218: - `(accountant OR accounting AND NOT intern`: missing closing parenthesis 219: before AND 220: We recommend using parentheses to make sure operator precedence is what you 221: intend. 222: For example filter `(CFO) OR (Cofounder) AND NOT ((Vice) OR (Assistant) OR 223: (Executive Assistant))` will match title `Assistant CFO.` The Boolean 224: expression is `True OR False AND NOT True` and is evaluated as `True OR 225: False AND NOT True = True OR False AND False = True OR False = True` 226: In this case, the intended filter is `((CFO) OR (Cofounder)) AND NOT ((Vice) 227: OR (Assistant) OR (Executive Assistant))`. Note the extra parenthesis around 228: the first part. 229: If you need help with writing title filters, contact your account manager to 230: schedule a call with the support team. 231: --- 232: ## 2. Multiple Title Filters 233: The `title_filters` parameter allows requesting multiple title filters in a 234: specific order. It is used when 235: [title_filter](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-title-filter) 236: is not present. 237: Example: 238: ``` json 239: "title_filters": [ 240: { 241: "name": "ceo level", 242: "filter": "ceo OR founder OR owner" 243: }, 244: { 245: "name": "sales", 246: "filter": "revenue OR growth OR sales" 247: }, 248: { 249: "name": "marketing or operations", 250: "filter": "marketing OR operations" 251: } 252: ] 253: ``` 254: Waterfall will try each filter in the order provided up to the requested 255: `limit`. 256: You can provide up to 5 `title_filters` entries per request. 257: --- 258: ## 3. Location Filter 259: The location-based search is performed with `location_name`, 260: `location_country`, and `location_countries`. 261: #### location_country 262: The `location_country` parameter represents the country of the contact's 263: current address. Use full country names such as `United States` or `France`. 264: Partial values such as `United` or `Saudi` should be avoided. The country 265: list is available 266: [here](https://waterfall-io-public.s3.amazonaws.com/waterfall_location_country.txt). 267: Empty values are ignored. 268: #### location_countries 269: The `location_countries` parameter is a list of countries where the 270: contact's current address can be. If it is present and non-empty, it is used 271: instead of `location_country`. 272: - \["France"\] 273: - \["France", "Germany"\] 274: You can provide up to 50 countries. The full list is available 275: [here](https://waterfall-io-public.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/waterfall_location_country.txt). 276: #### location_name 277: The `location_name` parameter represents the location of the contact's 278: current address. Typical locations are: 279: - `San Francisco, California, United States` 280: - `Paris, Ile-De-France, France` 281: A location can include city, region/state, and country. Partial matches are 282: possible. Common partial formats are: 283: - city, region: `San Francisco, California`, `Paris, Ile-De-France` 284: - region, country: `California, United States`, `Ile-De-France, France` 285: - city: `San Francisco`, `Paris` 286: - region: `California`, `Ile-De-France` 287: - country:`United States`, `France` 288: In many cases, the best results are obtained using only the region. 289: Empty values are ignored. 290: --- 291: # Errors 292: The waterfall API uses conventional HTTP response codes to indicate the 293: success or failure of a request, with detailed information in case of error. 294: Error payload structure: 295: - `category` is the high-level classification (`AUTH`, `VALIDATION`, 296: `NOT_FOUND`, etc.). 297: - `code` is the stable machine-readable identifier for a specific failure 298: case. 299: - Every `code` is namespaced by category using the format `CATEGORY_DETAIL` 300: (for example `VALIDATION_BAD_REQUEST`). 301: - The `category` field must always match the prefix of the `code` field. 302: - Use `category` for broad handling (retry/auth/permissions) and `code` for 303: precise logic and analytics. 304: | Status Code | Description | 305: | --- | --- | 306: | 200 OK | The request was successful. | 307: | 400 Bad Request | Your request was not valid. | 308: | 401 Unauthorized | Missing API key. | 309: | 403 Forbidden | Bad API key. | 310: | 404 Not Found | The requested endpoint does not exist. | 311: | 500 Internal Server Error | Something went wrong on our end. | 312: --- 313: # Contact Support 314: Contact Support: Email: 315: [felix@waterfall.io](https://mailto:felix@waterfall.io) 316: termsOfService: https://www.waterfall.io/#FAQs 317: contact: 318: email: felix@waterfall.io 319: servers: 320: - sources.numbered_text: 1: > ## Documentation Index 2: > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.waterfall.io/llms.txt 3: > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further. 4: # Company Reveal Launcher 5: > Look up company information associated with an IPv4 address, with IP location and confidence fields. 6: Use Waterfall Company Reveal when your starting input is an IPv4 address and you want company context. The response can include a company profile, an organization type, IP geolocation, and a confidence label. 7: ## How it works 8: Company Reveal returns the result synchronously. Read `output` in the response; no separate polling step is required. Use the job identifier in `input.task.job_id` with [Company Reveal Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/company-reveal-finder.md) to retrieve the stored result. 9: ## Example request 10: ```json theme={null} 11: { 12: "ip": "8.8.8.8", 13: "custom_fields": { 14: "session_id": "abc123" 15: } 16: } 17: ``` 18: This illustrates the request format; it does not establish which company will be returned for that address. 19: ## Assess the result 20: * `output.type` can be `company`, `education`, `government`, `isp`, or `null`. An ISP result is not proof of a visitor's employer. 21: * `output.confidence_score` can be `very_high`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, or `null`. These are labels, not percentage probabilities. 22: * `output.company` can be empty. Check that it contains the company data your workflow needs. 23: * `output.ip_geo` describes the IP's location context. It does not identify an individual visitor or establish the company's headquarters. 24: ## Choose the next step 25: See [website company identification](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/website-company-identification.md) for a workflow that uses this result. If you already have a company domain, use [Company Enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/company-enrichment-launcher.md) directly. 26: ## OpenAPI 27: ````yaml api_specs.yaml POST /v1/company-reveal 28: openapi: 3.1.0 29: info: 30: title: Waterfall 31: version: 1.7.0 32: description: >- 33: Waterfall API provides a broad set of capabilities in V1. Most endpoints are 34: asynchronous: you start a job (POST) and then retrieve results (GET). Some 35: endpoints return immediate responses. Webhooks are also available to 36: simplify asynchronous integrations. Below is an overview of the available 37: endpoints: 38: #### 1\. Prospector 39: Find contacts at target accounts using filters like job titles and location. 40: Get contact details such as titles, real-time verified emails, social 41: profiles, and phone numbers. 42: - **Prospector Launcher:** Start a contact search using a domain name, 43: LinkedIn profile, or company name. Returns a `job_id`. 44: - **Prospector Finder:** Retrieve results using the `job_id` from the 45: Prospector Launcher. 46: #### 2\. Contact Enrichment 47: Enrich contact information by inputting professional/personal emails, 48: LinkedIn URL/slug, or name + domain. Get enriched data like verified emails, 49: job titles, and locations. 50: - **Contact Enrichment Launcher**: Start a contact enrichment process. 51: Returns a `job_id`. 52: - **Contact Enrichment Finder**: Retrieve results using the `job_id` from 53: the Contact Enrichment Launcher. 54: #### 3\. Company Enrichment 55: Enrich company data by inputting a domain, LinkedIn URL/slug, or company 56: name. Receive details like headcount, industry, and headquarters. 57: - **Company Enrichment Launcher**: Start a company search using a domain 58: name, LinkedIn URL/slug, or company name. Returns a `job_id`. 59: - **Company Enrichment Finder**: Retrieve results using the `job_id` from 60: the Company Enrichment Launcher. 61: #### 4\. Phone Number Enrichment 62: Get mobile numbers by inputting an email, LinkedIn URL/slug, or name + 63: domain. 64: - **Phone Enrichment Launcher**: Start a phone number enrichment process. 65: Returns a `job_id`. 66: - **Phone Enrichment Finder**: Retrieve results using the `job_id` from the 67: Phone Enrichment Launcher. 68: #### 5\. Search Contact 69: Search contacts using either a specific contact LinkedIn, a specific 70: company, or company-set filters, with optional title, seniority, department, 71: location, and hiring-date constraints. 72: - **Search Contact Launcher**: Start a search contact job and get the result 73: payload. 74: - **Search Contact Finder**: Retrieve search contact job state and output by 75: `job_id`. 76: #### 6\. Search Company 77: Search companies by industry, country, and company size filters with 78: pagination support. 79: - **Search Company Launcher**: Start a search company job and get the result 80: payload. 81: - **Search Company Finder**: Retrieve search company job state and output by 82: `job_id`. 83: #### 7\. Job Change 84: Detect whether a contact has changed jobs using company and/or contact 85: identifiers. 86: - **Job Change Launcher**: Start a job change check and get the result 87: payload. 88: - **Job Change Finder**: Retrieve job change job state and output by 89: `job_id`. 90: #### 8\. Company Reveal 91: Reveal company information from an IPv4 address and retrieve persisted 92: reveal jobs by `job_id`. 93: - **Company Reveal Launcher**: Submit an IPv4 and get the reveal job 94: envelope immediately. 95: - **Company Reveal Finder**: Retrieve a persisted company reveal job state 96: and output by `job_id`. 97: #### 9\. Email Verification 98: Verify emails with high accuracy, reducing bounce rates. This endpoint works 99: asynchronously, providing results in a single API call. You can start an 100: email verification process and get the verification status of a given email. 101: #### 10\. Account Reporter 102: Provides information about your account's usage. 103: #### 11\. API Keys Management 104: Use a single master key to manage all your API keys: create new keys, 105: activate/deactivate them, and view all your keys in one place. See [API Keys 106: Management](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/api-keys-overview). 107: --- 108: # Versioning 109: Waterfall API versioning follows Semantic Versioning (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`): 110: - **Patch** (`1.1.x`): Non-breaking revisions and fixes only. No existing 111: contract changes. 112: - **Minor** (`1.x.0`, for example `1.2.0`): Backward-compatible additions. 113: Adding new services/endpoints uses a minor version increase when existing 114: services are unchanged. 115: - **Major** (`x.0.0`, for example `2.0.0`): Breaking changes to existing 116: contracts/behavior and major platform overhauls. 117: ## Endpoint Lifecycle Stages 118: Waterfall uses modern launch stages aligned with Google Cloud terminology: 119: - **Preview** 120: - Meaning: Early public version available for testing and feedback (equivalent to older Alpha/Beta phases). 121: - Production use: Not recommended for critical production workloads. 122: - SLA: No. 123: - Stability: API behavior may change. 124: - **GA (General Availability)** 125: - Meaning: Fully released and production-ready service or API. 126: - Production use: Yes. 127: - SLA: Yes. 128: - Stability: Backward compatibility is guaranteed within the version. 129: - **Deprecated** 130: - Meaning: Feature or API is scheduled for retirement and a newer alternative exists. 131: - Production use: Should migrate away. 132: - SLA: Limited. 133: - Stability: No new features; removal date announced. 134: - **Decommissioned / End of Life** 135: - Meaning: Feature or API has been shut down and is no longer available. 136: - Production use: No. 137: - SLA: No. 138: - Stability: Endpoint disabled or removed. 139: Current mapping in this API spec: all endpoints are `GA` except 140: `/v1/company-reveal`, `/v1/search/company`, `/v1/job/change`, and 141: `/v1/company-titles`, which are `Preview`. 142: --- 143: # Authentication 144: To access the API, you need the API key provided in your contract. You can 145: ask for multiple API keys for different teams' usage. 146: All API request URLs start with 147: [https://api.waterfall.io/v1/](https://api.waterfall.io/v1/). Provide your 148: API key in the `x-api-key` header. 149: --- 150: # Rate limit 151: The Prospector, Search, Enrichment, Job Change and Verify Email APIs allow a 152: maximum of 50 requests per minute (60 seconds). Should you encounter rate 153: limit errors or anticipate a need for increased capacity, please reach out 154: to your account manager for assistance. There are no rate limits for the 155: Account Reporter API. 156: ##### X-RateLimit-Limit 157: The maximum number of requests you can make per interval. Only sent when the 158: rate limit is reached. 159: ##### X-RateLimit-Interval 160: The length of the interval in seconds. Only sent when the rate limit is 161: reached. 162: ##### Retry-After 163: The number of seconds to wait until the rate limit window resets. Only sent 164: when the rate limit is reached. 165: --- 166: # Filters 167: Waterfall offers three filtering options for prospect requests: 168: ## 1. Title Filter 169: The `title_filter` parameter allows requesting specific titles with each 170: request. 171: - If `title_filter` is present, it must not be empty. 172: - If `title_filter` is present and not empty (for example `"title_filter": 173: "((accountant) OR (accounting)) AND NOT (intern)"`), Waterfall will use that 174: filter. 175: - If `title_filter` is not present, Waterfall will try 176: [title_filters](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-multiple-title-filters). 177: - At least one of `title_filter` or `title_filters` must be provided. 178: The filter can be any Boolean expression. Accepted operators are `AND`, 179: `OR`, and `NOT`. Operators must be uppercase and separated by spaces. 180: There is no need to enclose multi-word titles in parentheses. 181: Matching for each title is inclusive. For example: 182: - `manager` will match `program manager`, `senior manager` and `account 183: manager sales` 184: - `vp data` will match `vp innovation, data science, co-founder`, `vp 185: information and data` and `vp data science` 186: - `head product` will match `global head of product` and `head of product 187: management office` 188: - `data lead` will match `lead data scientist`, `data lead engineer`, `data 189: lead` and `data engineering lead` 190: A few valid filter examples: 191: - manager 192: - manager AND NOT project manager 193: - manager AND NOT (project manager OR sales manager) 194: - ( (manager OR director) AND (sales OR marketing) ) AND NOT ( project 195: manager OR sales manager) 196: - (accountant OR accounting) AND NOT intern 197: - ( (ceo) OR (c.e.o) OR (co-ceo) OR (coceo) OR (chief executive officer) OR 198: (founder) OR (co-founder) OR (cofounder) OR (owner) OR (co-owner) OR 199: (coowner) OR (cmo) OR (c.m.o) OR (chief marketing officer) OR (cco) OR 200: (c.c.o) OR (chief commercial officer) OR (chief e-commerce officer) OR 201: (chief ecommerce officer) ) OR ( ( (chief) OR (cheffe) OR (director) OR (vp) 202: OR (svp) OR (vice) OR (president) OR (vicepresident) OR (executive) OR 203: (head) ) AND ( (marketing) OR (growth) OR (e-commerce) OR (ecommerce) ) AND 204: NOT ( (assistant) OR (analyst) OR (intern) OR (apprenticeship) OR (sales) OR 205: (finance) OR (recruitment) OR (project manager) OR (hr) OR (human resources) 206: OR (talent) OR (design) OR (logistic) OR (warehouse) OR (engineer) OR 207: (developer) OR (student) OR (merchandising) OR (digital) OR (brand) OR 208: (trade) OR (influencer) OR (export) OR (wholesale) OR (whole sale) OR 209: (information) OR (specialist) ) ) 210: A few invalid filter examples: 211: - `mangerANDdirector`: spaces must be used around operators 212: - `manager NOT (project manager)`: invalid boolean expression 213: - `(accountant OR accounting AND NOT intern`: missing closing parenthesis 214: before AND 215: We recommend using parentheses to make sure operator precedence is what you 216: intend. 217: For example filter `(CFO) OR (Cofounder) AND NOT ((Vice) OR (Assistant) OR 218: (Executive Assistant))` will match title `Assistant CFO.` The Boolean 219: expression is `True OR False AND NOT True` and is evaluated as `True OR 220: False AND NOT True = True OR False AND False = True OR False = True` 221: In this case, the intended filter is `((CFO) OR (Cofounder)) AND NOT ((Vice) 222: OR (Assistant) OR (Executive Assistant))`. Note the extra parenthesis around 223: the first part. 224: If you need help with writing title filters, contact your account manager to 225: schedule a call with the support team. 226: --- 227: ## 2. Multiple Title Filters 228: The `title_filters` parameter allows requesting multiple title filters in a 229: specific order. It is used when 230: [title_filter](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-title-filter) 231: is not present. 232: Example: 233: ``` json 234: "title_filters": [ 235: { 236: "name": "ceo level", 237: "filter": "ceo OR founder OR owner" 238: }, 239: { 240: "name": "sales", 241: "filter": "revenue OR growth OR sales" 242: }, 243: { 244: "name": "marketing or operations", 245: "filter": "marketing OR operations" 246: } 247: ] 248: ``` 249: Waterfall will try each filter in the order provided up to the requested 250: `limit`. 251: You can provide up to 5 `title_filters` entries per request. 252: --- 253: ## 3. Location Filter 254: The location-based search is performed with `location_name`, 255: `location_country`, and `location_countries`. 256: #### location_country 257: The `location_country` parameter represents the country of the contact's 258: current address. Use full country names such as `United States` or `France`. 259: Partial values such as `United` or `Saudi` should be avoided. The country 260: list is available 261: [here](https://waterfall-io-public.s3.amazonaws.com/waterfall_location_country.txt). 262: Empty values are ignored. 263: #### location_countries 264: The `location_countries` parameter is a list of countries where the 265: contact's current address can be. If it is present and non-empty, it is used 266: instead of `location_country`. 267: - \["France"\] 268: - \["France", "Germany"\] 269: You can provide up to 50 countries. The full list is available 270: [here](https://waterfall-io-public.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/waterfall_location_country.txt). 271: #### location_name 272: The `location_name` parameter represents the location of the contact's 273: current address. Typical locations are: 274: - `San Francisco, California, United States` 275: - `Paris, Ile-De-France, France` 276: A location can include city, region/state, and country. Partial matches are 277: possible. Common partial formats are: 278: - city, region: `San Francisco, California`, `Paris, Ile-De-France` 279: - region, country: `California, United States`, `Ile-De-France, France` 280: - city: `San Francisco`, `Paris` 281: - region: `California`, `Ile-De-France` 282: - country:`United States`, `France` 283: In many cases, the best results are obtained using only the region. 284: Empty values are ignored. 285: --- 286: # Errors 287: The waterfall API uses conventional HTTP response codes to indicate the 288: success or failure of a request, with detailed information in case of error. 289: Error payload structure: 290: - `category` is the high-level classification (`AUTH`, `VALIDATION`, 291: `NOT_FOUND`, etc.). 292: - `code` is the stable machine-readable identifier for a specific failure 293: case. 294: - Every `code` is namespaced by category using the format `CATEGORY_DETAIL` 295: (for example `VALIDATION_BAD_REQUEST`). 296: - The `category` field must always match the prefix of the `code` field. 297: - Use `category` for broad handling (retry/auth/permissions) and `code` for 298: precise logic and analytics. 299: | Status Code | Description | 300: | --- | --- | sources.numbered_text: 1: > ## Documentation Index 2: > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.waterfall.io/llms.txt 3: > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further. 4: # Job Change Launcher 5: > Check whether a known contact has moved to another company, left a company, or stayed in place. 6: Use Waterfall Job Change to check whether a contact's company information has changed. This helps you review CRM records and reconnect with contacts who have moved. Each request checks one contact; your application controls when to run the next check. 7: > [!NOTE] 8: > 9: > Job Change returns its result synchronously. Read `output.job_change_status` in the response. Use [Job Change Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/job-change-finder.md) to retrieve a previous result by `job_id`. 10: ## Supported inputs 11: | Starting information | Supported combination | 12: | - | - | 13: | Company domain and a contact | `company_domain` plus `contact_linkedin`, `professional_email`, `personal_email`, or `contact_full_name` | 14: | Company LinkedIn and a contact | `company_linkedin` plus `contact_linkedin`, `professional_email`, or `personal_email` | 15: | Professional email | `professional_email`, optionally with `contact_full_name` | 16: A personal email or a name alone is not a supported input combination. Use the field names above; the contact LinkedIn field is `contact_linkedin`. 17: ## Example request 18: ```json theme={null} 19: { 20: "company_domain": "waterfall.io", 21: "contact_linkedin": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/jane-doe/", 22: "custom_fields": { 23: "crm_id": "001ABC" 24: } 25: } 26: ``` 27: ## Read the result 28: The outcome is `moved`, `left`, `no_change`, or `unknown`. An `unknown` result does not establish that the contact still works at the original company. See [Job Change Finder](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/job-change-finder.md) for result handling and [the job change workflow](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/use-cases/job-changes.md) for using these checks with your CRM. 29: Returned profile data has email and phone channels redacted. Use [Contact Enrichment](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/contact-enrichment-launcher.md) when you need contact channels for a matched person. 30: ## OpenAPI 31: ````yaml api_specs.yaml POST /v1/job/change 32: openapi: 3.1.0 33: info: 34: title: Waterfall 35: version: 1.7.0 36: description: >- 37: Waterfall API provides a broad set of capabilities in V1. Most endpoints are 38: asynchronous: you start a job (POST) and then retrieve results (GET). Some 39: endpoints return immediate responses. Webhooks are also available to 40: simplify asynchronous integrations. Below is an overview of the available 41: endpoints: 42: #### 1\. Prospector 43: Find contacts at target accounts using filters like job titles and location. 44: Get contact details such as titles, real-time verified emails, social 45: profiles, and phone numbers. 46: - **Prospector Launcher:** Start a contact search using a domain name, 47: LinkedIn profile, or company name. Returns a `job_id`. 48: - **Prospector Finder:** Retrieve results using the `job_id` from the 49: Prospector Launcher. 50: #### 2\. Contact Enrichment 51: Enrich contact information by inputting professional/personal emails, 52: LinkedIn URL/slug, or name + domain. Get enriched data like verified emails, 53: job titles, and locations. 54: - **Contact Enrichment Launcher**: Start a contact enrichment process. 55: Returns a `job_id`. 56: - **Contact Enrichment Finder**: Retrieve results using the `job_id` from 57: the Contact Enrichment Launcher. 58: #### 3\. Company Enrichment 59: Enrich company data by inputting a domain, LinkedIn URL/slug, or company 60: name. Receive details like headcount, industry, and headquarters. 61: - **Company Enrichment Launcher**: Start a company search using a domain 62: name, LinkedIn URL/slug, or company name. Returns a `job_id`. 63: - **Company Enrichment Finder**: Retrieve results using the `job_id` from 64: the Company Enrichment Launcher. 65: #### 4\. Phone Number Enrichment 66: Get mobile numbers by inputting an email, LinkedIn URL/slug, or name + 67: domain. 68: - **Phone Enrichment Launcher**: Start a phone number enrichment process. 69: Returns a `job_id`. 70: - **Phone Enrichment Finder**: Retrieve results using the `job_id` from the 71: Phone Enrichment Launcher. 72: #### 5\. Search Contact 73: Search contacts using either a specific contact LinkedIn, a specific 74: company, or company-set filters, with optional title, seniority, department, 75: location, and hiring-date constraints. 76: - **Search Contact Launcher**: Start a search contact job and get the result 77: payload. 78: - **Search Contact Finder**: Retrieve search contact job state and output by 79: `job_id`. 80: #### 6\. Search Company 81: Search companies by industry, country, and company size filters with 82: pagination support. 83: - **Search Company Launcher**: Start a search company job and get the result 84: payload. 85: - **Search Company Finder**: Retrieve search company job state and output by 86: `job_id`. 87: #### 7\. Job Change 88: Detect whether a contact has changed jobs using company and/or contact 89: identifiers. 90: - **Job Change Launcher**: Start a job change check and get the result 91: payload. 92: - **Job Change Finder**: Retrieve job change job state and output by 93: `job_id`. 94: #### 8\. Company Reveal 95: Reveal company information from an IPv4 address and retrieve persisted 96: reveal jobs by `job_id`. 97: - **Company Reveal Launcher**: Submit an IPv4 and get the reveal job 98: envelope immediately. 99: - **Company Reveal Finder**: Retrieve a persisted company reveal job state 100: and output by `job_id`. 101: #### 9\. Email Verification 102: Verify emails with high accuracy, reducing bounce rates. This endpoint works 103: asynchronously, providing results in a single API call. You can start an 104: email verification process and get the verification status of a given email. 105: #### 10\. Account Reporter 106: Provides information about your account's usage. 107: #### 11\. API Keys Management 108: Use a single master key to manage all your API keys: create new keys, 109: activate/deactivate them, and view all your keys in one place. See [API Keys 110: Management](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/api-keys-overview). 111: --- 112: # Versioning 113: Waterfall API versioning follows Semantic Versioning (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`): 114: - **Patch** (`1.1.x`): Non-breaking revisions and fixes only. No existing 115: contract changes. 116: - **Minor** (`1.x.0`, for example `1.2.0`): Backward-compatible additions. 117: Adding new services/endpoints uses a minor version increase when existing 118: services are unchanged. 119: - **Major** (`x.0.0`, for example `2.0.0`): Breaking changes to existing 120: contracts/behavior and major platform overhauls. 121: ## Endpoint Lifecycle Stages 122: Waterfall uses modern launch stages aligned with Google Cloud terminology: 123: - **Preview** 124: - Meaning: Early public version available for testing and feedback (equivalent to older Alpha/Beta phases). 125: - Production use: Not recommended for critical production workloads. 126: - SLA: No. 127: - Stability: API behavior may change. 128: - **GA (General Availability)** 129: - Meaning: Fully released and production-ready service or API. 130: - Production use: Yes. 131: - SLA: Yes. 132: - Stability: Backward compatibility is guaranteed within the version. 133: - **Deprecated** 134: - Meaning: Feature or API is scheduled for retirement and a newer alternative exists. 135: - Production use: Should migrate away. 136: - SLA: Limited. 137: - Stability: No new features; removal date announced. 138: - **Decommissioned / End of Life** 139: - Meaning: Feature or API has been shut down and is no longer available. 140: - Production use: No. 141: - SLA: No. 142: - Stability: Endpoint disabled or removed. 143: Current mapping in this API spec: all endpoints are `GA` except 144: `/v1/company-reveal`, `/v1/search/company`, `/v1/job/change`, and 145: `/v1/company-titles`, which are `Preview`. 146: --- 147: # Authentication 148: To access the API, you need the API key provided in your contract. You can 149: ask for multiple API keys for different teams' usage. 150: All API request URLs start with 151: [https://api.waterfall.io/v1/](https://api.waterfall.io/v1/). Provide your 152: API key in the `x-api-key` header. 153: --- 154: # Rate limit 155: The Prospector, Search, Enrichment, Job Change and Verify Email APIs allow a 156: maximum of 50 requests per minute (60 seconds). Should you encounter rate 157: limit errors or anticipate a need for increased capacity, please reach out 158: to your account manager for assistance. There are no rate limits for the 159: Account Reporter API. 160: ##### X-RateLimit-Limit 161: The maximum number of requests you can make per interval. Only sent when the 162: rate limit is reached. 163: ##### X-RateLimit-Interval 164: The length of the interval in seconds. Only sent when the rate limit is 165: reached. 166: ##### Retry-After 167: The number of seconds to wait until the rate limit window resets. Only sent 168: when the rate limit is reached. 169: --- 170: # Filters 171: Waterfall offers three filtering options for prospect requests: 172: ## 1. Title Filter 173: The `title_filter` parameter allows requesting specific titles with each 174: request. 175: - If `title_filter` is present, it must not be empty. 176: - If `title_filter` is present and not empty (for example `"title_filter": 177: "((accountant) OR (accounting)) AND NOT (intern)"`), Waterfall will use that 178: filter. 179: - If `title_filter` is not present, Waterfall will try 180: [title_filters](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-multiple-title-filters). 181: - At least one of `title_filter` or `title_filters` must be provided. 182: The filter can be any Boolean expression. Accepted operators are `AND`, 183: `OR`, and `NOT`. Operators must be uppercase and separated by spaces. 184: There is no need to enclose multi-word titles in parentheses. 185: Matching for each title is inclusive. For example: 186: - `manager` will match `program manager`, `senior manager` and `account 187: manager sales` 188: - `vp data` will match `vp innovation, data science, co-founder`, `vp 189: information and data` and `vp data science` 190: - `head product` will match `global head of product` and `head of product 191: management office` 192: - `data lead` will match `lead data scientist`, `data lead engineer`, `data 193: lead` and `data engineering lead` 194: A few valid filter examples: 195: - manager 196: - manager AND NOT project manager 197: - manager AND NOT (project manager OR sales manager) 198: - ( (manager OR director) AND (sales OR marketing) ) AND NOT ( project 199: manager OR sales manager) 200: - (accountant OR accounting) AND NOT intern 201: - ( (ceo) OR (c.e.o) OR (co-ceo) OR (coceo) OR (chief executive officer) OR 202: (founder) OR (co-founder) OR (cofounder) OR (owner) OR (co-owner) OR 203: (coowner) OR (cmo) OR (c.m.o) OR (chief marketing officer) OR (cco) OR 204: (c.c.o) OR (chief commercial officer) OR (chief e-commerce officer) OR 205: (chief ecommerce officer) ) OR ( ( (chief) OR (cheffe) OR (director) OR (vp) 206: OR (svp) OR (vice) OR (president) OR (vicepresident) OR (executive) OR 207: (head) ) AND ( (marketing) OR (growth) OR (e-commerce) OR (ecommerce) ) AND 208: NOT ( (assistant) OR (analyst) OR (intern) OR (apprenticeship) OR (sales) OR 209: (finance) OR (recruitment) OR (project manager) OR (hr) OR (human resources) 210: OR (talent) OR (design) OR (logistic) OR (warehouse) OR (engineer) OR 211: (developer) OR (student) OR (merchandising) OR (digital) OR (brand) OR 212: (trade) OR (influencer) OR (export) OR (wholesale) OR (whole sale) OR 213: (information) OR (specialist) ) ) 214: A few invalid filter examples: 215: - `mangerANDdirector`: spaces must be used around operators 216: - `manager NOT (project manager)`: invalid boolean expression 217: - `(accountant OR accounting AND NOT intern`: missing closing parenthesis 218: before AND 219: We recommend using parentheses to make sure operator precedence is what you 220: intend. 221: For example filter `(CFO) OR (Cofounder) AND NOT ((Vice) OR (Assistant) OR 222: (Executive Assistant))` will match title `Assistant CFO.` The Boolean 223: expression is `True OR False AND NOT True` and is evaluated as `True OR 224: False AND NOT True = True OR False AND False = True OR False = True` 225: In this case, the intended filter is `((CFO) OR (Cofounder)) AND NOT ((Vice) 226: OR (Assistant) OR (Executive Assistant))`. Note the extra parenthesis around 227: the first part. 228: If you need help with writing title filters, contact your account manager to 229: schedule a call with the support team. 230: --- 231: ## 2. Multiple Title Filters 232: The `title_filters` parameter allows requesting multiple title filters in a 233: specific order. It is used when 234: [title_filter](https://docs.waterfall.io/v1/prospector-title-filter) 235: is not present. 236: Example: 237: ``` json 238: "title_filters": [ 239: { 240: "name": "ceo level", 241: "filter": "ceo OR founder OR owner" 242: }, 243: { 244: "name": "sales", 245: "filter": "revenue OR growth OR sales" 246: }, 247: { 248: "name": "marketing or operations", 249: "filter": "marketing OR operations" 250: } 251: ] 252: ``` 253: Waterfall will try each filter in the order provided up to the requested 254: `limit`. 255: You can provide up to 5 `title_filters` entries per request. 256: --- 257: ## 3. Location Filter 258: The location-based search is performed with `location_name`, 259: `location_country`, and `location_countries`. 260: #### location_country 261: The `location_country` parameter represents the country of the contact's 262: current address. Use full country names such as `United States` or `France`. 263: Partial values such as `United` or `Saudi` should be avoided. The country 264: list is available 265: [here](https://waterfall-io-public.s3.amazonaws.com/waterfall_location_country.txt). 266: Empty values are ignored. 267: #### location_countries 268: The `location_countries` parameter is a list of countries where the 269: contact's current address can be. If it is present and non-empty, it is used 270: instead of `location_country`. 271: - \["France"\] 272: - \["France", "Germany"\] 273: You can provide up to 50 countries. The full list is available 274: [here](https://waterfall-io-public.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/waterfall_location_country.txt). 275: #### location_name 276: The `location_name` parameter represents the location of the contact's 277: current address. Typical locations are: 278: - `San Francisco, California, United States` 279: - `Paris, Ile-De-France, France` 280: A location can include city, region/state, and country. Partial matches are 281: possible. Common partial formats are: 282: - city, region: `San Francisco, California`, `Paris, Ile-De-France` 283: - region, country: `California, United States`, `Ile-De-France, France` 284: - city: `San Francisco`, `Paris` 285: - region: `California`, `Ile-De-France` 286: - country:`United States`, `France` 287: In many cases, the best results are obtained using only the region. 288: Empty values are ignored. 289: --- 290: # Errors 291: The waterfall API uses conventional HTTP response codes to indicate the 292: success or failure of a request, with detailed information in case of error. 293: Error payload structure: 294: - `category` is the high-level classification (`AUTH`, `VALIDATION`, 295: `NOT_FOUND`, etc.). 296: - `code` is the stable machine-readable identifier for a specific failure 297: case. 298: - Every `code` is namespaced by category using the format `CATEGORY_DETAIL` 299: (for example `VALIDATION_BAD_REQUEST`). 300: - The `category` field must always match the prefix of the `code` field. 301: - Use `category` for broad handling (retry/auth/permissions) and `code` for 302: precise logic and analytics. 303: | Status Code | Description | 304: | --- | --- | 305: | 200 OK | The request was successful. | 306: | 400 Bad Request | Your request was not valid. | 307: | 401 Unauthorized | Missing API key. | 308: | 403 Forbidden | Bad API key. | 309: | 404 Not Found | The requested endpoint does not exist. | 310: | 500 Internal Server Error | Something went wrong on our end. | 311: --- 312: # Contact Support 313: Contact Support: Email: 314: [felix@waterfall.io](https://mailto:felix@waterfall.io) 315: termsOfService: https://www.waterfall.io/#FAQs 316: contact: 317: email: felix@waterfall.io 318: servers: 319: -
