evidence.observation: quote: ## Basics

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: - **Base URL:** `https://api.ahrefs.com/v3/{tool}/{endpoint}` (for example `https://api.ahrefs.com/v3/site-explorer/domain-rating`).

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: - **Authentication:** send your API key as a bearer token in the `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` header. Free "public" endpoints do not require a key. See [API keys creation and management](/api/docs/api-keys-creation-and-management.md).

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: - **Requests:** all data endpoints are `GET` with query-string parameters.

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: - **Responses:** JSON by default (`application/json`); most endpoints also support XML. Use the `output` parameter to choose the format.

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: - **Selecting fields:** most reports take a `select` parameter listing the columns to return; response cost depends on the rows and fields requested. See [Parameters](/api/docs/parameters.md).

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: - **Filtering:** rows can be filtered with a JSON filter expression via the `where` parameter. See [Filter syntax](/api/docs/filter-syntax.md).

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: Most requests consume **API units**; the minimum cost of any billable request is 50 units. Rank Tracker, Management, Public, and some other endpoints are free, and each tool's documentation marks free endpoints. During development, prefer the [free test queries](/api/docs/free-test-queries.md) to avoid spending units. See [Limits consumption](/api/docs/limits-consumption.md).

evidence.observation: quote: Monetary values across all endpoints (for example `value`, `org_cost`, `paid_cost`, `traffic_value`) are returned in **USD cents**. Divide by 100 to display dollars.

quote: "description": "The filter expression. The following column identifiers are recognized (this differs from the identifiers recognized by the `select` parameter).

**ahrefs_rank_source**: The strength of the referring domain's backlink profile compared to the other websites in our database, with rank #1 being the strongest. 
type: integer

**ahrefs_rank_target**: The strength of the target domain's backlink profile compared to the other websites in our database, with rank #1 being the strongest. 
type: integer

**alt**: The alt attribute of the link. 
type: string nullable

**anchor**: The clickable words in a link that point to a URL. 
type: string

**broken_redirect_new_target**: The new destination of a modified redirect. 
type: string nullable

**broken_redirect_reason**: The reason the redirect was considered broken during the last crawl. 
type: string nullable 
enum: `"droppedmanual"` `"droppedtooold"` `"dropped"` `"codechanged"` `"nxdomain"` `"robotsdisallowed"` `"curlerror"` `"invalidtarget"` `"nomorecanonical"` `"isnowparked"` `"targetchanged"`

**broken_redirect_source**: The redirecting URL that was modified, causing the redirect to become broken. 
type: string nullable

**class_c** (5 units): The number of unique class_c subnets linking to the referring page. 
type: integer

**discovered_status**: The reason the link was discovered during the last crawl: the page was crawled for the first time, the link was added to the page, or the link re-appeared after being removed. 
type: string nullable 
enum: `"pagefound"` `"linkfound"` `"linkrestored"`

**domain_rating_source**: The strength of the referring domain's backlink profile compared to the others in our database on a 100-point scale. 
type: float

**domain_rating_target**: The strength of the referring domain's backlink profile compared to the others in our database on a 100-point scale. 
type: float

**drop_reason**: The reason we removed the link from our index. 
type: string nullable 
enum: `"manual"` `"noratingunused"` `"notop"` `"tooold"` `"oldunavailable"` `"rescursive"` `"duplicate"` `"nxdomain"` `"malformed"` `"blockedport"` `"disallowed"` `"unlinked"` `"lowvalue"`

**encoding**: The character set encoding of the referring page HTML. 
type: string

**first_seen**: The date the referring page URL was first discovered. 
type: datetime

**first_seen_link**: The date we first found a backlink to your target on a given referring page. 
type: datetime

**http_code**: The return code from HTTP protocol returned during the referring page crawl. 
type: integer

**http_crawl**: The link was discovered without executing javascript and rendering the page. 
type: boolean

**ip_source**: The referring domain IP address. 
type: string nullable

**is_alternate**: The link with the rel=“alternate” attribute. 
type: boolean

**is_canonical**: The link with the rel=“canonical” attribute. 
type: boolean

**is_content**: The link was found in the biggest piece of content on the page. 
type: boolean

**is_dofollow**: The link has no special nofollow attribute. 
type: boolean

**is_form**: The link was found in a form HTML tag. 
type: boolean

**is_frame**: The link was found in an iframe HTML tag. 
type: boolean

**is_homepage_link**: The link was found on the homepage of a referring website. 
type: boolean

**is_image**: The link is a regular link that has an image inside their href attribute. 
type: boolean

**is_lost**: The link currently does not exist anymore. 
type: boolean

**is_new**: The link was discovered on the last crawl. 
type: boolean

**is_nofollow**: The link or the referring page has the nofollow attribute set. 
type: boolean

**is_non_html**: The link points to a URL with non-HTML content. 
type: boolean

**is_redirect**: The link pointing to your target via a redirect. 
type: boolean

**is_redirect_lost**: The redirected link currently does not exist anymore. 
type: boolean

**is_root_source**: The referring domain name is a root domain name. 
type: boolean

**is_root_target**: The target domain name is a root domain name. 
type: boolean

**is_rss**: The link was found in an RSS feed. 
type: boolean

**is_spam**: Indicates whether the backlink comes from a known spammy domain. 
type: boolean

**is_sponsored**: The link has the Sponsored attribute set in the referring page HTML. 
type: boolean

**is_text**: The link is a standard href hyperlink. 
type: boolean

**is_ugc**: The link has the User Generated Content attribute set in the referring page HTML. 
type: boolean

**js_crawl**: The link was discovered after executing javascript and rendering the page. 
type: boolean

**languages**: The languages listed in the referring page metadata or detected by the crawler to appear in the HTML. 
type: array(string)

**last_seen**: The date we discovered that the link was lost. 
type: datetime nullable

**last_visited**: The date we last verified a live link to your target page. 
type: datetime

**len_url_redirect**: The number of redirect chain URLs. 
type: integer

**link_group_count**: The number of backlinks that were grouped together based on the aggregation parameter. This field cannot be used with aggregation 'all'. 
type: integer

**link_type**: The kind of the backlink. 
type: string 
enum: `"redirect"` `"frame"` `"text"` `"form"` `"canonical"` `"alternate"` `"rss"` `"image"`

**linked_domains_source_domain**: The number of unique root domains linked from the referring domain. 
type: integer

**linked_domains_source_page**: The number of unique root domains linked from the referring page. 
type: integer

**linked_domains_target_domain**: The number of unique root domains linked from the target domain. 
type: integer

**links_external**: The number of external links from the referring page. 
type: integer

**links_internal**: The number of internal links from the referring page. 
type: integer

**lost_reason**: The reason the link was lost during the last crawl. 
type: string nullable 
enum: `"removedfromhtml"` `"notcanonical"` `"noindex"` `"pageredirected"` `"pageerror"` `"lostredirect"` `"notfound"`

**name_source**: The complete referring domain name, including subdomains. 
type: string

**name_target**: The complete target domain name, including subdomains. 
type: string

**noindex**: The referring page has the noindex meta attribute. 
type: boolean

**page_category_source**: Comma-separated list of AI-predicted hierarchical category paths for the referring page. Each value is a slash-prefixed path (e.g. /Business_and_Industrial/Advertising_and_Marketing/Marketing). See [Page type and category classifications](https://docs.ahrefs.com/api/docs/page-classifications) for the taxonomy and filtering examples. 
type: string nullable

**page_size**: The size in bytes of the referring page content.

**page_type_source**: Comma-separated list of AI-predicted hierarchical page type paths for the referring page. Each value is a slash-prefixed path (e.g. /Article/How_to). See [Page type and category classifications](https://docs.ahrefs.com/api/docs/page-classifications) for the taxonomy and filtering examples. 
type: string nullable

**port_source**: The network port of the referring page URL. 
type: integer

**port_target**: The network port of the target page URL. 
type: integer

**positions**: The number of keywords that the referring page ranks for in the top 100 positions. 
type: integer

**positions_source_domain**: The number of keywords that the referring domain ranks for in the top 100 positions. 
type: integer

**powered_by**: Web technologies used to build and serve the referring page content. 
type: array(string)

**redirect_code**: The HTTP status code of a referring page pointing to your target via a redirect. 
type: integer nullable

**redirect_kind**: The HTTP status codes returned by the target redirecting URL or redirect chain. 
type: array(integer)

**refdomains_source** (5 units): The number of unique referring domains linking to the referring page. 
type: integer

**refdomains_source_domain** (5 units): The number of unique referring domains linking to the referring domain. 
type: integer

**refdomains_target_domain** (5 units): The number of unique referring domains linking to the target domain. 
type: integer

**root_name_source**: The root domain name of the referring domain, not including subdomains. 
type: string

**root_name_target**: The root domain name of the target domain, not including subdomains. 
type: string

**snippet_left**: The snippet of text appearing just before the link. 
type: string

**snippet_right**: The snippet of text appearing just after the link. 
type: string

**source_page_author**: The author of the referring page. 
type: string nullable

**source_page_publish_date**: the date we identified the page was published 
type: date nullable

**title**: The html title of the referring page. 
type: string

**tld_class_source**: The top level domain class of the referring domain. 
type: string 
enum: `"gov"` `"edu"` `"normal"`

**tld_class_target**: The top level domain class of the target domain. 
type: string 
enum: `"gov"` `"edu"` `"normal"`

**traffic** (10 units): The referring page's estimated monthly organic traffic from Google. 
type: integer

**traffic_domain** (10 units): The referring domain's estimated monthly organic traffic from Google. 
type: integer

**url_from**: The URL of the page containing a link to your target. 
type: string

**url_from_plain**: The referring page URL optimized for use as a filter. 
type: string

**url_rating_source**: The strength of the referring page's backlink profile compared to the others in our database on a 100-point scale. 
type: float

**url_redirect**: A redirect chain the target URL of the link points to. 
type: array(url)

**url_redirect_with_target**: The target URL of the link with its redirect chain. 
type: array(string)

**url_to**: The URL the backlink points to. 
type: string

**url_to_plain**: The target page URL optimized for use as a filter. 
type: string",

type: integer

**http_code_target**: The return code from HTTP protocol returned during the target page crawl. 
type: integer nullable

**is_content**: The link was found in the biggest piece of content on the page. 
type: boolean

**is_dofollow**: The link has no special nofollow attribute. 
type: boolean

**is_homepage_link**: The link was found on the homepage of a referring website. 
type: boolean

**is_lost**: The link currently does not exist anymore. 
type: boolean

**is_new**: The link was discovered on the last crawl. 
type: boolean

**is_nofollow**: The link or the referring page has the nofollow attribute set. 
type: boolean

**is_non_html**: The link points to a URL with non-HTML content. 
type: boolean

**is_root_source**: The referring domain name is a root domain name. 
type: boolean

**is_spam**: Indicates whether the backlink comes from a known spammy domain. 
type: boolean

**is_sponsored**: The link has the Sponsored attribute set in the referring page HTML. 
type: boolean

**is_ugc**: The link has the User Generated Content attribute set in the referring page HTML. 
type: boolean

**languages_source**: The languages listed in the referring page metadata or detected by the crawler to appear in the HTML. 
type: array(string)

**languages_target**: The languages listed in the target page metadata or detected by the crawler to appear in the HTML. 
type: array(string)

**last_seen**: The date your target page lost its last live link. 
type: datetime nullable

**last_visited_source**: The date we last verified a live link to your target page. 
type: datetime

**last_visited_target**: The date we last crawled your target page. 
type: datetime nullable

**len_url_redirect**: The number of redirect chain URLs. 
type: integer

**link_type**: The kind of the backlink. 
type: string 
enum: `"redirect"` `"frame"` `"text"` `"form"` `"canonical"` `"alternate"` `"rss"` `"image"`

**linked_domains_source**: The number of unique root domains linked from the referring page.

**links_external_source**: The number of external links from the referring page. 
type: integer

**links_to_target**: The number of inbound backlinks the target page has. 
type: integer

**lost_links_to_target**: The number of backlinks lost during the selected time period. 
type: integer

**new_links_to_target**: The number of new backlinks found during the selected time period. 
type: integer

**nofollow_to_target**: The number of links to your target page that have the “nofollow” attribute. 
type: integer

Filter with substring and a quoted path to match an exact taxonomy key. Unclassified pages return null. type: integer

**positions_source_domain**: The number of keywords that the referring domain ranks for in the top 100 positions. 
type: integer

**powered_by_source**: Web technologies used to build and serve the referring page content. 
type: array(string)

**powered_by_target**: Web technologies used to build and serve the target page content. 
type: array(string)

**redirects_to_target**: The number of inbound redirects to your target page. 
type: integer

type: integer

**refdomains_target** (5 units): The number of unique referring domains linking to the target page. 
type: integer

**root_name_source**: The root domain name of the referring domain, not including subdomains.

**snippet_left**: The snippet of text appearing just before the link. 
type: string

**snippet_right**: The snippet of text appearing just after the link. 
type: string

**source_page_author**: The author of the referring page. 
type: string nullable

**target_redirect**: The target's redirect if any. 
type: string nullable

**title_source**: The html title of the referring page. 
type: string

**title_target**: The html title of the target page. 
type: string nullable

type: float

**traffic_domain_source** (10 units): The referring domain's estimated monthly organic traffic from Google. 
type: integer

**traffic_source** (10 units): The referring page's estimated monthly organic traffic from Google. 
type: integer

**url_from_plain**: The referring page URL optimized for use as a filter. 
type: string

**url_rating_source**: The strength of the referring page's backlink profile compared to the others in our database on a 100-point scale.

evidence.observation:
quote: "description": "`where` filters the visits by the report's dimensions, which changes the totals and the shares, and the rows by their metrics, which does not. On the dimensions, `isubstring` ignores the case and `eq`, `prefix` and `suffix` match it, but on `search_term`, which ignores it.

The fields `where` filters by:

**country**: The visitor's country: a two-letter country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). 
type: string

**channel**: The acquisition channel, as `traffic-channels` lists it. 
type: string

**source**: The source of the visit, as `traffic-sources` lists it. 
type: string

**referring_website**: The root domain of the website the visitor came from, as `traffic-referring-websites` lists it. Visits without such a referrer are left out. 
type: string

**referring_host**: The host of the page the visitor came from, without `www.`. 
type: string

**search_term**: The search term the visit came from. Case-insensitive; `phrase_match` matches whole words. Visits with an unknown search term are left out. 
type: string

**utm_source**: The UTM source of the visit. 
type: string

**utm_medium**: The UTM medium of the visit. 
type: string

**utm_campaign**: The UTM campaign of the visit. 
type: string

**utm_term**: The UTM term of the visit. 
type: string

**utm_content**: The UTM content of the visit. 
type: string

**landing_page**: The URL of the page the visit started on, as `traffic-landing-pages` lists it. 
type: string

**city**: The visitor's city, as `City, CC` with the country code, as `traffic-geography` lists it with `level=city`. 
type: string

**region**: The visitor's world region, as `traffic-geography` lists it with `level=region`. 
type: string

**continent**: The visitor's continent, as `traffic-geography` lists it with `level=continent`. 
type: string

**previous_page**: The page the visitor was on right before the visit, as `traffic-previous-pages` lists it. 
type: string

**referring_page**: The URL of the page the visitor came from, as `traffic-referring-pages` lists it. 
type: string

**page_type**: Only the pages of this page type: a subtype as `traffic-page-classifications` lists it with `classification=type` (`/Article/Recipe`, `/Article/-other`, `unclassified`) or a whole type (`/Article`). Takes `eq` only. See [Page type and category classifications](https://docs.ahrefs.com/api/docs/page-classifications) for the taxonomy. 
type: string

**page_intent**: Only the pages of this page intent, as `traffic-page-classifications` lists it with `classification=intent`. Takes `eq` only. 
type: string

**page_category**: Only the pages of this top-level page category, as `traffic-page-classifications` lists it with `classification=category`. Takes `eq` only. See [Page type and category classifications](https://docs.ahrefs.com/api/docs/page-classifications) for the taxonomy. 
type: string

**avg_time_on_page**: The estimated average time from a view of the page to the next page view of the same visit, in seconds. 
type: integer nullable

**entry_bounce_rate**: The estimated share of the visits that started on the page and viewed a single page, as a percent. 
type: float nullable

**entry_pages_per_visit**: The estimated number of page views per visit, over the visits that started on the page. 
type: float nullable

**entry_visit_duration**: The estimated average duration, in seconds, of the visits that started on the page. 
type: integer nullable

**exit_rate**: The estimated share of the page's views that were the last of their visit, as a percent. 
type: float nullable

**pageviews**: The estimated number of page views. 
type: integer

**visits**: The estimated number of visits in the period. Visits that enter from the target's own website are not counted. 
type: integer

Of the filter grammar below, the report accepts this subset. Conditions on different fields combine with `and` at the top level. `or` and `not` combine the conditions on one field only, in one `and` or one `or` per field (`{"or": [c1, c2]}`, `{"not": c}` and `{"and": [c1, {"not": c2}]}` on the same field, not nested any deeper). On a dimension: `eq`, `neq`, `isubstring`, `prefix` and `suffix` (`search_term`: `eq`, `neq`, `isubstring`, `iphrase_match`, `iprefix` and `isuffix`, all regardless of case); `page_type`, `page_intent` and `page_category` take one `eq`, at most one of the three. On a metric: `gte`, `lte` or `eq`, combined with `and`.

Filter is a JSON string that represents a boolean expression, it should follow the following structure:
```
<bool_filter> ::= { "and" : <bool_filter>+ }
 | { "or" : <bool_filter>+ }
 | { "not" : <bool_filter> }
 | <expr>

<expr> ::= {
 "field" : <dimension|metric>,
 ? "is": <condition>,
 }

<condition> ::= [ "eq", <value> ]
 | [ "neq", <value> ]
 | [ "gt", <value> ]
 | [ "gte", <value> ]
 | [ "lt", <value> ]
 | [ "lte", <value> ]
 | [ "substring", <value> ]
 | [ "isubstring", <value> ]
 | [ "phrase_match", <value> ]
 | [ "iphrase_match", <value> ]
 | [ "prefix", <value> ]
 | [ "suffix", <value> ]
```"

evidence.observation:
quote: "description": "`where` bounds the ranked websites by their metrics before `limit`; without it the ranking is unfiltered, where the report hides related and utility websites by default (`shared_audience` `lte` 60 and `search_share` `gte` 1.5). It does not apply to `sites`.

The fields `where` filters by:

**shared_audience**: The share of the website's visitors who also visited the target, as a percent. Not a field of the rows; its `lte` bound is exclusive. Websites most of whose visitors are the target's are satellites of its audience, which the report hides by default (`lte` 60). 
type: float

**dr**: The Domain Rating of the website, on a 100-point scale. Rounded to an integer, 0 when unknown. 
type: float

**organic_traffic**: The estimated monthly organic traffic from Google to the website or page. 0 when unknown. 
type: float

**search_share**: The share of the website's visits that came from search (organic and shopping, not paid), as a percent. 
type: float

Of the filter grammar below, the report accepts this subset: `gte` and `lte` conditions, one of each per field, combined with `and` at the top level.

Filter is a JSON string that represents a boolean expression, it should follow the following structure:
```
<bool_filter> ::= { "and" : <bool_filter>+ }
 | { "or" : <bool_filter>+ }
 | { "not" : <bool_filter> }
 | <expr>

<expr> ::= {
 "field" : <dimension|metric>,
 ? "is": <condition>,
 }

<condition> ::= [ "eq", <value> ]
 | [ "neq", <value> ]
 | [ "gt", <value> ]
 | [ "gte", <value> ]
 | [ "lt", <value> ]
 | [ "lte", <value> ]
 | [ "substring", <value> ]
 | [ "isubstring", <value> ]
 | [ "phrase_match", <value> ]
 | [ "iphrase_match", <value> ]
 | [ "prefix", <value> ]
 | [ "suffix", <value> ]
```"

evidence.observation:
quote: "description": "The filter expression. The following column identifiers are recognized (this differs from the identifiers recognized by the `select` parameter).

**anchor**: The clickable words in a link that point to a URL. 
type: string

**domain**: The referring domain. 
type: string

**domain_rating**: The Domain Rating of the referring domain. 
type: float

**intersect**: Number of competitors linked from this result. 
type: integer

evidence.observation: quote: "description": "A filter expression for your brand's visibility, mirroring the \"Your brand\" filter. `brand_name` matches whether a response mentions your brand: `\"mentioned\"` or `\"not_mentioned\"`. `page_status` matches how the AI used your pages: `\"cited\"` (the AI retrieved pages from your site and referenced them in the answer), `\"found_but_not_cited\"` (the AI retrieved pages from your site as potential sources but did not reference them in the final answer), or `\"not_found\"` (the AI did not retrieve any pages from your site). \nUses [filter syntax](https://docs.ahrefs.com/api/docs/filter-syntax) with the following restrictions: the only valid operator is `\"eq\"`; each field is one section: give a single value, or combine several values of the same field with `or`; join the `brand_name` and `page_status` sections with a top-level `and`/`or`. Selecting every value of a field is rejected, since it matches everything (omit the field instead).",

evidence.observation:
quote: "description": "A filter on how the responses talk about your brands and competitors, like the Sentiment filter in Brand Radar. Uses [filter syntax](https://docs.ahrefs.com/api/docs/filter-syntax) with three fields:
- `brand` (required): a name from `brands` or `competitors`, with `"eq"`.
- `sentiment` (optional): `positive`, `neutral`, `negative` or `mixed`. With `"eq"`, the brand is mentioned with this sentiment. With `"neq"`, the brand is mentioned with a sentiment, but never this one. With `"empty"`, the brand is never mentioned with a sentiment, which includes responses that don't mention it. With `not` `"empty"`, the brand is mentioned with some sentiment. Without `sentiment`, any response that mentions the brand matches.
- `aspect` (optional): what the sentiment is about, with `"eq"`: `features_specs`, `performance_effectiveness`, `price_value`, `reputation_popularity`, `quality_reliability`, `design_comfort`, `usability_compatibility`, `availability_delivery`, `safety_health`, `service_support` or `general`.
Each rule is about one brand: one condition, or an `and` of conditions. To combine rules, put each one in its own `and` and join them with a top-level `and` or `or`.",

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: * *MCP server* - a programmatic interface for external AI agents, IDEs, and CLIs. Use it when you build or operate your own agent.

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: * *MCP client* - An AI agent or client that supports Model Context Protocol (MCP). This could be [claude.ai](https://docs.apify.com/integrations/claude-ai.md), [Claude Desktop](https://docs.apify.com/integrations/claude-desktop.md), [VS Code](https://docs.apify.com/integrations/vscode.md) with MCP support, or any application that implements the MCP specification. candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: How product extraction works

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: The product format extracts the product deterministically from on-page structured data — no LLM is involved. It merges multiple sources by priority: JSON-LD > schema.org microdata > RDFa > embedded state (__NEXT_DATA__/Nuxt/Apollo/Redux/Remix) > AliExpress runParams > GA4 dataLayer > OpenGraph/<meta>. The merge is identity-aware, so fields from different products are never combined. Currency is reported only when the page sources it.

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: Product extraction is fail-closed: ambiguous pages yield no product, and weaker sources such as OpenGraph only contribute when a price is present. On a page with no extractable product, the response omits the product object and adds a warning (e.g. “No product found…”).

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: Self-hosting: the product format is backed by a dedicated product-extraction service. On Firecrawl Cloud it works out of the box. If you self-host, set PRODUCT_EXTRACTION_SERVICE_URL to point at that service — when it is unset, requesting the product format returns a warning and no product (the same pattern the audio/video formats use for their service).

evidence.observation: quote: An integration that connects over HTTP can name itself with an X-Firecrawl-Origin header, for example X-Firecrawl-Origin: my-agent. The server reports it to Firecrawl as the request origin mcp-my-agent@<server version>, in place of the client name or User-Agent it would otherwise report. Use letters, digits and dashes: each run of other characters becomes one dash, leading and trailing dashes are dropped, and the name is cut at 48 characters. Tool results are unaffected; only the origin sent to the Firecrawl API (and passed to an embedder's beforeKeylessRequest) changes.

evidence.observation: quote: In this mode the server only answers requests addressed to localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] (on any port), plus the address in HOST when it isn't 0.0.0.0 or ::. A request whose Host header names another host, or whose Origin header names another site, gets 403, and CORS headers echo an allowed origin instead of *. GET and HEAD requests to /health are answered whatever the host, so health checks keep working, and the server logs a line naming FIRECRAWL_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS for every request it refuses. This stops web pages you visit from calling the local server through DNS rebinding or cross-origin requests and using its FIRECRAWL_API_KEY.

evidence.observation: quote: The Clay Public API enforces per-workspace request rate limits. When you exceed a limit, Clay returns HTTP `429` and you should back off before retrying.

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: The default limit is **300 requests per minute per workspace** (about 5 requests per second), shared across all API keys and OAuth credentials in the workspace.

evidence.observation: quote: `clay login` opens a browser to authorize the CLI with OAuth — this works from a human terminal or an agent's shell tool. Use `clay whoami` as the canonical check that authentication is working, and `clay logout` to clear a stored credential.

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: Each sign-in covers one workspace — the one you pick on the consent screen. To work across several, run `clay login` once per workspace: signing into a second keeps the first. `clay workspaces list` shows what you are signed into, `clay workspaces current` shows which one commands run against, and `clay workspaces switch <id>` switches. Signing in makes the workspace just added the active one, so switch back explicitly if you were working in another. `clay logout` signs out of the active workspace and leaves the rest.

evidence_rules:
# Research format and evidence rules

Contract version 1.1, 2026-11-23 (updated in Task 06 from v1.0 based on verified Task 05 pilot findings; sealed v1.0 runs retain their frozen contract snapshots).

### Changelog (v1.0 → v1.1)
- Added `vendor_approval_required` to `credential_eligibility.{testing,production}` to separate platform/vendor API-access review (e.g., Google Ads Explorer/Basic/Standard application) from commercial/agency `partner_approval_required`.
- Clarified edition-matching for `mcp.discovery`: a community MCP targeting a different product edition (e.g., personal web/cookie scraping vs. Enterprise REST API) must not assert `found` for the Enterprise scope without explicit edition alignment.
- Reinforced per-claim attachment: every material detail in a claim (including `purpose` and MCP tool-list observations) must be anchored inside that claim's own attached evidence array and locator line range.

## Files and migration

- `data/apps.json` is the 100-app identity roster, in assignment order. Its provenance identifies the original conversation and user turn. Original app/hint Markdown is retained verbatim, including link targets and parenthetical hints. Categories and normalized names match the audited roster.
- `legacy_candidate_doc_urls` preserves the scaffold's URL leads with their separate provenance. Neither these URLs nor assignment hints establish auth, access, API or MCP findings. Do not inherit the old OAUTH/APIKEY/GATED/MCP lists, generic descriptions, breadth placeholders or buildability labels.
- `schemas/record.json` is a Draft 2020-12 schema for one app in one immutable run. `examples/unresearched-record.json` is a format example, excluded from research and accuracy totals.
- Initialize substantive claims as `not_researched`, with null values and empty evidence. Keep prior artifacts intact as legacy material; a migration must not relabel their guesses as documentary observations. Existing scripts do not yet consume or enforce this contract.
- Paygent Connect (84) is unresolved. Preserve the original `paygent (NMI-powered)` hint. The legacy paygentglobal.com lead has no established identity match. Resolve vendor/product/edition with primary evidence before attaching that domain's facts; do not substitute a similarly named payment company. The example intentionally leaves this unresolved.

## Claim states and evidence

Each scalar claim has a stable `claim_id`, `status`, `value`, `context`, `evidence`, `supporting_claim_refs` and `rationale`. Context names the edition, API version, account type, region and environment where relevant; say which details remain unknown. IDs remain stable across revisions for the same question. Split materially different scopes into distinct method/entry claims rather than merging them.

| Status | Meaning and counting |
| --- | --- |
| `observed` | Explicitly supported by captured source content; non-null value and evidence required. This means documentary observation, not verified truth or a successful API call. |
| `inferred` | Reasoned conclusion; non-null value, evidence, rationale and supporting claim references required. Report separately from documentary observations. |
| `unknown` | Attempted investigation did not resolve the question. Null value; explain the gap. |
| `disputed` | Conflicting content has not been reconciled. Null value; at least two evidence observations and an explanation required. |
| `not_researched` | No investigation yet. Null value; never count as a finding. |
| `not_applicable` | Evidence explains why the question does not apply to the stated scope. Null value; not a negative result or a correct auth/access claim. |
| `not_found_in_checked_sources` | A bounded search found no supported result. Null value and evidence identifying checked content/search scope required. Use for MCP discovery; never translate to 'no MCP exists'. |

`coverage_status` on auth/protocol/resource collections is workflow metadata: `not_researched`, `partial`, or `checked_sources`. `checked_sources` means only the listed sources were examined, never exhaustive coverage of the vendor. Empty arrays do not prove absence. Record unresolved questions in `notes`; a researched collection can still be incomplete.

For each evidence observation record:

- The actual source URL, source kind, exact heading/anchor, page/line range, or repository path plus commit and line range in `locator`.
- A short captured observation or faithful paraphrase supporting this specific claim. A homepage URL, search-result snippet, or a whole-page citation without a locator is a lead, not substantive evidence.
- `captured_on` (ISO date), capture method, and document date/version when known. Null document metadata means unknown, not current. Capture dates must reflect actual reading, not run creation.
- SHA-256 of the captured content and a relative `snapshot_ref` where feasible. Hash normalized/extracted content only if the snapshot is exactly that content and the extraction method is recorded. If no content snapshot/hash is available, use null and a specific `hash_unavailable_reason`; do not fabricate a digest. A hash proves content identity, not correctness. Never store credentials in snapshots.

For actual operational tests, use `source_kind: execution_receipt` and `capture_method: execution_log`. These require a real local receipt/log in `snapshot_ref` and its SHA-256; `source_url` may be null for a local log. Its locator identifies the run/tool call and relevant log lines; observation states the actual result. This is the only source kind that allows a null source URL. This format permits future receipts; it implements no execution functionality and the Task 02 example has no operational findings.

Prefer vendor developer/auth/pricing/access docs and official repositories. Community repositories support their own implementation claims, not vendor endorsement. Assignment text supports identity/category/hints only. Cite approval and pricing sources for eligibility claims; an API reference alone need not establish a free credential path. If official sources conflict, preserve both observations and their time, version and scope; do not silently pick one. `conflicts` links the affected claim IDs and explains the discrepancy; `disputed` claims may also hold both observations directly.

Evidence is attached per claim. Each auth method, API protocol, resource group and MCP entry has its own claim and evidence. A shared page may be cited repeatedly with the appropriate locator. One citation must not silently support other array members or scopes. When one claim necessarily includes several details (e.g. an auth method plus documented scopes), its evidence must support every detail; otherwise split the claim or omit unestablished optional details. For review, any unsupported material detail makes that whole claim unsupported; do not inflate the denominator by splitting punctuation into claims.

## Field rules

**Identity and purpose.** `identity.id`, `app` and `category` come from the roster; resolve product identity in `identity.resolution` using a cited product/edition description. Category is assignment metadata, not a researched auth claim. `purpose` is a short, single-line, cited description. Do not put placeholder prose in an observed value.

**Auth.** `auth.items` contains a separate claim per method and scope. Preserve OAuth2, API key, Basic and tokens separately; don't choose a single winner. `context` and `details` explain API/edition/actor, OAuth grant or signing scheme; `scopes` lists only documented scopes relevant to the described use. An empty scopes list means no scopes captured, not unrestricted permissions. For CLI/local software, only assert `none` or `not_applicable` when supported for that interface; lack of a REST API does not settle CLI buildability.

**Credentials.** `credential_eligibility.testing` and `.production` each contain independent boolean claims:

- `free_access`, `trial_access`, `sandbox_access`: true means a documented credential/use path is available for this environment; false requires evidence of its absence or inapplicability. Unknown stays null.
- `paid_required`, `admin_approval_required`, `vendor_approval_required`, `partner_approval_required`, `contact_sales_required`: true means this condition is required for the stated path/scope. False needs explicit support for proceeding without it; silence is unknown. Distinguish `vendor_approval_required` (vendor/platform API-access review or application, such as Google Ads Explorer/Basic/Standard) from `partner_approval_required` (commercial, agency, or technology partnership program gating) and `admin_approval_required` (customer tenant/organization admin role or approval).
- `self_serve`: a documented path allows the intended developer to obtain the relevant credentials without vendor/partner intervention. A paid path may be self-serve; an existing tenant's admin can still be required. State actor/plan/prerequisites in each claim's context. Never derive this by default or from 'Sign up'.

These conditions can coexist. A free sandbox can require admin approval; production may require a paid account and partner approval. For alternative credential paths, the context of each claim must identify exactly which path it describes. Do not collapse conflicting paths to one app-wide boolean: use unknown/disputed with explanatory evidence until a scoped answer is possible. A paid product does not automatically mean API access is gated, and a free trial does not establish production access.

**API surface.** Protocols, public documentation, resource groups and breadth are independent claims. A known REST protocol must survive even when breadth and resource groups are unknown. Record each documented protocol and resource group separately with supporting sections; a source can establish 'contacts' while leaving 'billing' unresearched. `public_documentation` refers to documentation visibility for this API scope, not credential eligibility or public data access. Public documentation does not mean anonymous API access.

`breadth` is an inference supported by resource-group claim IDs: `narrow` = one focused workflow/group; `moderate` = multiple related groups; `broad` = multiple distinct business domains. Explain the classification and captured examples in context/rationale. This is qualitative scope, not a fabricated endpoint inventory or a guarantee of completeness. Leave unknown if not enough resource documentation was read. REST/GraphQL/SDK/CLI can coexist; include other interfaces when relevant to agent-callable tools.

**MCP.** `mcp.discovery` is `observed` with value `found` only when at least one supported entry matching the record's declared product edition/scope is recorded. A community MCP targeting a separate consumer/personal edition (e.g., undocumented web-cookie scraping) does not establish `found` for an Enterprise API scope unless tested and documented for that edition; preserve such community entries only with explicit edition separation or leave Enterprise MCP discovery `not_found_in_checked_sources`/`unknown`. Otherwise use the appropriate null state. Each `mcp.entries` item is its own claim with `official`/`community`, source URL, scope, and repository/server URL where established (null otherwise). A server URL may be a hosted endpoint, while a local stdio server may have only a repository URL. No guessed URL. Vendor endorsement must be supported to call it official. Entries for outgoing MCP clients do not establish an app's callable server; record tool direction/scope. `operational_check` remains `not_researched` unless actual execution logs support the result. Docs, a server listing, or a GitHub README cannot establish successful connection, tool calls, or production readiness. This task runs no operational checks.

**Buildability.** This is an explicit inference for a stated agent workflow: `build_now`, `conditional`, `outreach_required` or `not_buildable_for_stated_scope`. Cite supported identity/auth/access/API/MCP or CLI claims through `supporting_claim_refs`, include relevant source evidence, explain the conclusion, list blockers and next steps. A public API can still require outreach; no MCP alone is not a blocker to building an API wrapper. Unknown identity/access/API details can leave buildability unknown. `build_now` is feasibility from evidence, not an implemented or tested integration. Blocker statements also require support; do not label an app unbuildable because a fetch failed.

## Fetch telemetry is separate

`fetches` records URL, attempt date, status, HTTP status, resolved URL, error and optional content digest. It never supplies claim truth. DNS/HTTP errors, login walls, robots blocks and timeouts do not establish no API, paid access, partner gating or nonexistent MCP. A 200 response does not establish a cited claim. Fetch outcomes can prompt follow-up but cannot promote research states automatically.

## Review, runs and accuracy

1. Every saved run gets a unique `run_id`, creation date and producer identity/type. Persist the run input roster hash, schema/rules versions, tool/model versions and configuration alongside that run in a run manifest. Never reuse a run ID or overwrite original records, evidence snapshots, logs or adjudications. The example's run ID is illustrative only.
2. Corrections create a new run with `parent_run_id` and `correction_refs` naming original run/claim IDs plus reasons. Keep the original value/evidence unchanged in the parent; revised claims reuse the same question ID where scope is unchanged. Record added/removed/split claims explicitly in the correction log. New evidence does not retroactively become first-pass evidence.
3. `review` is pending until actual claim adjudications exist. Completed means the listed adjudications are completed, not that every field/app was reviewed. Capture reviewer ID, `ai` or `human`, date, original run ID, each claim ID, judgment, rationale and review evidence. A tool/browser action or another AI is still AI review; only an actual identified person can sign human review. Producer and reviewer identities must be distinct for independent review; disclose shared model/context. Do not copy pending entries over completed reviews.

   An `unresolved` judgment may have an empty evidence array when no source content could be captured. Its required reason must name the actual fetch attempt (for example `fetches[0]` and its date/URL) or an existing failure-log path and describe why adjudication could not finish. Runtime review must resolve that reference. Do not fabricate a source observation for a DNS/access failure. `correct`, `incorrect`, `unsupported` and `not_applicable` judgments still require captured evidence; a failure-only review cannot establish any of them. A completed review containing unresolved judgments does not mean those claims have been verified and contributes no accuracy denominator for those judgments.
4. Before full-run verification, freeze a sampling manifest: manifest ID/path, target run, roster SHA-256, selection date, method/algorithm/version, seed, selected IDs, category counts, reviewer assignments and claim rubric. Use a deterministic seeded selection of two apps per category (20 total), without replacement; report all ten categories including Support and Helpdesk. Preserve pilot/targeted reviews separately from this sample. A seed alone does not reproduce an unspecified algorithm. Do not select actual sample IDs in Task 02.
5. Freeze the claim inventory and scoring rubric before review. Unit = each non-null `observed` or `inferred` claim object, identified by `(run_id, app_id, claim_id)`. Count auth methods, protocols, groups and MCP entries separately; nested operational checks are separate claims only if asserted. Score a compound claim correct only if all material details hold for its scope. Report documentary and inference results separately. Category/roster metadata, example fixtures, collection metadata, null states and bare URLs are not scored findings.
6. Each adjudication is `correct`, `incorrect`, `unsupported`, `unresolved`, or `not_applicable`. Unsupported is a failure to substantiate, not proof of factual falsity. Let C/I/U be completed correct/incorrect/unsupported judgments for asserted claims. Evidence-backed accuracy = C / (C + I + U); print those counts, with unresolved/pending/excluded totals alongside. If the denominator is zero, accuracy is null ('unmeasured'), not 0% or 100%. Exclude null-state claims and not-applicable judgments from this accuracy denominator; report any invalid applicability claims as audit issues. Do not drop incorrect or unsupported results after correction.
7. Report review coverage = completed C/I/U judgments / eligible asserted claims in the frozen sample, with unresolved and pending counts. Separately report research coverage across all 100: counts of observed, inferred and each null state for the six required research areas (purpose, auth, credentials, API, MCP, buildability), plus identity resolution. A collection is not covered just because it exists; distinguish partial protocol knowledge from missing breadth. Report area completion criteria and every denominator. Unknowns do not count as correct findings. No one overall 'accuracy' number should conceal missing research or missing review.
8. First-pass and corrected scores refer to immutable runs, the same sample and the frozen claim questions. Link changed/removed/split/new questions; publish paired results on comparable questions and the changed inventory separately. Do not claim improvement by deleting hard claims, changing denominators or relabeling a failure unknown. A corrected/previously reviewed sample is not an unbiased held-out estimate; disclose reuse. Report no accuracy or improvement until actual adjudication exists. Prepare a human checklist if no person has reviewed yet; do not claim human checks were performed.

## Publication contract (later tasks only)

A hosting config, Site registration, expected URL, local Git directory or ZIP is not proof of publication. Save a repository creation/write receipt, actual repository URL, commit SHA, source/README existence and readback evidence. Save the deployment ID/status, actual live URL, deployed commit or artifact SHA-256, date, and an independent fetch/browser result demonstrating the page is accessible to the intended reviewer. Record real errors/blockers when unsuccessful. No publication is attempted in Task 02.
